The MRT connection makes it easy to connect, but if you're out for shopping or night-life, it's a long way from town! Excellent for business travellers or those who need to catch an early morning flight!

reviews.author: Ceasar Corkery
reviews.content: Stayed here twice waiting for a connecting flight. Very convenient. Rooms surprisingly quiet considering it's an airport! Nice room, pleasant staff and great breakfast. The pool is lovely, you can lay in the sun and watch the planes take off. We just had to jump on the 'Sky Train' to connect with our flight.

reviews.author: Felicity Harris
reviews.content: Singapore does not have too many options for hotels that are close to the airport. This trumps them all. Conveniently located in T3, it offers walk-in access to passengers. Plus, you have all the usual facilities at Changi airport, that you can use. Also, with the MRT station in the basement, you can move into the city, pretty quickly, without your luggage. Opt for this as waiting in line for taxi at T3, can be pretty taxing, especially during peak hours. Eat at joints, in the airport terminal - you have a range of options. Do check out the bar at the hotel - but, be warned, they close pretty early.

reviews.author: Dena O'Keefe
reviews.content: The hotel is considered very new, and this is reflected in the furnishings and general condition of the room. First glitch was in the booking - I had requested twin beds but turned up to be told it was a room with one King bed. This was rectified, but the service was not with a smile at all. The porters were timely, and the rooms are extremely spacious, as expected with 'out-of-the-way' hotels. Its proximity to Terminal 3 of Changi Airport makes it very handy for transitting passengers though. The porters will provide an airport trolley for luggage upon checkout. Our room faced the communal pool, which was not audible from the 7th floor. However, voices of other hotel guests are easily heard from the common corridor. The lighting in the room was rather minimal too, given its size. All in all, a hotel that serves its purpose in providing a comfortable environment close to the International Airport terminals, but is still considered relatively pricey given its location.

title: Newport (Pembrokeshire)

description: self catering - 20 beds in 4 person rooms.
name: Uist Outdoor Centre

reviews.author: Berneice Herzog
reviews.content: Well I was there these past 10 days since I was working at the LA Auto Show at the convention center. Last year I stayed at the Westin (see review). So, I have to admit that this location is definitly MUCH better. Much more within a 3 block radius, including a supermarket, Ralphs. The hotel is brand new. The rooms are spacious, the bathrooms are huge. The pool on the 4th floor is gorgeous, and I LOVED the Illy caffe in the lobby...my favorite coffee place...sure beats starbucks anyday. That being said theres a starbucks within steps from the hotel..as is so many restaurants, and the staples center! Now as far as service...I guess it was fine. Nothing in particular happened for them to demonstrate extraordinary service, but they were always friendly from the moment I arrived to the moment I left. Now I just had 2 complaints. ONE, no free wifi/internet in the room. Its $12.95 a day!!! I thought this is ridiculous since this isnt a run of the mill hotel. BUT!!!! i found out the way around it! ish! There IS free wifi in the lobby. So you can connect to the wifi in the lobby then go to your room and you have a free hour! et voila! The other thing is that they dont provide microwaves. Now if you are only staying a few days, who cares, but since I was there for almost 2 weeks, to save money I bought alot of groceries and it would of been nice to have (as i had in the westin). So considering that was my only 2 complaints, which neither are too significant, I definitely give this hotel 5 stars!!! And did I mention the pool area is GORGEOUS!

reviews.author: Lavada Stiedemann
reviews.content: My husband and I stayed for 2 nights this past week. First the positive: Front desk and concierge service is top notch. Rooms are spacious and clean. The location Is great if you are attending an event. Areas that need serious improvement: The service in both the lobby lounge and the mixing longe is absolutely terrible. On a Monday evening we went to the mixing lounge and sat at a table (the bar was full but the seating area only had 8 people seated) and waited for approximately 10 minutes to order. There were 2 waitresses working but seemed to be more interested in talking to each other than serving customers. I finally went to the bar and ordered. In the hour I was seated at a table not 1 of the staff asked if I would like anything else or even approached me. this is unacceptable particularly when you are paying top $$ for cocktails. The lobby bar is not much better. I was also really disappointed in the housekeeping service. I left my room at approx. 1 PM and saw that housekeeping was servicing the adjacent room. I returned to my room at 5PM and the room had not been cleaned. I spoke with the front desk and they acted like it was no big deal and they would have someone service it. I'm sorry but at $300+ a night it was a big deal to me. The gym is great but he again the staff really need to work on their customer service skills. Too long of a story to bother with... For $300+ a night there should be free internet service for all guests in their room. Also, be aware that overnight parking charges are ridiculous at $40 per night.

reviews.author: Jefferey Waelchi
reviews.content: Very nice rooms, restaurants and appealing design. Mike at the concierge desk was great - helped be get all around LA. One negative - they need to wash their exterior windows... couldn't tell if it was overcast or sunny, they were SO dirty.

reviews.author: Kariane Kassulke
reviews.content: I was in LA for a quick trip to visit some friends and stayed here for two nights. Located right next to LA Live, and while there isn't too much to do here unless there are events going on (ex: sports, concerts etc) it was a pleasant and enjoyable stay. I came in late morning and they were still able to accommodate an early check-in and room upgrade (junior suite) with a view overlooking their pool. The room itself was very nice and I appreciated the early check in as well as the upgrade. The Lounge is great to grab a few snacks on the go, and the pool is a great place to relax at. I was visiting friends in the area and was not familiar with the area so Concierge was very helpful in helping me get to where I needed to go. Staff was very friendly and helpful. Overall, a great experience

title: North Uist

description: Bed and Breakfast from 25 - 30 pounds per person per night.
directions: Around 15 minutes walk from the ferry.
name: The Old Courthouse

reviews.author: Willie Von
reviews.content: Stay two night in this hip hotel in the heart of LA. Locations is great(daytime) with everything you need in walking distance. Comfortable bed, nice flat screen TV, clean, spacious, decent room service quality(a bit pricey) and good choice of restaurants inside this hotel and in the adjacent Ritz Carlton(hotels are connected). Customer service was top notch.

reviews.author: Destiny Ritchie
reviews.content: When I walked into the spacious lobby I was instantly impressed. The hotel is beautiful with a lot of wide open space. After check in the room was large with a view of LA. I went to the pool bar, which also had a view, had a few drinks, then walked to LA Live. There is a good selection of restaurants within walking distance. There also just happened to be the FLoyd Mayweather-Victor Ortiz pre-fight conference right in the plaza. Great location. Great hotel. It will serve all your downtown LA needs and then some. The staff was courteous and attentive, the food was decent.

reviews.author: Nina Collins
reviews.content: Arrived just before 3 pm with a confirmed reservation since October 2010 for double beds. The hotel could only give us a room with a king size bed and then a promise with a room change for the next day. The first room was the smallest, dirtiest room I believe in the hotel. The bathroom was lacking enough towels, only had a shower and the shower floor was dirty. Having stayed at the hotel last year we were amazed how worn it seemed- from the service, the rooms, to the presentation of flowers in the lobby. The second room wasn't much better- dirty rug, bathroom walls, bent lamp and an unusual shower curtain- two uneven halves and colors not matching anything in Marriott that we have seem before. It appeared that excellence is not what this hotel is all about.

reviews.author: Myrtle Dickens
reviews.content: My advice is to avoid this upholstered cesspool like the plague. Even though I was travelling on business, had a confirmed (and paid for) room, I was unable to check in without a credit card. After much dancing I got it arranged but corporate has no flexibility and no mercy - all for the sake of 'possible incidental charges' (there were none, I used none of the additional services, thanks Marriott!). The room, on entry seemed clean enough but on close inspection I found long black hairs in the bathroom sink (I have photos) and curly brown (pubic??) hairs on the shower soap dish. YUCK. Housekeeping eventually (1 hour+) showed up to reclean the bathroom, no apology from the non-english-speaking staff. While I waited I tried to get a snack and a drink. Drinks you can get - that's the ONLY vending there is in the entire building. $1.25 bottle of Coke in hand I checked the room service menu - $14.95 was the cheapest item, club sandwich. Nearly $15 for a SANDWICH? Unless it's delivered by a naked dancing girl that's too much. No, dancing girls not available. Attempted to have pizza delivered - only Pizza Hut apparently pays the kickback and is allowed to deliver there. $15 got a large pepperoni delivered (and was quite good). Tried to call home - cordless phone handset dead, despite 'charge' light. Corded phone would not reach desk area - also had a ring loud enough to startle me and no obvious control to turn down. Cheap and flimsy set to boot. Cinema-size television had extremely weak and very directional remote (cheap) that took several seconds per channel change (television signal obviously delivered via house computer network) and dropped out / broke up / went dark a LOT. Nice robe in closet for use in spa - size far too small for average guy like me, unless I wanted to flash the other guests, so no spa for you. I decided to try and get some work done - wireless NOT free (don't buy the dodge about 'free wireless in the lobby' - you get one hour and your machine is locked out by MAC address, contrary to staff's hopeful fibs, besides I paid for a ROOM to work in). Not willing to cough up $15 a night (!) for likely awful service I resorted to local Starbucks for my email and web support. After the event I worked, our team gathered for a drink in the bar - their 'best' single-malt scotch? Glenlivet. Waiter had no idea what any of the other truly good malts were - and took 15 mins to deliver one drink with the lounge virtually empty. Motivation obviously pretty low despite the tony ambiance. The lobby was filled with ear-hurtingly-loud boom-boom disco music even in the morning... not sure what that says about the place. My guess is the manager was on vacation. Combine that with the must-have-room-card-to-access-elevator (for every single guest - some trips took nearly five minutes to go through the foolishness of card-in/punch floor) and the 1960s style (ie hideous) furniture with lots of sharp corners (ow) and I felt very unwelcome. The Holiday Inn in Fremont made me feel so much more welcome - and was far less than half the price.

reviews.author: Deonte Gutkowski
reviews.content: As the heading states, this is absolutely a fabulous facility, but make sure you check your bill constantly throughout your stay if you booked a package deal. For some odd reason, this hotel isn't able to track the different packages offered and, in some cases, the staff isn't familiar with the deal, which just adds to the confusion. This happened in my case, but fortunately I had a printed copy of the rate rules for the deal that I had booked through the Marriott website, so they were able to make the necessary adjustments without any problem. But, of course, it was annoying to see the charges (rate included breakfast for two) and then have to provide proof of the rate details to get them adjusted. Of all the Marriott's I've stayed in as a Platinum MR member, I've never encountered this before to the extent that the hotel offers so many different packages that the hotel staff is oblivious to the details of many of the offers and asks for proof from the guest. I'm sure they get lots of push back considering the level of clientele staying in this hotel, but in my case since I had printed the reservation details and had a copy, it eliminated an argument. So, just keep an eye on your bill and make sure you print a copy of the details....just in case!

reviews.author: Edythe Hand
reviews.content: JW Marriot at LA Live is fantastic. Highly recommend it. Stayed there during the Gartner conference. The room was very spacious and nicely decorated. the big flat screen hd tv was an unexpected surprise. the bed was very comfortable. the room was quiet and I slept great. the LA Market restaurant in the hotel was really good. there's also a number of good restaurants near by. ate at ESPN Sportszone and Rock Fish, both of which were very good. the hot tub and pool were very nice. loved watching the projected tv images on the building from the hot tub at night. visible security in the hotel as well outside in the LA Live area so felt very safe.

reviews.author: Neal Treutel
reviews.content: Stayed over Labor Day weekend for concert at Staples. One block to Staples and convention center; 3 blocks to downtown. New, spacious rooms with frig and safe. Beds were nice and comfy and room was very quiet (maybe cuz hotel not that busy?). Lobby is airy and has free wi-fi! Unfortunately, no free wi-fi in rooms. 4th floor pool was nice and overlooked LA Live. Draft beer at bar was $8 but soda from vending machines were only $1.25! Valet parking is expensive but no free parking in area.

reviews.author: Thalia Yundt
reviews.content: This hotel gives Marriott a bad name. Try calling their front desk before you arrive... "Hello, Ritz Carlton" "Sorry, I dialed the wrong number" (dial again) "Hello, Ritz Carlton" (Hang up and try again) "Sorry, I'm trying to reach the Marriott and I think I have the wrong number" "No, we share the same line" Really?! Is the Marriott manager that ^*(#ing stupid? You can't afford your own phone line or operators?! It doesn't end there. During a 5 day stay ordered room service 7 times. 6 times the order was completely screwed up. 5 times the food was very late. No joke. Even after speaking with the manager, after the 2nd room service disaster, the problem was never fixed. And the food quality was poor, at even half the price we paid. The manager eventually offered us complimentary breakfast at the restaurant downstairs, but failed to mention (even after we told her we were in a hurry in the morning and the usless, late room service forced us to skip breakfast and be late for work) she failed to tell us that there's a 30-45 minute wait for a table at breakfast. If a hotel can not get even these elementary services right, it says a lot about the management. And none of what it says is good. These kind of shortcomings are unacceptable for a Marriott, especially a Marriott in the price range of this one. I'd give them negative-one star if it weren't for the nice decor, view, and amenities.

title: North Uist

description: An established hotel next the ferry terminal.
directions: 2 minutes walk from the ferry terminal.
name: Lochmaddy Hotel

reviews.author: Roscoe Conn
reviews.content: Currently staying on the 21st floor of this brand new hotel. I have to admit I was not looking forward to staying here. We had to stay downtown because of a convention and I know that downtown LA is pretty bleak. However, this hotel is really a bright oasis despite its not fantastic location in terms of things to walk to easily. The furnishings are are bright and elegant. I am sitting in an aqua butterfly chair next to a golden rod, retro-mod loveseat. We have a nice view of the mountains but I think the rooms on the freeway side of the building actually offer the best view.Rooms are almost silent from noise and the hotel feels very booked. The JW toiletries are great and the bathroom is large although no tub in our room. Coffeemaker and small fridge without minibar clutter make this a great room. The thing that really impressed me so far is the staff. The check in team was wonderful. Bright smiles. Very eager to make our stay terrific. Here is how I know this is a great hotel. The real sign of a fantastic hotel is shown when things go wrong. Yesterday the valet smashed the rear end of our rental car. We got a call from Rick the manager and he told us what happened and he did absolutely everything to make sure this did not disrupt our trip in any way. He swaped out the car with our rental company and gave us the use of the garage's car service. We were the first accident the garage has had since it opened so they were very apologetic and quick to make things right. Truthfully, it did mess up our day somewhat but everyone's attitude was so accomodating that we were able to get past it. My only criticism is the fee for Internet at $12.95 a day per computer. I wish these chains would wake up to the fact that free internet is essential for all travelers. I don't want to be charged for something that is not a luxury! Overall, very pleased with the experience here and if you must stay downtown this is the absolute best option.

reviews.author: Jayde Pacocha
reviews.content: I stayed here for nearly 3 months when my employer transferred me to their corp HQ, it was a second home to me.The room was clean, comfy & within easy walking distance to downtown, Space Needle, Pike Place, waterfront. As a woman alone, I never once felt unsafe. Staff & management are EXCELLENT. They're warm, friendly, greet you by name, and are very helpful & responsive to every request. I would recommend it HIGHLY to anyone who is looking for a quality, reasonably priced stay in Seattle. Thank You "Bell"town Inn.

title: North Uist

description: Formerly the Tigh Dearg Hotel, a new hotel (opened in 2005) located about 15 minutes walk from the ferry.
name: Hamersay House

reviews.author: Emerson Rath
reviews.content: We first stayed at the bell town inn in may of 2011 and we thought what a wonderful inn, from the free use of bikes and umbrellas, to the helpful and very freindly staff our room was very clean and a nice size the location is one of the best in town close to everything Seattle has to offer. So here it is oct of 2011 as we are in the process of moving to Seattle and again we stayed at the bell town inn, and again what a wonderful experience, we are going back and forth for interviews and this place always makes us feel so welcome. the best part is we take light rail from the airport to westlake and then a very short six blocks and you have arrived at the inn. I recomend this wonderful inn

reviews.author: Frederick Sipes
reviews.content: We stayed two nights, August 30 and 31 on a trip west and one night - September 9 - on the way back home. Found the hotel to be charming and quirky, in keeping with the neighborhood. We thoroughly enjoyed our days and nights during the stay, were able to walk to Pike Place Market, great restaurants, and local shopping. The staff was knowledgeable about restaurants and totally accommodating to our requests; kudos to Courtney, Cesar, Rachel and others whose names I can't remember. The neighborhood around the hotel was filled with interesting characters, but no one ever harassed us or made us feel uncomfortable. Room was very comfortable, even though not air-conditioned. Could hear some "discussion" through the courtyard on our last night there, but it subsided pretty quickly. Definitely a place we would look to stay again; Seattle people are the best hosts!

reviews.author: Sonia Schmitt
reviews.content: Have previously stayed at this hotel and think it is great for price and location but this stay was during hot weather in Seattle (85') and it was impossible to cool the room down. This made it hard to sleep. It was cooler in the lobby and outside.

reviews.author: Emmet Crist
reviews.content: I stayed here with my boyfriend over the Fourth of July weekend. Neither one of us had ever been and just booked this hotel as a package deal. It was a perfect location to everything. We walked everywhere. It felt like no matter where we went it was no more than a ten minute walk. The hotel staff was so accommodating and helped us with anything we needed. They recommended great places to eat and see. They have free bikes you can rent to tour the city that includes a bike lock and a helmet. It is a hotel for a more younger crowd. I wouldn't necessarily want to take my family there. There was just a younger crowd. I highly recommend this place to anyone that was an affordable and comfortable hotel in Seattle.

title: North Uist

description: Hotel and event venue offering 150 bedrooms and 36 meeting/event rooms, all connected to Wi-Fi.
name: Eastwood Hall

reviews.author: Juwan Ernser
reviews.content: Nice hotel with spacious rooms and options for various group sizes. Rooms haev all facilities for short and long stay and staff is very helpful.

reviews.author: Doris Kilback
reviews.content: We are a family of four, with two children aged 8 and 11. We stayed at the Point Resort for 2 weeks in April 2011. The rooms were huge, much bigger than I was expecting - plenty of room for all our gear. We got a two bedroom apartment which would easily have functioned as two separate apartments. The kids room had a big bed, tv, their own separate kitchen and bedroom. We got a separte tv room/kitchen area which had everything you would need, washer, dryer, dishwasher, cooker, cooking pans. We didnt cook but if you are so inclined on holiday then everything is there for you. The second bedroom also had a tv, with a huge ensuite with a jacuzzi bath, shower, separate toilet room, airing press. The beds are v. very comfortable which is important when you come back from parks tired. We had a nice view over the pool area - at night you could see the fireworks at Disney in the distance. Outside there is a nice pool with a lovely hottub which is great after a long day walking in the parks. A new bar pool has just opened which is a nice addition. There is an indoor gym next to the pool area. The hotel is in a good location for parks - wet n wild is 5 mins walk away. Universal Studios is just a mile down the road. We didn't drive, but a free shuttle bus brings you to all the parks. There is a nice TGI Fridays and a Chilis about 5/6 mins walk away. There is a small area in the lobby where you can get breakfast in morning (they serve starbucks coffee) and they serve tapas/snacks in evening. We didn' t eat there as we self-catered for breakfast, but the food looked nice. I would definitely recommend this hotel to someone travelling with children who wants a bit more space than a hotel and some of the comforts of home. It is in a quiet area, away from the madness of I-Drive. I found the staff at the hotel to be very friendly and helpful, we were always greeted with a smile. I would definitely stay here again.

reviews.author: Joseph Sipes
reviews.content: excellent attentive staff. the new pool bar was a great addition. The attention given by angie at the pool bar was great. and jose had good stories.

reviews.author: Abe Bernier
reviews.content: Husband and I stayed at THE POINT ORLANDO RESORT for one of our many stops for our honeymoon... Neither of us has kids, so while we understood that we were in the heart of Orlando's theme park district, we didn't want to be bothered with them the entire time. So choosing the Point and staying there was definitely a good idea.... everything wasn't perfect but we definitely would return.... The way that the rooms are set up is really nice... makes you feel that you are in an apartment.. Very spacious rooms for the price. The lobby is also very pretty.... The parking lot was never too busy, maybe because we were there during the week, but it was spring break... I did NOT like the stain that was on the floor in front of our room and every now and then it smelled like bad water in the hallways.. At one point I asked hubby did he let one go and he said NO... lol But overall, it was a nice experience and really really close to everything near Universal Studios, Wet n' Wild, carnivals, Downtown Disney, etc.

reviews.author: Adolf Krajcik I
reviews.content: We loved our stay here but, felt the pool was a bit small and quiet for 2 young kids. The pull out was uncomfortable for adults but, fine for kids. The room was super clean and we really loved having a kitchen and washer/dryer. The location was great as it was quiet but, close to International Drive. I liked it here and would stay again although I felt is was not a true 'resort'. However, the staff was great! OUr friends had a great room overlooking the pool (we did not) and their room was bigger (we had a 2 bedroom lock off)- it did make a big difference having the bigger room.

reviews.author: Kylie Abbott
reviews.content: Stayed for two nights at the Point Hotel (my second stay there). Everything was wonderful. The 1 bedroom suite is huge- with a full kitchen, washer/dryer, bathtub with jets and a pullout couch. We were close enough to walk to Universal Studios and City Walk and took a short cab back. The location couldn't be better- and the staff was extremely accommodating. The only place I want to stay when I go to Orlando.

reviews.author: Ewell Moore
reviews.content: My husband & I made the decision to stay here based on reviews we read on Trip Advisor but have to say that our experience at this hotel was one of the worst we have had. We have never had a problem with any of the hotels we have stayed at in Orlando before. This one disappointed us on every single level - only thing in its favour is the location as it is very convenient for Universal Studios and the International Drive area. However, there are much better hotels to choose from in this area and for much better, lower rates as well!! We figured we would pay more as we wanted to treat ourselves before we went on our cruise but it was such a bad mistake. The hotel was not very clean - in fact the carpets were positively filthy!! Also the bed was the most uncomfortable bed we have ever slept on and the result was that neither one of us got much sleep due to the sagging mattress and poor quality of the bed. They really need to invest in some decent beds in this establishment!!! After all, when you book to stay at a hotel it is in the hope of being able to get some rest before continuing with your onward travel - we were both exhausted after our stay at this hotel and found the staff to be very unhelpful and disinterested when we told them of the problems. There are much much better hotels to choose from in Orlando than this one and the biggest mystery to me is how this hotel is so high in the ratings on Trip Advisor as our experience there bears no relation whatsoever to how some of the reviewers have described it. It is as though they are describing a completely different hotel to the place we stayed at!!! I have to agree with the people who have left poor reviews and the best advice I can give to anyone looking for a place to stay whilst in Orlando is to do yourself a favour and give this one a miss.

reviews.author: Ervin Strosin
reviews.content: I would have never stayed here had I not read prior reviews and noticed that it was recognized as a Univeral Studios partner hotel. We were within 5 min of Universal and within only minutes of anything to eat. Wet and Wild Park is across the street. The hotel was clean, staff helpful, and was very nice!

title: Nottingham

description: Private hostel, relaxed, fun, clean and cosy. Landrover day tours of 'hidden Argyll' available leaving daily.
name: Oban Backpackers

reviews.author: Lonny Flatley
reviews.content: Spent a weekend at the Henderson Wharf Inn located in the Fells Point section of Baltimore. I had a great time. Its directly on the water and has a boardwalk that stretches almost all the way down to the Inner Harbor. The hotel is in a great spot within easy walking distance of the restaurants and bars of Fells Point. Room felt very "homey" and comfortable. Friendly staff. 2 drawbacks, no bell staff to help with baggage and bad pillows. Otherwise it was great. Definitely get tickets for the Aquarium at the hotel and save yourself a lot of time and money.

reviews.author: Miss Clint Barton
reviews.content: Will come again in spite of a couple of small things... We requested a room close to the lobby as walking is a problem, but that request was ignored and we had to wait over a half hour for another room. The TV did not work well and the remote was broken. Someone came and played w the TV, got it to work on one channel but it was annoying to have to get up to shut it after dozing off. Never got our complimentary wine either. All in all though, a nice place and as I said, we would give them another try.

reviews.author: Marcel Kemmer
reviews.content: Came down from PA for a relaxing night and found it at Henderson's Wharf. It was a great place to stay and wander the Fells Point area. Our room was beautiful, extremely spacious and had a great view. The lobby was great and breakfast the next morning was wonderful. Sat in the courtyard and enjoyed a cool morning with coffee and croissants. We were given a complimentary bottle of wine upon arrival - which I thought was very nice. Only wish that we could have stayed longer.

reviews.author: Cayla Hermann
reviews.content: My wife and I recently stayed at the Henderson's Wharf Inn and we definitely enjoyed our stay. The room was spacious, the beds were very comfortable, but the room could have had more light. We kept our shades closed because our room was on the ground level (as are all the rooms) and we did not want walker/runners along the pier peering into our room. But, our view from the room of the harbor was lovely. Service: There could be more front desk staff. During our stay, it seemed like the young lady working the front desk was extremely busy and she was the only person at the front desk working until the next morning. Inspite of this, she provided great service. The bottle of wine upon check-in is a nice touch. Food: the continental breakfast was fantastic and was one of my favorite aspects of the hotel. The continental breakfast offered nice variety and the fool was delicious. The woman who tended to the breakfast was friendly and efficient; she provided great service. Value: Truly, the only issue I had with the hotel was the price. It's an expensive hotel for what one receives. My wife and I have been fortunate to travel and stay in some great hotels worldwide and it seems in our travels; we have experienced more for what we paid for at other hotels than what we paid for at the Henderson's Wharf Inn. The Henderson's Wharf Inn is a nice hotel and I will recommend it, but it could add something more.

title: Oban

description: small ensuite dorm rooms and private guest rooms, sea-front location.
name: Corran House

reviews.author: Lemuel Paucek
reviews.content: First time staying at Henderson's, and I was not disappointed. The front desk were very pleasant and accomodating, providing me with useful info for my stay, making sure I knew about the free continental breakfast and complimentary bottle of wine. The room could not have been any nicer, the bed was comfortable, it was immaculate with all I needed for my stay. I would stay there again and highly recommend it to anyone wanting to stay in Baltimore.

reviews.author: Aracely O'Hara
reviews.content: My wife and I stayed at Henderson's Wharf Inn for 2 nights. What an amazing place to stay. The hotel is incredibly charming and the service was amazing. A good continental breakfast every day and a bottle of wine at check in. The location is very good as well as many restaurants and bars/pubs are in walking distance in Fells Point. The only thing I would change is the bath tub, which was more like the type of thing you would see at a Holiday Inn than this type of place. Otherwise, the room and hotel was amazing.

reviews.author: Hailee Will III
reviews.content: I'm somewhat a very picky traveler when it comes to hotels. Based on reviews on Trip Advisor, decided to stay for 2 nights June 25-26, 2010 with Loyola University bound daughter. Based on availability we were going to have to change rooms for the 2nd night, however, the hotel accommodated us prior to our arrival to a harbor view room. This was the most amazing boutique hotel which I've stayed in. The beds were extremely comfortable, the view incredible and the morning breakfast excellent. Will definitely stay here again over the next four years. Thank you.

reviews.author: Aron Schmitt
reviews.content: This was our 3rd stay at Henderson Wharf Inn. This time we had a corner room facing the wharf. We will keep coming back. Comfortable, classy rooms, a free bottle of wine, and the best complimentary breakfast you will find. You can't beat the location if you want to visit the pubs and resturants in Fell's Point. Parking in free at the marina right across the street.

reviews.author: Eloisa Crist
reviews.content: My husband and I celebrated my birthday at our favorite place -- Henderson's Wharf Inn! We love Baltimore and all there is to do there, but more importantly than the town is the place -- and this is it! There is just this feeling of "ahhh" as you walk in, feeling like you've just entered the home of a dear friend. From the welcoming lobby (and front desk staff) to the wine in your room to the beautiful furnishings, you'll know within ten minutes of your arrival that you picked the right place! The rooms are very large and furnished like a bedroom out of a model home. You will not feel in the least like you are staying in a hotel! The mattresses and sheets are top of the line -- you'll get a wonderful night's sleep! The breakfast is just incredible with every sort of fresh fruit, crunchy granola, a large assortment of fresh breads and pastries, cheese and crackers, many fresh fruits -- you name it, it's there! I took pictures but somehow they got deleted from my camera card and I'm very disappointed because I've described this place to my friends, but it's not until they saw the pictures on my camera that they realized how truly unique and wonderful this place is. The front desk staff will attend to your every need and are so gracious and pleasant to deal with. The Inn at Henderson's Wharf combines the best of a Bed and Breakfast (charm, good food, warm ambiance) with the privacy and luxury of an upscale hotel. The water taxi comes within a few minutes of the front door -- it gets you wherever you want to go in Baltimore within minutes at a very low cost. We would never consider staying anywhere else when we're in Baltimore and in fact consider the Inn a destination in itself!

title: Oban

description: A SYHA hostel. 4, 6 and 8 bed dormitories housed in a large Victorian building, on the Esplanade. Great sea views. Within easy walking distance of the town centre.
name: Oban Youth Hostel
title: Oban

description: Corran Esplanade, Oban, PA34 5AE, +44 1631 562051. Rooms from £47 ppn
name: Oban Bay Hotel
title: Oban

description: As it is on the North Pier, rooms on three sides have sea views, some rooms at the back can be noisy from the pubs below.
name: Columba Hotel

reviews.author: Suzanne White
reviews.content: This inn was wonderful, beautiful and spacious rooms and bathroom. Our room had a great view of the harbor, I really cannot say enough good things. The breakfast had a large selection of fresh fruit, bagels and cereal with coffee, tea and hot chocolate available 24 hours a day. Ok the negative was, in Fells Point there are really only pubs and ice cream shops you must walk (20--25 minutes) or water taxi to the inner harbor for restaurants. But then you can return to the Inn and escape.

reviews.author: Zita Ward
reviews.content: We have four children and stayed in two rooms next to one another during the gap between Christmas and New Years Day. Extremely happy with the rooms; very comfortable beds, towels and very much liked the breakfast buffet.

reviews.author: Charity Goyette
reviews.content: I recently extended a business trip a few extra days, decided to avoid the chain hotels, and made reservations at Henderson’s Wharf Inn. It’s the smartest thing I’ve done in a long time! The inn is ideally situated in Fell’s Point, within walking distance to Baltimore’s Inner Harbor. The inn’s entrance, lobby, and rooms are nicely decorated and very comfortable. The inn provides luxurious robes, a complimentary bottle of wine, and a well-stocked snack and beverage bar. The Inn also provides complimentary breakfast, which is enough to get you going in the mornings. You can enjoy your breakfast, weather permitting, in their courtyard garden. It’s worth noting that the inn’s guest rooms are on the first floor with either marina or garden views. The floors above are residences, which add to the appeal. You never quite feel like a tourist, and instead feel quite at home. The cobblestone streets, shops, pubs (lots of them), cafés and restaurants of Fell’s Point might keep you busy and away from the Inner Harbor. However, if you do remember to visit the harbor, you're within walking distance. The walk will take you along the water’s edge, or you can just as easily take the water-taxis that will take you back and forth all day long for one fare. Please try the taxis at nights; the city lights are wonderful at night! I’ll be returning again, and will only consider staying at Henderson’s Wharf Inn!

title: Oban

address: Bella Vista, Tremeirchion Road, Bodfari LL16 4EG
description: 2 dbl (one ''en suite''), 1 ''en suite'' twin.
name: Valeside B&B

reviews.author: Miss Betsy Lowe
reviews.content: My mother and I stayed here for a bridal shower that was in the North end...so nice! Beautiful location, very close to restaurants/North end. Staff could not be more helpful and pleasant. I was sad to leave...would definitely recommend!

reviews.author: Damaris Graham
reviews.content: The convenience of this hotel can't be beat! It is the first stop on the Old Trolley Tour (a great way to see the city if you're a first time visitor), has a metro stop at the front entrance, is conveniently located across the street from a large variety of quick food stops and restaurants, AND offers scenic views of the Wharf. It is located next door to the aquarium. The water taxi stop that goes to and from the airport is located adjacent to the side entrance of the hotel. The water taxi offers a unique and fun method of transportation that is uniquely Boston! Also, the taxi is highly reasonable and efficient. There is a Starbucks on the ground floor serving light breakfast fare and most Starbucks beverages- a great quick breakfast stop for us! The location, friendly staff, and knowledgeable hotel concierge truly make this hotel an excellent location for anyone visiting Boston, but especially those that have never been before. Our room (located down the hall, away from the lobby, and with a water/Wharf view) was clean and comfortable; however, it was not quiet. The noise from the lobby echoes, (including lobby music and typical lobby hustle/bustle sounds), can be heard while in the room. The walls are extremely thin, so much so that we could clearly make out conversations from our neighbors. The Wharf, although scenic, is also quite noisy. Every morning, throughout the day, and sometimes late at night, the loud horns from the boats coming and going are easily heard. If you're up and out early, and out late, sightseeing and enjoying all Boston has to offer, this noise might not be a problem. After all, we didn't come to Boston to sleep and lounge in the room. The pro's definitely outweigh the con's here; Overall, a great place to stay in Boston!

reviews.author: Ms. Earnestine Nader
reviews.content: We were a family of six ages 5 thru 70 staying one night and we all had a wonderful experience here. Easy walk to Faneuil Hall, the North End and the Aquarium. Short taxi ride to the theater district or Newbury street. Excellent staff and service. The children had lots of fun using the pool after dinner when there's not a lot for young ones to do in winter. Rooms were very clean and comfortable. Breakfast buffet was plentiful and very good. We'd stay again.

title: Offa's Dyke Path

description: Campground with a local pub nearby.
name: Station House Caravan Park

reviews.author: Caesar Rempel
reviews.content: We have stayed here several times, at least once on the concierge level. This time we just had a standard room, typical Marriott, comfy beds, nicely furnished, granite countertops, single serving coffee/tea maker, mini frig, about average size for a hotel in the heart of the city. The location cannot be beat - the T is right outside, as is the harbor, the aquarium, the (very good) Legal Seafood restaurant and, of course, Quincy Market and the North End. Even the tour buses and harbor tour boats are right there. Also positive - great view of harbor from our room, a new lobby with a very welcoming bar/restaurant, with tv screens everywhere including some for your private viewing in the booths. A few negatives - no newspaper delivered to the door, USA Today and WSJ are available in lobby but no local newspapers. Would be nice to have the Boston Globe to check out local events and get a feel for the city. For the first time, our stay here was very noisy. We are silver Rewards members with standing request for quiet room, which has always been honored in the past. Our room was on the fifth floor, but it fronted on the atrium, right over the bar/lounge/restaurant. Not sure if they had a convention meeting there or just a large crowd, but it was noisy well into the night. I would definitely ask for a room away from the atrium if we return, and stay elsewhere if they couldn't guarentee it. Also, they charge for internet use, even in the lobby and the business center. They do have computers in the business center for free use, but center is not very private (no door, and it's open to the lobby). I also found that I could not navigate on their computers as I would on my laptop, there seemed to be some limitations -- and I was not trying to access any racy sites!! Just gmail, trip advisor, and some event listings. The towels were also extremely thin, not at all up to the standard that the price of the room would suggest. The room lacked a magnifying mirror, which is surprising with all the business people (incl women) who stay there. Altho the new lobby was nice, we did miss the seating near the Starbucks downstairs (the ground floor has just Starbucks, registration & lobby are up a flight). Before the renovations there was seating for Starbucks so you could have breakfast there or relax with coffee and pastry in afternoon. Now it is "to go" only, so you'd have to bring your coffee and treats back to the room or eat/drink on the go. Wondering if they eliminated seating to encourage guests to have breakfast in their newly renovated restaurant??

reviews.author: Travon Little
reviews.content: I have been to this location before children a number of times. However, did not realize how unsafe the inner balcony design was until my 22 months old son tried to climb. We almost lost him, I just turned around for 2 seconds to open the hotel door when I saw him half way up on the balcony. There is no safety measure built under, so it's a straight drop to a few floor down. It was a scary experience. Tried to write and talk to someone in the hotel regarding this matter but no one seemed to notice or care. Also, there were a lot of drunken people being very loud outside the corridor in the middle of the night.

reviews.author: Louvenia Harber
reviews.content: We had a wonderful time staying at this Marriott. We stay in Boston quite often, but usually dont stay right down on the water. We had the kids and thought this would be fun. This hotel is wonderful, right across the street from teh aquariam, shopping, and food vendors. Parking was also very, very easy as they will valet everything. It was surprisingly easy to get to, but we knew how to avoid the traffic. We did see some of the notes regarding the construction, but to be honest, we never heard a thing. Looking forward to going back

reviews.author: Reginald Goodwin Jr.
reviews.content: We took the kids to Boston for a sightseeing weekend to kick off summer break. I debated whether to reserve two rooms or pile into one room. We have one pre-teen and two teenagers. I ended up reserving one room and requesting a roll away. We arrived very late on our arrival day (nearly midnight) and were relieved the roll away was already in our room. The hotel was under renovation, so felt compartmentalized and rather plain, but the cleaning staff added her own sense of sparkle to our stay which dramatically improved our opinion of the hotel. (Smiles, fresh towels, spotless room, etc...) The location was picturesque and easy. You can hop on the T literally right outside the door and there were dining options within steps of the hotel. One evening, our tired kids grabbed dinner across the street at Quincy Market and headed back to the hotel while my husband and I had a leisurely dinner at Legal Seafoods, also across the street. We did not spend a lot of time at the hotel, but found it convenient and comfortable for our stay. Positives: location, comfortable beds, excellent staff. Negatives: a little noisy.

title: Offa's Dyke Path

description: Has 40 pitches and 4 caravan sites.
name: Llyn Rhys Campsite

reviews.author: Mrs. Dovie Harber
reviews.content: Seeking a convenient location to Quincy Market and activities, we stayed here on our last night of vacation. The hotel is under construction but they had someone there to guide you where to go at all times. We were able to check in very early. Unfortunately the room we were given was right above the outdoor bar area which was very loud on a Saturday night. We called the front desk around midnight to see how late the bar would be hopping and when we got our bill in the morning, they had comped us half the cost! We were very impressed with the management. The rooms are very comfortable and clean. But the location is the best thing about this hotel (besides the Starbucks in the lobby).

reviews.author: Olga Wunsch
reviews.content: When travelling we usually stay in one of the Marriott family hotels with good experience. However, we found the experience at Marriott Long Wharf below Marriott standards. At time of booking (early June) it mentioned construction was to be finished by mid May 2011. Big surprise to find out at checking in that construction was far from over. First morning 7:10 AM we woke up at the sound of heavy construction machinery... Unacceptable! We were moved to another section of the hotel which was far less noisy, but ..... why put guests in rooms so close to the construction in the first place when other rooms are available??? Besides the construction sounds, the hotel is built in such a manner that the noise from public area below, lobby and/or events areas cannot be blocked from most rooms. That means when in your room you will certainly hear kids running around and doors being shut(throughout the night!). We were 'forced' to enjoy the music of a wedding taking place in the events area and sounds of breakfast taking place in that same area since the restaurant was temporarily under construction. Finally, service is courteous but certainly not friendly or warm. Rooms are spacious, neat and housekeeping is good. Marriott: Yes! Boston Marriott Longwharf: No!!

reviews.author: Keshawn Lockman
reviews.content: My family and I travelled to Boston for spring break, this hotel was a great choice. Step outside and the Boston waterfront, Fanueil Hall and much more is right there. They are doing construction on the lobby areas which did not affect us at all and will be done soon. Lovely pool and hot tub, great views from our room and super nice staff. The price was more than I'd hoped to pay for this trip but all in all, it was worth it and the kids LOVED it (ages 8 and 12).

reviews.author: Anastacio Kilback
reviews.content: We have stayed in or near Boston a few times before, but this was our first time at the Long Wharf. We were able to get a decent rate as a Marriott Rewards members - $195/night (although still a little hard to swallow with tax and daily parking fees but it was our five year anniversary). The location was by far one of the better places we have ever stayed in Boston. It was not even a five minute walk to Fanueil Hall/Quincy Market, and the North End was less than 10 minutes away. It was right along the water, which we probably would have taken advantage of more had the weather been nicer, but it was still a beautiful area with plenty to do. We also took advantage of one of the trolley tours which in some ways was like door to door service because the main stop is on the side of the hotel. I would definately return to the Marriott Long Wharf, and think it would be a fabulous place for the kids. Besides the aquarium, and other area attractions, there is a small park next to the hotel that has a small playscape and there is even a carousel just outside the back entrance. I cannot really comment on the service or amenities because we did not use any of the facilities or have a need to call the front desk or house keeping. The only somewhat of a downside is that the hotel does not have an area for free coffee and fruit (not a necessity, just a nice perk) although there was a Starbucks on the lower floor and there is the option to make it in your room. We were not expecting a free breakfast with our stay, so to keep the cost minimal (we splurged on lunch and dinner) we just grabbed bagels at Quincy Market in the morning. Overall, it was a very nice stay, and based on the location alone, I would definately recommend it to anyone with or without children. Our stay was pleasant, our room was clean, the beds were comfortable, there was a big screen TV in the room. In and out, our needs were met. Wish the price could have been slightly lower, but we knew that going into our stay that we could get a place with a lower price and free breakfast just outside of the mainstay. . . but then you lose the ambiance of staying in the city.

reviews.author: Ms. German Schowalter
reviews.content: We went to Boston to tour the city and stayed here. Overall, this is a nice hotel with a great location. Very close to Quincy Market, NE Aquarium, the waterfront and the Italian section of Boston. Rooms were clean and the pool and gym are excellent. Only complaints are relatively minor...we expect that for the price you would get queen beds instead of twins. Also, service by the bartenders in the restaurant and one of the bellhops did not meet my expectations for a hotel of this calibre. Otherwise, would definitely stay there again due to location and cleanliness of the hotel.

reviews.author: Cheyanne Rohan
reviews.content: We chose this hotel because it was close to the attractions we wanted to visit: aquarium, IMAX theater, Quincy Market, etc. We were steps away from the wharf where the cruises launched and the trolley bus tour also departed from the corner in front of the hotel. We stayed for two nights and the room was OK - we had requested two double beds, but were given a King room with a cot. The space was pretty tight with the cot in the room and the bathroom was on the small side. The room was very clean and the beds (and cot) were very comfortable.

reviews.author: Celestino O'Conner
reviews.content: I have stayed at the Marriott Long Wharf several times while in Boston for both business and pleasure. Overall, it is standard Marriott fare in the lobby, lounge, and restaurant. Everything is adequate and the beds are great. However, the hotel does also offer a great view from most rooms and an excellent location for visiting the historic and business areas of downtown Boston. Overall, I recommend this hotel and have chosen it myself for most visits to this fine city.

reviews.author: Lukas Murray
reviews.content: The Marriot is located right next to the Aquarium, the wharf with all of the different ferries to various places, Fanuel Hall, and the gem of the city, the North End. You can just park your car and walk any where you want, or hop on a shuttle and tour the city. It was nice and clean, quiet even though it is a huge hotel, and very comfortable, even with 4 adults in one room. The bathroom doors were a little odd - it was two small doors that opened out into the room. So they were sort of in the way at times, and not that easy to shut in a hurry. But the view was great and the stay was pleasant. I am looking forward to going back, even though it is pretty pricey to stay ($300 to start), the location is well worth it.

reviews.author: Lisette Hodkiewicz
reviews.content: We were attracted by a recent special which was run by Marriott. We stayed two nights in a room which actually had a view of Long Wharf and the boat docks. It was a quiet, spacious, well-ventilated, comfortable room, clean, with some nice new touches since our previous stay at least four years ago. Thereâ€™s a nice flat screen TV, and a refrigerator to replace the mini-bar (nice touch). Pillows are a little too soft for our tastes, and I doubled up on mine. The breakfast buffet is as well-equipped as it ever was. As we experienced in the past, check-in was quick and professional and the staff remains friendly.

title: Offa's Dyke Path

description: B&B; Self-catering accommodation
name: Forest Cottage Self-Catering

reviews.author: Lindsay Emmerich
reviews.content: The Boston Marriott Long Wharf is a spectacular hotel! The location in the city is perfect for tourists who don't know where they're going - you can walk anywhere and everywhere! The room was beautiful, the view lovely, the beds were extremely comfortable, and the staff and service was great! Right outside the hotel you can grab a delicious meal, take in the historical sights or pick up the ferry for a moonlight harbor cruise out to see the USS Constitution - breathtaking sights and a great stay! I would come back to the Marriott in heartbeat - it is well worth the cost. I highly recommend this hotel to anyone and everyone! It is a beautiful place in a great city!

reviews.author: Miguel King
reviews.content: 1st stay here, and the main + is the location: short fast cheap MTA ride from airport; close to many attractions, and on the harbor. It's in walking distance of almost everything, and if not, the MTA is great. Don't even think of renting a car in Boston--that is really asking for problems. many rooms, including mine, have water views, and others overlook a nice park. Ask for a room toward harbor end of hotel. It can get noisy on wkends with music from outdoor restaurants/bars nearby. also in spring there are hordes of school kids around the area, I suppose because of the nearby aquarium, boat rides, and on the Freedom Trail.:Reminded me of Hitchcock's The Birds, with adolescent kids substituting for birds. Rooms are small and pricey [mine was $280] and the total taxes are high--another $50+. But rooms are comfortable and clean. I wanted to open the window to get some seabreeze, since the window looked like it was designed to opne--but when I called the desk, I was told they don't open. The a/c took a while to cool the room down, but once it did so, it was comfortable. Then i went for a walk and noticed that a number of room windows were open--no explanation. As usual at Marriotts--which is why I like them--, all personnel are pleasant and responsive.

reviews.author: Devante Leuschke Jr.
reviews.content: On stopovers on my way to or from Europe, I usually stay either here or the Hilton at the airport. The Long Whart is getting a little long in the tooth and could stand some rennovations, but still it is a competent hotel only a few yards from the most "high value" sites in Boston. The cab ride from the airport to the hotel has gone up considerably over the years but it's good if you are "on your way through" and have a little time to do some sightseeing.

reviews.author: Cordia Kreiger III
reviews.content: We just came back from 3 nights stay at the Marriott Long Wharf in Boston. Whatever can go wrong went wrong with our stay. 1. Marriott made mistake with our reservation so we were placed in their small standard room with 2 double beds for $299.00. We were party of 2 adults and 2 teenage daughters. We were told by CARMEN at the front desk that they didn't have the corner unit that I requested. She said that our reservation didn't request the corner unit so that when the corner unit next to us opened up, we couldn't get it. She had to give it to someone who REQUESTED it. Finally around 9:30, we decided that this wasn't going to work so that we called in to shorten our stay. ROCHELLE from the the front desk immediately searched for bigger room for us and found the corner unit which we were told were fully booked. She apologized for the misunderstanding since our reservation shows my request for the bigger room. 2. Our third and final night, room next door left their joining door open and decided to have a LOUD LOUD sex session at 10:00 pm. We were all watching TV. My husband tried to match the volume with TV but they were louder. Thank God the session were interrupted by a phone call from their friend. After 3 calls to the front desk went without any action, I went down to ask if anything can be done about this. ANDREW placed me and my daughters in another room for no charge. This room was located right above the street level bar which were filled with at least 50 young patrons. They all left by 2:00 am. My daughters slept with pillows over their head. At least this noise was preferred to the other noise. Beside our events, we were extremely happy with the service from rest of the staff. This will not deter me from other Marriott hotel/resort since I have stayed in so many without any incidents but I will ask more questions and double check with my future hotel bookings.

reviews.author: Kaitlyn Osinski
reviews.content: We stayed here while so that we could be in the middle of everything in Boston. If I went back, I would certainly stay here again. It is close to everything and right on the water. It is close to the Chart House Restaurant and the Aquarium. The lobby was great and everyone was very friendly. The layout of the hotel is definitely different; however, it is very nice. The only downfall is the $40+ per night parking. However, you must consider that you are staying downtown Boston and that's just the price you pay for convenience. The beds were nice; however, they will soon need some upgrading. I would recommend this hotel to anyone staying in Boston for business or pleasure.

reviews.author: Rosa Moore
reviews.content: Expensive and dumpy. Nearly $200 a night and the still charge $12.50 for Internet. Go elsewhere.

reviews.author: Allison Walter
reviews.content: The hotel has a great classic vibe but they charge three times what you pay at a nice Hilton or Marriot. The bathrooms are tiny and the low pressure, archaic tub wouldn't drain. They charge $12.50 per day for wi-fi - it's 2012, McDonalds and Best Western hotels provide free wi-fi - it should not be considered a "special" service but rather a standard amenity, just as much as phone and TV serice. Residential internet costs $12.50 PER MONTH. How in the world do they justify this? Speaking of phones, they need to update those too, they look like they came from a Miami Vice set. The room had no comfortable chairs to sit in, only two rickety dining room chairs so old that there was no padding left in the seats. When I checked out, I had to wait in a 10 minute line at the desk where two atttendants tried to service 30 guests. This place obviously has the resources to update the furniture and fixtures, hire more desk help, and provide free internet. But the truth is, they're counting on guests to be so enamoured with the idea of staying at the "Historic Plaza Hotel" that they feel justified in the ridiculous room rates and embarrasing lack of comfort and tech amenities. Next time I'll go to a Double Tree for a third of the price, reasonable guest servies, and a friendlier staff. This place is overated to the extreme.

reviews.author: Seth Crist
reviews.content: Really nice staff, somewhat small rooms and double beds only but really nice. My room was perfectly updated and spotless. There were a ton of young European kids in the lobby but they were very quiet at night, and it was a wonderful stay. Thank you!

reviews.author: Blanche Cole
reviews.content: classy hotel but the water pressure in my shower made it feel like I was taking a bird bath, but other than that had a great stay

title: Offa's Dyke Path

description: [[Bed and Breakfast]] with 3 bedrooms (1 ''en suite'') welcomes families and also has camping facilities. Evening meals and packed lunch (£4) available on request.
name: Glan-yr-Afon B&B
price: £30 pppn (£25 for >2 nights) includes guests' sitting room and own entrance

reviews.author: Tiffany Kiehn
reviews.content: I would never ever stay at this hotel again...Inside the hotel is run down and the lobby is nothing spectacular.. I know it is an old hotel but they really could modernize it.. I stayed here with my boyfriend for a concert.. (and believe me we are not picky.. we are only in our early 20's) and hated it.. we got a suite and there was only the bed, desk, and two chairs in the room.. it was just tons of empty space with no seating area.. and a really tiny bathroom.. our smoke detector was hanging out of the ceiling and all of the paint in the room was chipped.. The location is fantastic and the places to eat connected to the hotel are very good.. but the location itself does not make up for how awful the hotel is.. I thought for a city like Boston it would have some charm.. but nope.. stick to the Back Bay Hotel or the TAJ

reviews.author: Franco Mitchell
reviews.content: We were terribly disappointed by this hotel. During our first night we were awakened by screaming and pounding on the door of the room beside us by some man who was clearly intoxicated. This lasted for quite a while and was actually quite scary. However since it was NYE we hoped it wouldn't occur the next night. The next morning the room service dishes that were sitting outside that room since early the day before had still not been cleared. Far worse was what we saw running through our closet and then under our door into the hallway.....a mouse!! I was horrified. After calling down and explaining the girl said "gross" and promptly transferred me to someone who offered a room upgrade and to comp that night for us. The next room had a mouse trap under the bed (empty thankfully). Obviously this is an ongoing problem for the hotel which they have failed to adequately address over the years.

reviews.author: Julius Fahey
reviews.content: We stayed here for one night on Jan 2, 2012. I booked the hotel after much debate after reading mixed reviews on TripAdvisor, Google, and other travel sites. However, for a price of $102 for a Deluxe King Room, I couldn't argue. Our room was on a corner of the building and was sizeable. The linens were fresh, the bed seemed fairly new, the carpet was plush and everything was really clean. They even had a sizable LCD TV, with actual HDTV. Most places you go have the LCD TVs, but regular standard def. Anyway, the room was perfect for what we needed, a place to relax in the evening and get a nice night of sleep. I didn't encounter any issues with the thermostat, I simply lowered the temperature to 68 and it was perfect. I could even cut off the heating/cooling unit, had we gotten too hot or cold, so those complaints from other reviewers are unfounded. Complaints about the bathroom are valid, it was pretty small. Barely enough room for the shower, toilet and sink. However, being a guy I don't have an issue with it, as I shower, or use the sink and toilet and get out, and don't plan on spending hours at a time in front of a mirror. For that, it was adequate. Also you should remember that this hotel was built in the 1920s, so its historic and things may be small. In the end, this hotel is a great spot to spend a few nights. Its got a great location, its relatively cheap, and its easily a 4 star hotel. Is it 5 star? Definitely not on account of the bathroom. I feel like some people may be a bit picky on this site and expect a Ritz Carlton. The fact is, the price is much lower than many other hotels in the area, so any 'issues' you may run across are compensated for. Also, the complaints about $12.50/day for wifi are valid, BUT you have to remember EVERY other hotel in Boston, as well as most chains - Marriott, Hilton, Ritz Carlton, charge that amount or more for wi-fi. Its a way for hotels to make money. Back in the 80s-90s they made it off of phone calls, but now with cell phones they have to make up for it somewhere. If you don't like it, go to a Starbucks, McDonalds or get a smart phone like the rest of the country.

reviews.author: Kiel Mertz
reviews.content: There is much to be said about this hotel that is great. The location is excellent - the lobby is old world style elegant and well-maintained. The front desk staff is very helpful and courteous -might be the fastest check-in service ever. We booked a standard king room, which turned out to be two small rooms that had been combined. Good size space in the room, and there were two bathrooms. Here's the caution - they were the tiniest bathrooms I've ever seen. On one side were the toilet and bathtub and no space in between. The sink was at the end of the bathtub. There is minimal counter space and most of it was taken up by the rack holding shampoo, soap, etc, plus a tissue box and cups. So just beware -- not all the bathrooms in this hotel are the same. Bed was very comfortable and there was a flat-screen tv in the room. The view was non-existent - both windows looked out on an air shaft and another building. There was no closet - only a free-standing wardrobe about 20" wide. (The bottom of this was very dusty, as I found out when a pair of dark slacks fell off a hanger.) One inexcusable oversight - I got out the extra blanket that had been neatly stored in a zippered bag in the wardrobe - hence the fallen pants - and when I opened it, discovered that it had multiple holes cut out of it. It looked like someone had tried to remove burn spots but only made it worse. I dropped it on the floor and it was left there the entire time of our visit. Kind of made me wonder if the room ever got vacuumed. I would stay here again because the price was right and location very convenient.

reviews.author: Sabina Shields
reviews.content: Obviously been a grand hotel in it's heyday, BUT, that was a long tome ago. The pictures are great but it's quite a bit shabbier in reality. Plus Point, the staff were really friendly and gave " GOOD OLD AMERICAN SERVICE ". I HAVE STAYED IN PLACES A LOT WORSE BUT I REALLY DID EXPECT BETTER IN AMERICA.

reviews.author: Ara Wintheiser
reviews.content: Was here for business and stayed Friday and Saturday nights (November 4 and 5, 2011). Was in Room 708, I think. Had a king bed. Room was very warm. Kept the heater turned off. I am usually a very sound sleeper, but the noise from the hallway and the street were unbearable. The windows have absolutely no soundproofing from the outside noise. Every car, horn and person was heard at all hours of the night (and I live in NYC!!). On Saturday night, there was some party in the club on the ground floor. It was packed, and the loud rap music was blaring. I could hear the THUMP THUMP THUMP of the music. I called downstairs about 1 am and was practically laughed at when I requested if they could do something about the noise. The room itself was mediocre, at best. Small, outdated bathroom, with sporadic hot water. There were two phones in the room. Neither worked. Twice I stopped at the front desk asking them to be fixed. Good thing my iPhone has a built in alarm, as I could not request a wake up call. Skip this place. Not worth it.

reviews.author: Henri Hayes
reviews.content: The Boston park plaza boast of history. However the rooms and the foyers need need carpets and decor. Furniture too needs replacement. Bedding was comfortable and sleep quality is good. The room needs better sound insulation . restaurants on site are good.

reviews.author: Virgie Watsica Sr.
reviews.content: My stay was not a happy stay, room is ok, no thermostat, tiny washroom, hot water is on and off phenomenon,rude staff, stuffy room...way too expensive for this...

reviews.author: Evan Hodkiewicz
reviews.content: Hotel is deceiving on first blush! Large, opulent, historic lobby...tiny, less than well appointed rooms, paper thin walls, NO WiFi/internet w/out ridiculous fees (what century are we in?), difficult to find/reach plugs in the room (many did not work) and staff who are not uniformly knowledgeable or helpful. So many little things added up to one major (and expensive!) disappointment, and I would not recommend a stay here.

reviews.author: Reyes Rippin
reviews.content: What a great staff and location! We were very pleased with our room and the friendliness of the staff. We were upgraded our second night (because we decided to stay another night) to a king suite. It had amazing views and was spacious. Kelly & Carlos were terrific! Would highly recommend to anyone who appreciates colonial charm rather than a "cookie cutter" hotel chain.

reviews.author: Cory Huels
reviews.content: An unexpected trip to Boston required us to find a room for the night. Trough trip advisor we got a room at the Park Plaza for $240. When I asked if we could reserve the same room for the next night, the rate would be $575! When we arrived at the hotel, we were upgraded to the tower level. When we arrived, the room looked as if it had been used for a meeting in the afternoon (room service trays outside the door and notes on the desk). Other than that the room was very clean. The bed was very comfortable -- but we could not control the room temperature -- even pushing the temp control down to 64, the room never went below 75. As a business traveller, I have a personal beef with high price hotels that charge for internet. We were only in the room for 10 hours, I did not want to pay $10.25 to send out two e-mails. Usually, there is a common area where internet is available. Such was not the case at this hotel.

title: Offa's Dyke Path

name: Blue Bell

reviews.author: Kariane Brekke
reviews.content: A/C-heat does not work, however Staff did supply a tiny "space heater" 9-8-11' Toilet flushes slowly and 9-10-11, upon flushing, it EXPELLED the entire bowl of human (my) waste onto the bathroom floor. - Staff (M) offered me a "free breakfast" when I reported the disgusting situation and threaten to have Security remove me from the Hotel when I declined the breakfast offer and pressed the Desk Manager for the Hotel Manager's name and telephone contact information. The Manager's name was given as Rob --, but he couldn't be contacted on a weekend. I had obviously pre-paid or Security might have been needed. I WOULD NOT GO NEAR THIS HOTEL AGAIN EVEN IF SOMEONE HAD ME AT GUN POINT !!! (One of the two "Desk Managers (C. S.) did agree to and accompanied me at my request to the room to witness the disgusting mess in person)

reviews.author: Tate Swift
reviews.content: My husband and I were only in town for one night. I decided to cancel our reservation at the Nine Zero and book here to save a little money. Huge mistake. I get the hotel is old, I expected that and it is charming in that way. What I didn't expect was 10 year old televisions and no free internet. The location is good and for business I could see the draw (except for the no internet). I think for the price you can find better at a place nearby. The check in and check out process was quick and painless. The beds were decent but the bathrooms showed their age and the floors are very slippery when wet, even with a towel down. Beware of the concierge, they seemed to be pushy when it came to getting a cab or taking the hotel truck, although either will set you back about $30 to Logan.

title: Offa's Dyke Path

description: 1870's Gothic mansion set in 280 acres of mature gardens and tranquil parkland with mullioned windows, oak panelling and beautiful staircase. 10 individually designed rooms and suites, all ''en suite'' with unlimited Wi-Fi. No pets allowed. Afternoon tea and home made cakes in the ''Offas Dyke Bar''. Lunch 12.00–14:00, Dinner 18.30–21:00 served in one of 4 restaurants: the ''Cwm Dining Room'', the ''Mahogany Panelled Restaurant'', the ''William Morris Room'', or the ''Shropshire Lounge''. Local ingredients and suppliers are used wherever possible with many ingredients traceable to source. Graded *** with Welsh Tourist Board. The most luxorius camp site I have met. Camp by lake next to facilities block. Phone owner for entrance code. Pay £5 pppn (2014) in the morning to groundsman. 5 star hotel next door are polite but claim to know nothing about camping as its under separate ownership. Hotel
name: Mellington Hall Hotel

reviews.author: Stephen Graham
reviews.content: End of a wonderful trip saw us land here. In a nutshell - rude bell staff (note I will not tip poor service and bad attitudes just because you expect it), rude front desk staff and staff who had to be kept out of the room - you may have been desperate to clean it but check out is 12 (and no later). This hotel has the smallest hotel room I have ever seen in the USA. Poor beyond words. Great location but that's all it's got going for it (don't be hopeful from the grand entrance and internet pictures!)

reviews.author: Madelyn Rolfson
reviews.content: I spent one night here on a quick getaway to do my own historical walking tour. The hotel touts its own history and though nice, I was not particularly impressed overall. The Park Plaza seemed almost as though it was trying to be too many things to too many people...more than one wedding booked (large lighted ,glossy photos and names of couples in lobby detracting from the historic decor), lots of high maintenance vacationers, European travelers, even airline flight crews. Amid the shuffle, I felt a bit overlooked as a lone traveler. At one point, I waited in a long line for the Concierge to ask for a walkable map of the historic African-American sites trail, only to be told hurriedly that they didn't have any but "the trail starts on the other side of the park". The group in front of me in line however, booked a boat tour, made dinner reservations for a family of 4, and got directions from the Concierge. All I wanted was a map. Maybe it would have been better had I not been traveling in the middle of the summer? In any case, the rooms have a nice historic flair (skeleton key doors) and are small but perfectly acceptable. The room was clean but my bed sheet was stained, which was pretty unexpected considering the caliber of the hotel. Overall, I could not have asked for a better location and for the seasoned traveler who needs little direction or attention, it was a reasonable choice.

reviews.author: Fabian Langosh
reviews.content: I booked a junior suite at the Park Plaza for our family vacation. Upon check in, there were no junior suites, so we were upgraded to some fabulous 2-room suite on the 15th floor of the Towers. It was lovely and the 15th floor suites include complimentary evening appetizers and morning breakfast. The 2-room suite accomodated us nicely and we were very gracious for the upgrade. However, the airconditioning would not go below 77-degrees (It was set to be 64-degrees when we arrived)!. Granted, on day one, Boston got hit by the near 100-degree heat wave. On day 2, i made 3 requests between 9 am and 10:45 pm for the AC to be looked at and i also requested a portable fan for the room. Sleeping night number one was miserable, difficult and hot! Anyhow, after my 3rd request for assistance, and it was now 11:15 PM and I needed to go to bed, so i walked down to the front desk and nicely explained my unhappiness and discomfort. The desk clerk appologized profusely and gave me her portable box fan from behind the counter. I was happy to have a fan at last, but displeased that my 3 earlier requests were disregarded. On day number 3 the room temp with AC would still only go down to 77, although the weather out was pleasant and mildat 78-degrees. We opened our windows and slept with them open because it was cooler out than in. All other aspects of the hotel were grand. The location right by a T station and 1 block from the Boston Public Garden can't be beat. The hotel is not cheap to stay at, and we were still paying a good chunk of change to stay there regardless of recieving an upgrade, so it is not accecptable to disregard a guests request for room comfort. Still, despite the AC situation, I would recommend this hotel and I would stay there again.

reviews.author: Makenzie Towne
reviews.content: We stayed on the 15th floor in the Towers. The price was very reasonable for a major city hotel ($130/night) and if you get a room on the 15th floor, you have access to a private elevator, free wifi, a private lounge with free continental breakfast and afternoon hors-d'oeuvres. The room was very clean and comfortable. The location is fantastic - a block away from the Gardens/Boston Common, two blocks from the shops in Back Bay, close to the beginning of the Freedom Trail. We caught a Red Sox game and actually were able to walk all the way to Fenway Park without much problem (took us about 40 minutes). You can also walk to the South End where there are some great restaurants.

reviews.author: Trevor Predovic
reviews.content: I found my room to be somewhat dark and gloomy but I suppose that relates in part to the age and historic ambiance of the hotel.The garage parking was expensive,$44 per day.Also they charge for internet access and local calls.The staff however were helpful,especiaaly the concierge Frank Gallagher.He recommended Old Town Trolley Tours who were excellent.
