Plenty of drawer space for a long stay if you need it. Bathroom amenities were Bulgari. The room and carpet were very clean - even the outside windows had been recently cleaned! The entire lobby smelled of fresh Gardenia - ahhhh and the lobby floral arrangements were stunning! Cabs are not plentiful in New Orleans right now. We had trouble getting cabs more than once. We managed one to Commander's Palace for Sunday Brunch, but we never even thought to ask him to return to get us. We ended up walking all the way back to the hotel (almost 3 miles) which wasn't a bad idea after a big brunch - but I could have used other shoes to make the trip! One cabbie told us there are only 1/3 of the cabs left in town that were there before Katrina. The Ritz is a 1 block walk to Bourbon St. It is on the very end of Bourbon, which is a great location - still on the outside but close enough. It seems as though most of NOLA is headed in a positive direction. Once again we were treated to great southern hospitality and met very friendly people. The staff of the Ritz was pleasant, but not overly stuffy. My guess is that people who have negative opinions of the service here are used to getting fussed over a bit more (spoiled?). We saw a nice demonstration of that at the front desk as a man threw a fit that he needed help with his bags immediately because his "private jet" was due to leave asap! Whatever dude! We found the service to be excellent - especially during the busiest time of year. The hotel was spotless and if you weren't in town to celebrate Mardi Gras this would be the place to stay - it was downright quiet even though the hotel was very full. I would stay here again if the price was right, but I don't know if I will ever find the great deal that we had again!

reviews.author: Addie Lowe
reviews.content: I just returned from a trip to New Orleans and was somewhat disappointed by the Ritz Carlton. I can't say that anything especially bad happened to me when I was there, it's just that the service was not up the Ritz standards. I travel a fair bit for work and usually stay in Ritz Carltons and Four Seasons and I like this hotel less than any other Ritz I've stayed in. I thought the decor of my room was pretty horrifying. There was dark Victorian-looking wallpaper with matching drapes and near matching comforter. Suffice it to say that it was not my thing stylistically. Also, there was hair on the shower walls in the bathroom (not a lot but enough to make you wonder about how thoroughly the rooms are cleaned). The service was pretty good but just not as crisp as a typical Ritz. For example, when I called down to get my car brought up the morning of my departure, the attendant's answer was "gotcha covered." I didn't think that was especially appropriate. Finally, once I got downstairs 10 minutes after calling, the car still hadn't been brought up. I had to wait another 5 minutes. Maybe that would have been understandable if it was busy, but this was 5am and no one was around. Until I find a better hotel in NO, I'd probably stay there again but would certainly lower my expectations.

reviews.author: Keaton Murazik
reviews.content: We just returned from visiting the Ritz for our 20th anniversary. As I'm originally from Pascagoula, MS, I was anxious about seeing how New Orleans was rebuilding (lives as well as buildings). Many thanks to all of you who posted encouragement to visit, you were right...it welcomes visitors with open arms. I'll try to be concise with my info, so here goes. Where we ate: Breakfast at the Club Level-light stuff, fruit, berries, etc. which was good, considering our other meals. Lunch-Masperas (sp?) one day as I was scouring the city for a soft-shelled crab po-boy. Hot and hungry, settled for a shrimp sandwich (po-boy like, but on a bun) and it was good. The line outside cracked me up-all these cranky and hot people waiting to get in-you feel like you've won the lottery to get in AC. Other lunch-New Orleans School of Cooking which is in the quarter, 2 1/2-3 hrs., good food, very entertaining. Loved their jambalaya, bread pudding and pralines but the gumbo was just soso as they had to make it in less than 4-6 hrs. Dinners-the hotel restaurant. Crab trio was great, filet with crab was good, hubby's was so bad he had to complain (very unusual as he'll eat most anything). Great jazz band in there, preceded by a female singer who was also good. Also went to Commander's Palace. The BEST service I've received that I can remember, ever. Very reasonable ($39 for appetizer/entree/dessert!)-started with the waiter's suggestion of crawfish something-it was divine. Hubby said the turtle soup was good, not great. He regularly eats it at the Brennans in Houston which he prefers. Entrees were soft-shelled crab prepared with some other stuff-I'm sorry I can't remember. The crab was very good. DH had a fish dish that had crabmeat which he loved. The dessert...I truly have never tasted better cheesecake in my entire life! They make their own cream cheese! Hubby had the praline parfait but couldn't stay out of my cheesecake. We had the rest wrapped up to fit in the little fridge. It was that good. The hotel: Smells WONDERFUL! Beautiful flowers, great service (although they forgot turndown both nights), nice bathrooms with separate toilet area, nice furniture in the rooms, and frette linens!!! Slept like a baby... Other things we did: lots of walking around, antiquing, looking at art, took a nice carriage ride and got to see a funeral! You must see a New Orleans funeral! The band plays jazz (happy or sad, depending on the direction they're going) and the mourners follow it, carrying umbrellas. It was so moving, we got out of the carraige to pay our respects. I know this probably doesn't sound very action packed to most of you, but we really needed to relax this weekend. We did walk around with a 'hand grenade' which was a green drink in a silly glass. Thats always fun. And we spent Sunday morning watching Nadal beat Federer...again! Thanks for reading and please don't hesitate to visit NOLA. Yes, its hot (just like Houston), and yes, some areas you don't want to venture down-like empty streets, but we truly never felt unsafe. Oops, not so concise, but I tried

reviews.author: Gerald Koch
reviews.content: I have to start by saying that the following stay occured during the weekend before Mardi Gras. With that said, when we arrived at the hotel at 3 o'clock in the afternoon we were first told our room was ready, then it would a few minutes, so they would buy a drink, very nice. After an hour we were told, someone else actually had our room, so it would be a few more minutes. I should interject here, that some of the staff were very poorly trained and acted as if we were inconviencing them because they were so busy. We were told to go to the lounge and wait they would call us on our cell phone. Finally at 5:30, 2 and 1/2 hours after we arrived, we went back to the registation desk. The woman said, "We have plenty of rooms in the club section, we will upgrade you". But what she meant was we will put you in club level and charge you more. It was an extra $150 per night. We were tired from our flight and said fine. So finally after now 3 hours we were about to get to a room. Here is the kicker, when we got to the room it was occuppied. I mean, the bell boy, actually opened the door, we walked in and someone was in there! Finally got a room 3 and 1/2 hours after arriving. By the way, many other people had to wait for their rooms and we were told they were short staffed for cleaning rooms. I'd like to assume that my experience was due in part to Mardi Gras, problems finding staff in the wake of Katrina, and a hotel being renovated. ROOM Nice bed, but suprisingly a regular TV, 24 inch, limited cable. Great bathtub and a menu of exotic baths they will prepare for you. Bulgari bathroom amenities. High speed internet, but they charge you an additional $12.95 on top of the $500 plus a night they are already getting during Mardi Gras for a club level room. CLUB LOUNGE While they state 5 "tastings" or meals, in reality there is only 5 on Friday & Saturday. The other days it is really only 4, in fact the 4th or last of the day is simply drinks and some desserts. Overall I'm not sure if the club level is worth the extra money, in our case about $150 extra per night on top of a standard room for around $350 during Mardi Gras. In addition, it should be noted that getting to the club level requires 2 elevators and a walk. To get to your room requires a 3rd elevator. They claim a new elevator direct to the street will be open in April, so that should no longer be an issue. LOCATION While you are close to Bourbon St. and the French Quarter, it is not in the safest area of New Orleans. Be careful at night near the hotel and DO NOT WALK THE WRONG WAY UP CANAL ST. If you've been drinking, take a taxi back to the hotel. Also, always ask taxi drivers to turn on their meters. New Orleans taxi drivers are notorius for ripping off their fares. CONCIERGE We had really wanted to go to Jaces Imo's restrurant. We asked the concierge to make a reservation and she simply said it is closed. I would've expected another recommendation at least. Granted she was busy, but hey I thought this was the Ritz Carlton and they could handle Mardi Gras with their usual high level of service. They certainly knew how to charge at a high level.

title: South Uist

description: A guest house with ensuite bedrooms about a mile from the ferry.
name: Brae Lea House

reviews.author: Bruce Mitchell
reviews.content: This is one of many wonderful Ritz Carlton properties. Although they do not all live up to their brand, this facility definitely does. Great location walking distance to the French Quarter. Wonderful rooms, beautiful courtyard, many well appointed bars and restaurants.

reviews.author: Rosemary Kuhn
reviews.content: I have stayed in many Ritz-Carlton's and was always a satisfied guest when checking out. But not his time!!! This time, my experience was not a very good one and I am very disappointed. The New Orleans Ritz-Carlton has to many flaws to justify a high classification of a top ranked luxury hotel. The rooms do not seem to be in a very good shape. The carpet in my room had many stains, and it looked like it need a proper cleaning. My room was also very noisy, letting me hear lots of disturbing noises from the street and from the rooms next to mine. Most of the hotel staff (housekeeping, room service, front desk) did not act very professional and seem to lack training. My recent New Orleans Ritz-Carlton experience was terrible in comparison to other Ritz-Carlton hotels, and well below the high service standard it normally offers under this flag.

reviews.author: Roselyn Veum II
reviews.content: Yes the Ritz sets high expectations which means they have to stay sharp. I respect that, understand it, and am willing to pay for it. However, my stay last week in New Orleans left a little to be desired. Four days later, I stayed at the Holiday Inn in Historic Charleston and received twice the service at half the price. And yes, part of that was based on expectations. My stay at the Ritz was off-kilter by a stained carpet, red wine or ?, my room charge going up by $40 mid-week, stuffy front desk staff, and a focus on exceeding the expectations of not me, but other people. The spirit is there, but the delivery is a little weak at this hotel. I'll try again and hopefully, they will try harder.

reviews.author: Jerrold Gutkowski IV
reviews.content: We stayed in an Executive Suite on a recent four day trip to New Orleans. The suite appeared perfect initially then we discovered an unclean bathroom facility and waited two days for a special request from housekeeping. Despite the rocky start the service for the most part was up to Ritz-Carlton standards though turn down was skipped one night. The lack of a swimming pool was a disappointment in the August heat of New Orleans. There always seemed to be security personnel around the entrances to both the Ritz and the Maison-Orleans during the day. At night there was no visible security. We had to report an obvious intrusion by a New Orleans "less fortunate" into the Maison elevators at 2 am to a befuddled night guest service person. The person wandering around was harmless and simply looking to gain access..but this was not reassuring about the hotel security concerns. All the personnel were friendly and helpful until departure when my traveling companion was instructed to find a taxi on Canal Street upon departure. I can say I amazed the Ritz in New Orleans has maintained its 5 star 5 diamond ratings. I wrote an email to management concerning both praise and a couple of the problems. I am happy to say I was answered promptly, courteously and in writing. For that reason I will return to the Ritz in New Orleans. Otherwise the Windsor Court would get my business in the future.

reviews.author: Abbey Carroll I
reviews.content: This is the second time I've stayed here and I really like antique decor, balcony, and porch. The relaxed friendly atmosphere gives me a homey feeling. I find the historical nature of the hotel inspiring for my photography activities in the French Quarter and surrounding areas. It has always been clean and well neat.

reviews.author: Allan Will
reviews.content: I booked this hotel because of the incredible location in the French Quarter and because the rest of the city was sold out. At the time of my booking this hotel was #143 out of 151 hotels in New Orleans, so I was expecting a complete dive. I have to say I was pleasantly surprised. We arrived in the evening and a gentleman met us as we got out of the taxi with our keys. The room we were in had a door facing Royal street on the 1st floor. Yes, the furniture was old. Yes, the decorations were old. Yes, it smelled a little musty. But it was a great experience. There aren't big frills like Room Service and Mini Bars, but there is a kitchen with a full size refrigerator, coffee maker, adequate shower and bathroom facility, beautiful antique decorations, and most of all a true New Orleans experience. The one staff member that met us was available when we needed him for an iron, directions, and general friendly conversation. I agree that if you're looking for somewhere fancy look elsewhere, but if you're interested in a room with charachter that is literally one block from Bourbon street and walking distance of everything you need, this is the place.

reviews.author: Kip Langworth
reviews.content: The valets were extremely informative and polite. I received my car very quickly. Thanks to Bobby. He was a pleasure to work with. He is commended for hiswork service. I would recommend this hotel to a friend.

reviews.author: Stephany Bauch
reviews.content: We stayed here before we took our cruise. Everyone was very friendly and helpful. Valet, while pricey, was very prompt with our car and very personable. I remember one valet team member, Richard, was super! The front desk staff was also wonderful. We actually booked the room on Priceline, and we had never heard of it before. We were very happy!! We had a balcony room, and the street noise was nonexistent. We would love to stay here again!!!

title: South Uist

description: Good bar meals in the evening.
name: Lochboisdale Hotel
title: South Uist

description: Ty Mortimer cottage situated on Treginnis Uchaf Farm, west of St Davids. 10 minute walk to the coastal path and Porthllisky beach. Or Y Nyth cottage in a quiet location near the centre of St Davids, shops & cathedral with easy car access to local beaches. Good for couples and families. Off road parking. Sleeps up to 5. Free Wi-Fi.
name: Treginnis Cottages

reviews.author: Lizzie Kerluke
reviews.content: Just spent 2 nights here and I have mixed reviews. The check-in and front desk staff were very nice and helpful - we were off to a good start. The room is eclectically decorated - fun and colorful and was reasonably comfortable. But we were disappointed that on 2 separate occasions when we called housekeeping to request a couple of items, 2 hours passed and we had to call again. Although the room looked clean - the carpets needed a good shampooing. The location of the hotel is excellent and parking was so easy. But at the rates charged for this hotel I would have expected clean carpets, a notebook in the room with the hotels internal numbers to call, local services and restaurants and an extra set of glasses for the bathroom. Overall the stay was fine - but I don't think I would stay here again considering the other hotel options in the area..

reviews.author: Dexter Thompson
reviews.content: We stayed at the Pier 5 Hotel and booked the Waterfront Invasion package for 3 nights that included the VIP Aquarium tickets, VIP Science Center admission and $25.00 gift certificate which we used at Ruth Chris for dinner. Our experience was wonderful. I really liked the happy hour crabby appetizers they held at our hotel. Jill our assistant hotel manager made wonderful crab dip on Thursday than crab crepes on Friday and they had beer and wine also complementary. She made the happy hour fun and we got to see hands on cooking while enjoying cocktails. Saturday was the fun Chocolate extravaganza with fun dessert to dip into chocolate. After we enjoyed our day at the harbor we came back and enjoyed the view from our balcony of the harbor and people watching. Even though we live in Catonsville, it was a fun weekend being a tourist in Baltimore. Thanks!

reviews.author: Queenie Gerlach
reviews.content: I got married at this hotel in June 2005 and have stayed here several times since for weekend getaways with my husband. We just love the place. The service is always wonderful and they always remember us. We've even received gifts in our room at times. We love the funky difference of this hotel, it isn't like your average place and the location is perfect. The decor is art deco and the smaller size makes it feel more comfortable. One of the most memorable things to me is how clean the rooms always smell. So fresh, I want to know what they use to clean or wash sheets with because it smells so good I instantly relax. I've heard alot about the noise in the hotel and I can't honestly remember ever being bothered by it, however, it does have 2 event spaces for weddings and other party events so I can understand the noise. It won't stop me from visiting again and again!

reviews.author: Daisy Robel
reviews.content: My husband and I had a wonderful stay at the Pier 5 Hotel. We booked through Priceline for $90 a night and felt it was well worth the price. The location was excellent - right on the Inner Harbor and close to the Baltimore Aquarium, Camden Yards, and the local areas of interest (Little Italy, Fells Point). The room was nice and quiet. They even had a complimentary 'crabby hour' each night where a snack was made and wine/beer was provided. My only complaint was the $9.95 activity fee that was charged for each night stayed. I wasn't aware of the fee before we checked in. Overall great stay.

reviews.author: Virginia Breitenberg
reviews.content: we spent a weekend at this hotel. our VALET parked car was broken into. this fine hotel pushed us to the parking lot company for answers. the good part about this is paying $31.00 a day for valet parking and not knowing someone else has your car. our car was parked in a gated parking lot with 24 hour guards and after the $1700.00 break in occurred we received a letter stating that since this was a premediated act they were not responsible for anything. i will let as many people as i can know about this customer care policy. thanks pier 5 hotel, baltimore inner harbor, wfoster

reviews.author: Wilber Quitzon
reviews.content: My husband and I decided to getaway mid week to go to Baltimore and see a concert at Rams Head Live in mid-July. We splurged and stayed at the Pier 5 Hotel. The hotel is absolutly gorgeous! The staff were extremely friendly. The room was AMAZING! It was so very modern, the color sceme in our room was gold and purple, and even the bathroom was gorgeous -much different than your typical hotel bathroom. The bed was very, very comfortable as were the couch and chair. I wanted to take the chair home with us! Avoid eating at the hotel's cafe. The breakfast there was awful. Don't bother purchasing a package deal either with the hotel. It's not worth the extra money and I found the breakfast coupons to be a total waste of money since no food was really offered with them. If you want to splurge stay here. We probably won't stay there again because it was very expensive for our means, but worth the night we spent.

reviews.author: Brody Lubowitz
reviews.content: Pretty much what I expected for the cost and location. I would stay here again if there were a bigger room. We spent most of our time at my family's timeshare rental and came back here at nights to walk the boardwalk and crash. This is all you need at the beach, nothing more. Generally, the room we stayed I was clean. Toiletries are minimal and so are the furnishings. Management isn't really visible regularly, but we never needed them.

title: St Davids

description: Caravan Club site, level site for tourers and camper vans. Fantastic views. Water tap and disposal point. Batteries charged.
name: Treginnis

reviews.author: Pedro Skiles
reviews.content: We only went down to ocean city for one night and wanted to stay close to the boardwalk..This was very close to the boardwalk and beach..The hotel is in great condition. The only complaint is that our room had a small shower and the water pressure wasn't very good. I would stay there again. I also think that they have apartment rooms so I'm sure that would be more spacious.

reviews.author: Jess Kiehn
reviews.content: The room was clean, but sparse. Not even a chair to sit in. There was a TV, but it was one of those smaller flat-screens that you sometimes see, I guess I really didn't come to the beach to watch TV, though. If we hadn't been allowed to park in the Americana parking lot across the street while it's undergoing renovations, it would have been a nasty inconvenience to have to walk three blocks away across a busy street to get back and forth from the car. The porch was nice, rocking chairs were comfortable, and the breeze felt good. I was dismayed at first about not having a beach view from our room, but that soon faded when I realized what other places in the area were charging. Good thing we were there during the "off" season, or it might have seemed a bit cramped.

reviews.author: Rory Tillman Jr.
reviews.content: There are some good things and some bad things about this hotel. First the good: The hotel has a great location. It is located just steps from the boardwalk. It is the second building from the boardwalk which means it doesnt face it but you can see it from the hotels front porches that feature chairs. The managment is on site. The owners ( a husband and wife - although you deal with the wife) live on site. They take up the first floor of the three story hotel so if you need something you can ask them. Then the bad: There are no elevators and so you will have to walk up stairs that are outside with your bags. The rooms and the lobby are on the 2nd and 3rd floors because the owners live on the first floor. Many of the hotels in Ocecan City and even on the boardwalk feature on site parking. This is not one of them. There is a parking lot that is located 3 blocks away (across a very busy road). Another option though is on street parking. There are some spaces in the city that you do not have to pay for and can park for days on end and are very safe which I used my entire stay. I was able to find spaces three times. Since the hotel does not face the boardwalk the side of the hotel has views of the boardwalk. The boardwalk area is very dense so there is another row of buildings between the hotel and the boardwalk so room views arent that great. Overall this hotel was pretty good....it was not that expensive. The hotel is in a great location (there is a hotel across the street and a B&B next to it) so if you can live with the little quirks its worth a try.

reviews.author: Precious Heaney V
reviews.content: The rooms at this hotel are more like separate apartments so it is really good if you want a bit more privacy/independence. Our room (which I think was a medium suite) had a seating area, dining area, kitchen and massive bed. We were in the building on St Stephen's Street and we heard very little noise from the other rooms. The surrounding area was residential and really nice, quiet and felt safe. It was also near to shops (including the Prudential Centre) and two subway stations. Having looked around we found this hotel to be cheaper than a lot of others and, based on the quality of the room and the surrounding area, I think it is good value.

reviews.author: Vallie Botsford
reviews.content: Great location and clean rooms. I was in a one bedroom suite with two adults and 3 teenagers. The bed was comfortable, the pull out sofa was *very* uncomfortable. The bedding that was provided for the pullout sofa was inadequate, only a blanket and no bedspread or comforter, my kids froze. I called the next morning for a comforter or extra blankets plus an aerobed and when we got to the room that evening nothing had been placed in the room. Also we were not used to city noise, the windows were not new and thus not soundproofed and we were able to hear people talking in the street.

reviews.author: Miss Ova Heathcote
reviews.content: We were shown to an apartment in the cellar of a building that was a block away from The Copley House. The apartment was disgusting to say the least. The room had not been made up, the carpet dirty, fixtures in a poor state of repair and extensive mold on the walls. All though we paid for parking, the spot allocated at the property was already taken and we had to park a block away outside the main building. Much time was wasted attempting to get the apartment made up. Whilst The Copley House is well located; we will not be using it again and do not consider it good value for money.

reviews.author: Ms. Lonzo Deckow
reviews.content: First impressions count. Receptionist was busy eating at her desk when I arrived. Check-in forms strewn over her desk. Check-in was OK, but then was taken to the end of the street and given an address in an adjoining street. This was not a short distance away, but 3 blocks! The room was a bedsit, the furniture old and stained, the bedroom unbelievably small. The wallpaper was peeling and there were holes in them (the walls). There has been no attempt at renovation/updating in about 30 years. For the money this place is a ripoff. The final straw came when I realized I'd left my phone charger behind and called their reception he same day I checked out, but only got their voicemail service. I told them I would return in 2 weeks to collect. hen I called in, guess what? yes the receptionist had his takeout meal half eaten in front of him. No one seemed to have a clue. The senior assistant said they had no procedure for lost property, but then said they usually posted out! This hotel is the pits and you should avoid at all costs. I sure wish I'd taken some photos no one would want to stay, especially at the prices they're charging.

reviews.author: Raquel Batz
reviews.content: As most people know who are either going to visit boston or have visited boston already, the hotels there are outrageously expensive. Copley house is actually a great alternative. They offer self-catering apartments in an excellent location. When we first got to the office, which is in a beautiful back bay location on West Newton Street, we were told that they had four different properties and they had upgraded us from a small studio to a medium studio, free of charge, which was at their location on St. Stephens st., a few blocks away. When we got to the place, we found out that we were in a basement studio in a great, little building on a beautiful street, near many of the places that we wanted to go to. Despited being a "basement" studio, we really weren't underground and the place actually had it's own private backyard, which was nice, even though we never did use it. The only drawback was the noise. We could hear the water dripping from upstairs constantly, but it wasn't a big deal for us. Some people might get really bothered by these kinds of things, but we realize that when we are travelling, things are bound to happen and for 120 dollars a night, we had absolutely no complaints.

reviews.author: Adrien Becker
reviews.content: We've just come back home (in Montreal, Canada) from a three-night stay at Copley House, in Boston. This place is in a very nice sector of Boston, close to public transportation and all the major hotels and the business area. First of all, you should know that the pictures on the Copley House website are pretty misleading. Actually, theyâ€™re very misleading! We â€“ my wife and two kids â€“ had booked a one-room unit, which is supposed to be the most luxurious one they have. Ouch! If you donâ€™t mind the missing paint on the walls, the moldy smell, the dirty carpets, the so-so beds and sofa beds, and the slimy showers (just to name a few â€œfeaturesâ€�), go ahead and ask for unit 100 in the basement of the 239 West Newton Street building... right next to the laundry room!! That being said, when we saw our unit, we asked to be moved and were given two separate rooms for the first night (11 & 14-year-old kids weren't too happy about sleeping in a different room that their parents, but it was better that being in the basement...), we then had to go back to our smelly basement on the second night, and we were given a nice one-bedroom unit for our third and last night. Thatâ€™s a lot of moving around for such a short trip! We were in Boston with a few other people who stayed in another building (first floor of St. Stephen Street building), and their rooms were fine. I think Iâ€™d go back to the Copley House because of its affordable prices and its tremendous location, but I would ask for specific rooms, i.e. rooms 104 (which has been completely renovated and which is very nice) and room 109 (a one-bedroom unit) in the 239 West Newton Street building. I would also stay away from room 103 (and 100 of course) in this same building. While I wasnâ€™t too impressed with the Copley House, I must say that the staff were all VERY helpful, understanding and accommodating. I really appreciate what they did to make our stay more enjoyable. Finally, they gave me a substantial rebate, which was also greatly appreciated.

title: St Davids

description: Handy for the ferry and the bus station.
name: Caladh Inn

reviews.author: Miss Helmer Wisozk
reviews.content: If you are sound sensitive this is not the place for you, if you dont mind the noise its not a bad place, could do better , could do worrse. I checked in and asked for a quiet room was pleased to get an end room with a nice view, but it was right above very loud road construction and later had to endure very noisey drunks in bar on mezzanine right below me, I was told they would quiet down at 7pm, than 730 than maybe 930..was offered different rooms but all of the rooms had a very very noisey HVAC system that had a constant hummmm that was very annoying. I know from previous stays in nearby hotels the airplane noise is worse at other end Also was expecting a nice balcony but in reality it is only maybe 18" wide, just enough to stand there. The good: Very good front desk, especially the women on 2nd shift (Silver?) decent bathroom, good bed, nice view, quick shuttle to the strip, room was fresh and not too heavy on air freshener like some places. The bad: Road traffic noise, road construction noise, airplane noise, noisey hum in room from hvac, noisey bar patrons in atrium, food and service in restaurant need some improvement, plates for breakfast buffet dirty, fitness center disapointing, two long black hairs in bathroom sink that were not mine, slight cigarette odor coming from bathroom vent

reviews.author: Jordane Medhurst
reviews.content: We don't normally like to stay in Las Vegas but since it is half way to our destination we chose to stay there. We are not into the Las Vegas scene at all so wanted a hotel without a casino. We have 5 children and were looking for something affordable. We came across Embassy Suites on Priceline and for a family of seven it worked great. The room had a living room/sm. kitchenette area and then a separate bedroom. The room would sleep 6 and we put the baby in his own playpen and also had the staff bring up a portable single bed. The kids loved the pool and their favorite part (and mine) was the made to order breakfast in the morning that was included in the price of the room. That kind of breakfast would have easily cost us $40 at a restaurant. We were cozy in the place but it certainly worked for the one night we stayed and was clean and comfortable and the staff was helpful and the hotel was very nice. The kids loved the glass elevators as well.

reviews.author: Albina Kiehn
reviews.content: I was a little disappointed with this hotel. The rooms very outdated and look dirty. It's hard to tell if anything is clean as the decor is so dark. Our bedding had holes. No free WiFi, no flat screen tv's. It was okay for a night, but I would hate to spend a vacation at this hotel.

reviews.author: Geo Boehm
reviews.content: This hotel is off the strip and offers the sensitive traveler a quiet respite. Check in was impeccable and swift, the room was clean and comfortable. Breakfast was delicious. The only disappointment was my call to the Front Desk for more towels was either forgotten or ignored. The hotel is located behind the Wynn and it's about a mile walk to the Wynn entrance. There is a Las Vegas Monorail station a 5 minute walk away.

title: Stornoway

description: The furthest from the ferry.
name: Cabarfeidh Hotel

reviews.author: Aileen Blick
reviews.content: Enjoyed staying at this location off the Strip last year so decided to stay again this trip with our 25 year old son. Our suite on the 7th floor would have been a little cramped with our son sleeping on the sofa bed so we asked for a larger corner suite. No problem - we were given one on the 3rd floor. It was next to the restroom for the bar, but as the bar closes at 11pm it was never a problem. The staff at this hotel are very helpful, the breakfast buffet is excellent and sets you up until the evening.

reviews.author: Isaac Schoen
reviews.content: My wife and I stayed at this hotel from March 23-25 and enjoyed mostly everything about it. the location is great...not too far off of the strip. we rented a car for the weekend so it was not a problem to get to the strip and back. I would recommend renting a car versus taking the monorail or walking because the monorail is not that close to the hotel and parking is free all over the strip. The happy hour was fantastic and so was the breakfast. The only downside about the breakfast was the line got a little long..but it moved fairly fast. Plenty of choices and they kept bringing food and more food when it was getting low. The hot tub is huge! We didn't use the pool...so can't really comment on that. The rooms were big and the beds were comfortable. The only downside was our room smelt like smoke. It was a "non-smoking" room but clearly there was smoke in there. It didn't really bother us after a few mintues so we just stayed in the same room. Everything in the hotel was really clean and nice. I would say it was above average for the typical Embassy Suites. It was nice to be a little of the strip to receive a break from the lights, people, and casinos! I will definitely stay here again.

reviews.author: Jena Brakus DDS
reviews.content: I have to admit, I booked this little hotel for it's rate... But I will stay again and refer others because of it's location (within easy walking distance) from most major Istanbul sites. The kind and thorough attention we received from staff (my sister broke her ankle at the Hippodrone) and they went out of their way for her. Best part of all? Several wonderful restaurants that were fantastic respites for tired travelers and the kind neighbors... (if you're looking for a rug in Istanbul, just walk across the street...they had the finest and best priced rugs in Istanbul) plus? They ordered us dinner to be brought to the hotel when they heard my sister was injured that afternoon. That's more than kindness, that's family. I can't encourage you enough to stay Armagrandi Spina.

reviews.author: Antwon Metz
reviews.content: We stayed in this hotel for 5 nights. This lovley little hotel is close to all the major sites in the Sultanahmet district. The staff were pleasant, helpful and very knowledgable and accomodating. In particular, Serkan was always available to help. The view from the rooftop terrace is breathtaking in all directions. Rooms were clean and comfortable and the breakfast which is included was also very good.

reviews.author: Assunta Corwin
reviews.content: This hotel is quite literally in the middle of the Blue Mosque and the Haggia Sofia. Just stepping out through the back door, taking a few steps , and you are there! We stayed at the beginning of our 2-week stay and again for the final 2 days but in a different room. The first one was on the 1st floor and comfortable. It had some upkeep issues (peeling wall paper, missing molding) but the second time there, our room on the 2nd floor was better maintained (minus the broken shower head holder and less than sparkling white sheets). The breakfast was very tasty, offering a variety of cheeses, pastries, olives, eggs, breads, yogurt, breads, cereal. For a small fee, you could get fresh squeezed orange juice, too. As you return to the hotel after a day of touring, you are offered tea, coffee, or wine. I suggest having this outside your hotel at it would probably be just as expensive but with better ambiance. The staff was very helpful and pleasant, especially Suleman. He was very friendly, showing us the terrace, the tram system, and offering easy conversation. I would recommend this property for its location and value.

reviews.author: Estel Bechtelar
reviews.content: Hotel situated in a lovely, quiet street between the Blue Mosque and Hagia Sophia, perfect for travelers because you can walk to all major attractions. Rooms are very new and clean, and some of them directly overlooks the Blue Mosque. From the terrace you can see also the Bosphorus while you have breakfast. My experience in the hotel was very nice, excellent.

reviews.author: Bobbie Bergstrom
reviews.content: Lovely small cosy hotel in a great spot near to both the Blue Mosque and the Hagia Sophia; despite being very close to both these landmarks, the hotels location is extremely quite and peaceful. The Topkapi palace and tram station are also nearby. Our room was spacious and clean with excellent decor and the view from the rooftop terrace is absolutely stunning; there is also free wifi throughout the hotel. The staff spoke good english and were really helpful and polite.

reviews.author: Kassandra Haag
reviews.content: This location was perfect for 2 women traveling alone who wanted to spend their money elsewhere. The desk clerks spoke clear english are were most helpful with dinner reservations. The small tour buses were able to access the road and pick us up at the front door. This is how great the location was; we were within walking distance to the following-1 block from the Four Seasons Hotel; 1/2 bl from the Blue House(nice for an after dinner drink); 6 minutes to the tram- Balikci Sabahattin(phenomenal restaurant); 1 minute to the Blue Mosque, Sophia Haggis, Underground Cistern. At breakfast we looked out at the Blue Mosque and beautiful tulips planted in the center of the city. We were very comfortable walking around this area at night. There were slight inconveniences in changing rooms but the upside was that one night they moved us to a very nice suite. Request your rooms on the Blue Mosque side as there was a lot of noise (cat noise) on the front side.

title: Stornoway

description: The most central of all the hotels.
name: The County Hotel

reviews.author: Marilyne Reichel
reviews.content: i had a bad experience over there. Just feel myself being cheated. I had booked a room for 2 for through internet, and even from the preference coloumn i had mentioned i wanna 2 beds in a room. Guess what? whenever we reach there (which is about 10pm), they bring us in a room, which a standard size single bed, and claim that it is double bed, and that is a room for 2! i suspected they had rented out the actual double room to the walk in customers. In fact, i had been go through some of the review, and understand that the room is small, but i just couldnt understand that why they treat me like idiot and keep mentioning that this is HK standard size double bed!! we have no choice as that was the peak season of HK and i believe i could not locate another hotel in the new year eve. However, it spoilt my new year mood, and my 2009 was started in a bad experience! U might find it is difficult to get the hotel as it is not reachable by MTR. However, you really enjoy the local life of Hong Kees. With the crowded wet and dry market, fruit stalls, and food stalls, we did enjoy ourselves throughout our stay. Further, the bus station is 2 minute walking distance from the hotel, easily reach causeway bay, central through the bus. what i want to mean is, it is not easy to find the hotel, but easy to go central those places from the hotel.

title: Stornoway

description: Spacious detached property which sleeps 8 in comfort. Wales Tourist Board 3*. Children and pets are most welcome. Short breaks and longer stays available.
name: Gower Edge Self Catering

reviews.author: Kareem Schamberger
reviews.content: Stayed at the Comfort Inn from 18 - 21 Feb 2005. The advantages of this hotel are it's excellent location, it's a stone throw from Macy's and the Empire State was right next to our bedroom window. It is also only a 10 minute walk to Times Square. It has a nice bar next door called Brendan's where you can get the british footie results. However, on the negative, our room reaked of cigarette smoke, and even though we are both smokers it was unbearable. The hotel couldn't give us another room and despite them promising to elimate the odour and us purchasing air freshener, it did not go away. Also the receptionist Alex was abrupt to the point of being rude on some occasions, and the heating was roasting hot and very noisy. The breakfast was ok, just cereal, bagels, toast & doughnuts etc. But it's worth going to a diner for the real american breakfast experience. Try the Empire in Chelsea it's fab. I would recommend this hotel if you are on a budget but request a non-smoking room and hope that you get one as some people checked in when we were checking out and had requested this but ended up with our old room - poor them!

reviews.author: Neil Berge
reviews.content: We stayed for five nights in June 2004, encouraged by all the positive reviews the hotel had previously received. We were delighted to find those reviews were very accurate in respect of the excellent value for money, helpfulness of the staff and the close proximity to a lot of the main attractions. As a base for a sightseeing trip, we are sure it will be very hard to beat. Our room was clean and tidy, good sized and, being at the rear of the hotel, very quiet. The buffet breakfast was adequate enough, but we didn't choose it for the cuisine. As a budget hotel we would certainly recommend it to anyone visiting the city for a few days.

reviews.author: Hilda Prohaska
reviews.content: We had a one bedroom suite, spacious and modern. Nice view, nice interior and nice staff. Location ok, several restaurants and diners nearby, short distance to bus and subway.

reviews.author: Evie Kovacek
reviews.content: The staff is very helpful and nice. Always a smile and do you need anything if you approached the desk. You will not feel like you are staying in a hotel but like you live in NYC and this is your residence. We had a 3 bedroom 3 bath for X-mas week. The place was awesome with so much space because the bedrooms were big and the bathrooms. The best, you had a full kitchen and could make a breakfast before heading out which saves you money. The subway was a quick walk and its nice to get lost the best part and when you learn the routes you definitely feel like you live there. The Taxi rides were never over 20 (was holiday so a lot of traffic) and if you take the subway just take a Taxi back. Overall, if you want to experience NYC you don't need a fancy place because the time you spend in a room is only for sleep. However, this place is a clean, spacious, and attentive place that's inexpensive place to stay. Now, I would recommend a little TLC because it does show a little use the rooms like paint and new decor. Yet, for the time we were in the room it was nothing that bothered. Stay here if you want to experience living there, have a big group, and like space not the little hotel room.

reviews.author: Laverna McKenzie
reviews.content: If you are looking for a comfortable serviced apartment in a quieter area of Manhattan, this may be for you. The suites are large with well-equipped kitchens and a small balcony. For the size of the rooms, the price is pretty reasonable. The decor was a little faded, but the concierge is helpful and when you're in New York, you don't have to spend a lot of time indoors!

reviews.author: Arnaldo Blanda PhD
reviews.content: The brief to find accommodation suitable for 6 women for a week was proving difficult until we stumpbled across Marmara. 3 large bedrooms - we were willing to share with 2 king size beds and 2 singles - 3 bathrooms a great living area and fantastic 27th floor views. There was also a washer and dryer in the apartment which really made us feel at home. Some habits die hard! The location was fine with a good subway line close and with grocery and grog shops nearby we were set. The staff at reception were extremely helpful to us. They were happy to suggest places to shop, sightsee and eat. They also printed out some travel instructions to help us get to Brooklyn which made it easy and in general were accommodating of any request we made - thanks to all the staff who looked after us. It was great to have free WiFi although the connection was a little tempremental while we were there - not sure if this is usual. Would recommend Marmara to anyone who wanted to feel more at home than a hotel room can provide. Would also recommend Nicks Italian across the road - great food, great friendly service.

title: Swansea

description: Hurst Dene is located in the leafy suburb of Uplands just off Uplands Square on the main road to the heart of the Gower peninsula. They offer guest rooms and self-catering apartments at affordable prices.
name: Hurst Dene Guest House

reviews.author: Alvina Tremblay
reviews.content: We met a really serviceminded personnel, this is always a good start for a stay! Further on we got a really nice room - an appartment really - on 19th floor, and the view was spectacular! Walking south on 2nd Ave you find breakfast and dinner easily. Nearness of Central Park for fresh air, quick access to museums, and short way to Lexington Ave for shopping makes this hotel a really good starting point. If one doesn't want all the walking we did, getting on buses is no problem, and Subway is only some blocks away. We slept really well in comfortable beds. The kitchenette was well equipped - with fridge, freezer and cooking possibilities. Please note that we upgraded the room as we wanted to stay as high up as possible and this we find was well spent money. I really would recommend this hotel for other travellers when purpose is exploring NYC.

reviews.author: Wanda Mohr
reviews.content: We came to new york city for the holidays, and we stayed at The Marmara Manhattan and it was great. thank you for your hospitality. Special thanks to Mr.Mete ,Mr.Mehmet and all the other staff. We recommend everybody who would come to New York.

reviews.author: Randy Ferry
reviews.content: We had booked a studio at this apartment hotel and got a one bedroom suite. It was very roomy, clean and comftorable. There is alot of construction going on outside but that did not really bother us. It is probably as far north as you want to go but we did feel safe. There is an all night pizza place and a little grocery right across the street. It is just a short walk to Lexington where there are at least a million restaurants! You are close to bus and subway stops. On the subway you are not more than 15 minutes to most places including Times Square and the Theatre District. Otherwise you can walk to Central Park , alot ol the museums, restaurants and some shopping. The staff was very nice. All that said we will look for another location. It is a little out of the way and as I said earlier the location is not the best but, if you are looking for alot of room in a clean space this is great.

reviews.author: Seth Predovic
reviews.content: My husband and our 2 kids (1&2 yr olds) luckily used our credit card reward points to book a 3 night stay and paid for a 2 br upgrade and we are so happy with our pick. The room is spacious and clean and great for traveling with toddlers. The staff is extremely friendly and answered every question professionally. With every good thing there's always a few cons. The rooms are quite a bit outdated and in need of renovation (old old fixtures, door handles are loose and furnishings are different from the pics). The other think to be cautious of is if you're traveling with toddlers, there are alot of electrical wires from the printer and modem that are dangerous. But all in all, were happy with the space. Room to breathe!

reviews.author: Lurline Trantow
reviews.content: I strongly recommend the Marmara Manhattan. My husband was an in-patient at Mt. Sinai Hospital and we did not know the duration of his stay. I am a small town girl and intimidated by staying in New Your City by myself. The Marmara Manhattan became my haven. Nesli (and the others in reservations) are wonderful. They understand that surgical and medical stays are unpredictable in duration and very stressful. They provided us a great rate because my husband was in-patient at Mt. Sinai and were very flexible in scheduling. The hotel is very attractive, clean, roomy, and well maintained. It is unique, not your standard cookie cutter rooms. It is about a 20 minute walk to Mt. Sinai which I enjoyed taking. The suites are really attractive and even my teenage daughters were saying what I good job I had done finding it! In addition to the great rate, it has a full kitchen and a grocery around the corner. I cooked most meals there and was able to keep down the cost of my stay. What particularly struck me about the Marmara Manhattan is that everyone from reservations, to the front desk, to the doorman and bellhop, were friendly and helpful. This place understands customer service. Unfortunately we will not be coming back to the Marmara because my husband has chosen to change hospitals to Cleveland Clinic. When he is all fixed up and healthy again, my goal is to return to the Marmara for a few days with my family and relax and spend some time with them in the city. If you need to find a place while a family member is in one of the nearby hospitals, choose the Marmara Manhattan. I talked to other families who had chosen the Wales and the Marriot. They were not nearly as happy with their choices as I was with mine.

title: Swansea

address: Old Road, Ynysmeudwy, Pontardawe, Swansea SA8 4PL
description: 5 star Visit Wales cottages - each sleeps 6 - in quiet village location close to shops and amenities. Convenient for Gower, Mumbles, Brecon Beacons, Black Mountain. Dedicated bike storage and bike washing facilities - 20 mins to Afan Forest Mountain Bike Centre. Awards : Tripadvisor Certificate of Excellence 2014, Tourism Swansea Bay 2012 "Best Self Catering Accommodation".
name: Cwmshon Cottages

reviews.author: Daniela Frami
reviews.content: My wife, 4.5 yr old daughter and I stayed for 3 nights in a 14th floor, 1 BR standard suite @ $167 per night including taxes and fees. Pluses were the full sized kitchen, very roomy BR, nice bedding, pull-out couch, a good sized bath, free Wi-Fi, and overall cleanliness. Tons of storage space and the corner suite provided amazing views of the East River and NYC. The location was within pretty easy walking distance to museums, Central Park and subway stations. The furniture, including TV werenâ€™t new but they were very serviceable. On the down side, with all the windows and subway construction below, it was a bit noisy but youâ€™re in NYC after all. Also, the front desk wanted to charge us $35 per night to make up the sleeper couch but we pointed out that the reservation was clearly for 3 people and that there was no mention of the extra bedding charge when the reservation was made. They agreed to waive the charge without too much squabbling. Weâ€™ve stayed at other all-suite hotels in Manhattan and this was by far the best value of the bunch. Would highly recommend it and definitely stay there again.

reviews.author: Everett Waelchi
reviews.content: It was my first time at the Marmara Hotel. It was great like having an apartment in the city! Service was impeccable, rooms where clean and modern! Great place...

reviews.author: Audra Rempel
reviews.content: This is a great place to feel like home and most of the rooms are away from the NYC sirens and traffic noise - it's the best place to feel home away from home. Their is a kitchen with many gourmet markets near by for stocking up. Easy walking area and getting to the heart of NYC

reviews.author: Brooklyn Sauer
reviews.content: My parents and I love staying at the Phillips Club. We stay there almost everytime we go up. We usually take a 1 bedroom and I sleep on the couch. We like the fact that we don't step over each other in 1 room. Also we like the fact that there are two televisions and a kitchen. It helps especially in the mornings since we don't like big breakfast.

reviews.author: Elsie Kiehn
reviews.content: It is at good location near time square and close to subway. Price is also a good deal. Room is also clean. If I go to NY next time, i will choose to stay at Manhattan Broadway Hotel again.

reviews.author: Grady Little
reviews.content: The hotel service is excellent! Susie is a very nice person, and dedicated customers, have to admit! And the other staff were also committed to help with any questions or problems. Another great thing was the location point: very good! 3-4 blocks from Times Square! Close to everything! I did most things on foot. Now, points of improvement: cleaning the rooms. They were always dirty because the hotel never cleaned the floor. It had a lot of dirt, and hair from previous guests. The bed linen could also improve as comforters were old and very used. I found them too many hairs from other guests. We could pass a reform, it has many good things to offer. Overall I enjoyed staying there. It was a hotel used only to sleep. In short: excellent location, very friendly attendants and willing to help. But the room cleaning, linen, and conservation of the hotel were not good. If you are looking for a hotel with great location, just to sleep and with proper care, can stay there!

reviews.author: Emmanuel Ratke
reviews.content: I spent two nights in this hotel with my wife visiting friends in NY. This hotel was just fine for us. The room was rather small but the bed was big and confortable; same with the bathroom, and everything looked reasonable clean. What I liked the most is the location next to 8th avenue; it is very close to times square but not overwellmed by the turists crouds, and 8 and 9th avenues have more authentic NY restaurants and bars and better prices that the times square area. My room was not facing the street and in was very quiet. I was recomended by the hotel staff (by phone) to park at the Central parking structure at 40th between 7 and 8th. !!!Be prepared to take all your luggage and things from the car as soon as you pull over, since they will park your car for you and you can not access it untill you take the car away!!!. They charged me $60 for 47 hours with a boucher I was given at the hotel desk. We had breakfast at a chinese bakery next to the hotel with real NY people. The coffee and the pastries were surprisingly good.

title: Swansea

description: 2 self catering cottages,  sleeping 6 and 4-5 respectively.  Located in a very quiet hamlet, above the Swansea and Neath Valleys.  4* graded cottages, free Wi Fi, off road parking, cycle storage.  15 minutes from the M4 at Neath or Swansea.
directions: Easy access from the M4, Neath / Swansea
name: Tan yr Eglwys Cottages

reviews.author: Roel Konopelski
reviews.content: Upon most encounters with slovenly appearances, most would amend, fearing the thrifty and gaping caverns of dues to be paid. However, there is a crossing point: precisely where this slum seemed to have leaped off the pylons of great hotels, creating a tourist-friendly New York stay into paralytic asphyxiation of horror. It looms precariously on it's two-star rating. The distraught condition of drug predators and illegals cramming their holed guts into the trickling walls probably purchased the minimal rating. To this corroded stature of suckitude, I may ask to command you a simple trot away, scorchingly applying pressure to the gas pedal. First off, the "lobby" is a tight and small space... just like the stairway/room/elevator. Our room had no form of heating in the brutal cold of Manhattan. The bathroom door did not lock, "great". The bed was FILTHY!! STAINS! STAINS! HAIR ON THE BED! My goodness... there is no standards for this dump. The doors have stains... i don't know what it is? Mold? Feces? Basically, the room we had checked in online for about half a week was canceled the first hour we were there and the whole hour we were there was trying to book another hotel.

reviews.author: Aidan Kuhlman
reviews.content: Wow, the reviews are so bad, I feel like I need to stand up for this place. Look, it's not the Four Seasons, but for the price, it's really a decent place. We were close to everything, from sightseeing to shopping to dinning to the broadway shows. Rooms were small, but clean. The front desk agents there are super friendly and having wifi helped. So my friends and I had a good time and saved a bunch, so it was all good.

reviews.author: Manuel Hudson V
reviews.content: better to sleep on the street you do not have a lobby and extra charges for everything if been there once you will never come back there

reviews.author: Camden Durgan
reviews.content: I booked this hotel to be next to the place my girlfriend was interviewing at. We walked into the room and wanted to vomit. There were worn spots and stains on the sheets and urine staining (clearly from decades of men missing the toilet) on the bathroom floor, and a spongelike mold growing out of the "drain" of the "jet" tub. It was absolutely disgusting. AND...even though we walked in and walked right back out.....they would NOT refund our money. It was worth it to call hotels.com and find a great place at Broadway Plaza Hotel for only $10.00 more a night. I would stay very very far away. Bed bugs, urine, and who knows what other things lurk here. I've stayed in placed with cockroaches and ants crawling the walls that were better than this place.....

reviews.author: Dr. Kay Bednar
reviews.content: Finally I found somewhere I could write a review about this place to save others our pain. I see now on their website they have renovated somewhat. WE were NOT told at the time of our booking they were in the middle of renovations. Courtesy would at least grant that and give us the choice. Hopefully they have changed their ways but after reading latest reviews perhaps not. Towels were dirty, bathroom floor was dirty and room was dirty. I had to clean the bath before I could use it. Bed was hard, bedding disgusting. Glad it was a brief trip. They tried to put us in a room that had just been painted and the window didn't open at first. Then we asked for another room which had patches of carpet on the floor. Forget this hotel if you are light sleeper, tile floors line the hallways and suitcases rolling on the floors are noisy as is anyone walking by. We were on a tight budget and had to be in NYC that day. For around $170 at the time what a rip off!!!! I will go without food and save money to stay in a decent place and thankfully we have since found other hotels better quality for a cheaper price. Oh and yes there is no elevator and if they didn't have my credit card number I would have left on arrival after seeing the foyer!

reviews.author: Rita Jacobi
reviews.content: The other reviews scared me, but I already booked this place before I read them. I don't know about all the other rooms, but our room was pretty nice (not huge), but was very comfortable. I requested a room with two queen beds and not only got 2 queens, but two singles as well! Really cool! The T.V. was small and not very many channels, but hey, we weren't there to watch T.V.! Great location. Nice folks working there. If you go there, request room 309. That was ours. Not bad at all.

reviews.author: Dejuan Feil
reviews.content: Was expecting hotel to be poor if not terrible after reading reviews on trip advisor. Was not prepared for what we discovered. Nobody even heard of the hotel, bugs in the rooms, rooms not cleaned, leaking toilet, very noisy etc and the receptionist advised us we were getting the best room in the hotel. A joke ! Don`t know how they are even allowes keep this place opened. Awful !!!! We spent very little time in the hotel but still would not dream of reccomending it what so ever. Worst hotel I have ever come accross !!!!!!!!!!!! Don`t book it !!!

reviews.author: Rosemary Hessel
reviews.content: Our recent stay to this hotel was like going camping. Someone else booked this room for us. First of all we got there in the evening. We were not sure at first if we were in the right place because when the cab driver dropped us off we thought we were walking through the back door of a restaurant. We checked in took the elevator, which only held 3 small people to our room. The hall itself was so narrow two people had to take turns walking down them. Our room had no air on upon arrival, had to open the window to plug in the AC. In the room we had to take turns walking around because it was so small. We found smashed roaches on the wall, no soap, toilet lid, shampoo, no place to put toiletries in bathroom, had to ask for towels, looks to be like they had water leaks down the walls, had a dressing table but could not use it because the stool was between the table & bed and you could not pull out the stool. Make sure if you book here that your clothes are pressed unless you like ironing out in the hallway on attached to wall iron & board. NIGHTMARE!

reviews.author: Jesse Kessler
reviews.content: This hotel was the worst hotel I ever stayed in. The room was dull and cramped. The sheets were dirty and the walls stained. The staff entered our room while we were out shopping and moved us to another room. The packed our belongings in bags and moved us from two to one claiming there was a plumming problem but I demanded to see our old room to discover it was already let to new people. We had to call the police to sort the problem out he said it was a bad hotel and we should not have been there. Then on our last night I was confronted by a huge mouse in the lobby!!! The hotel manager was abusive and hung up the phone when we complained. Don't stay here. Lisa

title: Swansea

description: Hurst Dene is located in the leafy suburb of Uplands just off Uplands Square on the main road to the heart of the Gower peninsula. They offer guest rooms and self-catering apartments at affordable prices.
name: Hurst Dene Guest House

reviews.author: Celestine Keeling
reviews.content: We used Hotels to find a newyorkcity hotel. when we arrived it was like a bowery flop house! I had my children with me and we had to get two rooms and they werent even next to each other. There were broken bottles in the hall and pubic hairs in the bed. this was the broadwaymanhattan hotel. we were going to see a show and wanted to walk in the theater district. I couldnt stay there with my family, so we had to get another room at the hilton, which cost us 400. for the night, plus the 200 that was non refundable from the other place! We contacted Hotels that we booked through and they took no responsibility and wouldnt even discuss what we had found at this hotel that gets 2 stars on their site! Beware of the catchy Hotels commercials, we learned the hard way.

reviews.author: Mrs. Yolanda Emmerich
reviews.content: I would not stay here even if they pay me. The WORST hotel at which I've ever stayed. It's 10 times worse than what you can possibly imagine of a bad hotel. It's so very nasty. I couldn't stand it even with my eyes closed.

reviews.author: Mrs. Ellsworth VonRueden
reviews.content: My friend, her parents and I wanted to be able to go to New York and have a good time, but when we all saw this hotel, we knew what a dump it was. Just that the fact that there is a piece of paper taped to the door to tell you that this is a hotel should give you an idea about how bad it really is...No room, screws for sink handles, clogged bathtub drain. The TV didn't work, there was no VCR, you could hear everything that was going on in the rooms around you. The elevator smelled horrible and the curtains didn't even keep out the light. Lastly, there were no dressers, just hangers and hooks, that's it! Yes, the hotel IS located close to times square but is it worth it to stay somewhere that is totally disgusting just to be close to times square?

reviews.author: Ms. Thaddeus McDermott
reviews.content: I took my daughter and three of her friends here for a girls weekend. The room and bathroom were very clean and the staff was very helpful. The only problem (and to five females it was a big one) and surprise was that we saw several cockroaches!! I was very surprised as it all looked very clean. I think the attached restaraunt (a small chinese diner style place) is the culprit here. We all had trouble sleeping because of this, thank god we were only there for two nights and were not in the room except to sleep and shower. Ths day staff was great and we had plenty of heat once we asked for it. I have to say if it weren't for the bugs I would recommend this hotel but I will never go back, I hate bugs!!!!!

reviews.author: Ms. Jackson Stark
reviews.content: stayed for a week, older hotel, but clean rooms and very friendly staff, breakfast included in price and was very good. very good value for the money. staff was very helpful in getting our truck in the parkade, which was a close fit. beds were comfy. will definately be staying here again.

reviews.author: Dr. Hortense Ebert
reviews.content: We stayed at the Quality Inn for one night precruise. Our room was small but clean,and the beds were very comfortable with nice linens. Ice machines are on alternate floors. I would like to recognize Jacob at the front desk for providing excellent service. He gave us directions to the Aquabus to Granville Island,and also arranged a taxi at a specified time for our group to the cruise port. I see from other reviews that there were complaints about the restaurant in the hotel. We did not avail ourselves of the hotel restaurant. We ate dinner that night and breakfast the next morning at the White Spot restaurant,which is one block east of the Quality Inn(see review).

title: Swansea

description: Swansea University offers accommodation to the public during Summer and Easter holidays. They can offer a wide range of accommodation ranging from bed and breakfast non-ensuite single rooms through to self-catering apartments. They can accommodate large groups for events and conferences in the local area. Accommodation is available in Swansea University's Singleton Park campus set in beautiful parklands which is 5 minutes walk to the beach.
name: Swansea University

reviews.author: Gaetano Howe
reviews.content: My 11 year old daughter and I stayed here for two nights. Upon check-in, we were surprised to be upgraded to a king suite! Wow! We loved every minute...the hotel is nicely located a few blocks away from Granville Island (and a water taxi) and Granville Bridge...what a view! The pool was nice and refreshing after a long hot day, and the apple pie ala mode room service was sooo yummy! I also was thankful for the secure underground parking!

reviews.author: Willa Hoeger DVM
reviews.content: Our stay was nothing spectacular, but at the same time I don't have anything really bad to say. The beds were comfortable, there is a small pool, the front desk staff were nice, I found the area convenient...close to shopping, transit etc. The only bad experience was with the Restaurant server who i also believe was the manager. We had a visa/debit card and for those who have one would realize that if the company is not set up for visa debit- which they were not, it needs to be processed as a regular debit. Well no matter how hard we tried she insisted she needed to process it as a Visa. She would not listen. She insisted we were wrong, and she was right. This is our bank account, this is what we use day in and day out. She annoyed me beyond belief. Other then this situation we had a good stay.

reviews.author: Robin Gutkowski
reviews.content: I've stayed at this hotel in the past and it was one of my favorite hotels until this last trip. At check-in the desk clerk, Chris, was rude and embarrassed me in front of a group of people (there was a long line and check in was slow.) After he handed me the key to my room, I asked about breakfast and he informed me my room did not include breakfast. I explained that I had booked the "Stay and Eat" package and he informed me I did not. Then he said my room was only $89 a night and that if I wanted breakfast I could pay an additional $20 for it. I told him that I wasn't paying extra for something that was included in my package. Suffice to say, it was not the best start to my vacation. Chris told me if I could show him my reservation confirmation and PROVE TO HIM that I actually did book the package he'd give it to me...he even offered to allow me to use the business center FREE so I could get this information to him. After dropping off our bags I returned to get the key to the business center, but Chris was still busy checking in people (who looked at me like I was some sort of moron trying to get free stuff.) I asked a young woman behind the front desk if she could provide me with the key to the business center and explained that I needed to prove that I had booked the "Eat & Sleep" package. The young woman told me that they've had quite a few issues with the new reservation system and said that she didn't think it would be necessary for me to look up the reservation. She went to Chris and told him that she was just going to give me the breakfast coupons. He seemed quite annoyed with her, but didn't argue - which was good because at this point I was ready to check out and find a hotel where they wanted my business. The hotel accommodations are decent. The value fair. However, next time I go to Vancouver, this hotel will be off the list of options. It's kind of sad for me as I've stayed at this hotel probably more than ten times in the past and it had always been great. Must be new management or something. Chris was well dressed, but I sure hope he's not a manager - his people skills are horrific. I wonder if he's the person the other reviewers commented on. On the bright side, the hotel restaurant is great. The service for the morning breakfast was wonderful and the food yummy. Too bad the rude hotel clerk ruined the rest of the experience for me.

reviews.author: Julien Muller
reviews.content: We stayed at the Quality Inn at False Creek for a family weekend get-away. The hotel was very nice and was reasonably priced. We had breakfast one day in their restaurant and it was delicious. One of the neatest things about the location is that it is just a 3 minute walk from the Aquatic Center which is this absolutely gorgeous huge pool in this very nice neighborhood. They also had a pool for small children. Walking a few blocks towards the water and then going north takes you on a beautiful walk to Stanley Park, and going south takes you on an equally beautiful walk around False Creek. We took the Water Taxi to Granville Island, and while it's over in a blink of an eye, it's fun for little kids, as is Granville Island. On Davies street very near the hotel there are a lot of eating possibilities--tapas, French Bakery, Tim Horton's, Greek/Italian restaurant, etc.

reviews.author: Keeley Will
reviews.content: While checking in, a friendly staff member suggested a rear suite(for light sleepers) rather than facing the traffic bridge at the front. And while the 1 BR suite was spacious, the trade-off was punctual trash trucks picking up dumpsters at the stroke of 7AM the two days I was there. Their write-up promised both wireless AND wired high-speed Internet(complimentary); NOT having access to the latter, I experienced the utter failure of the former, that of a weak/non-existent wireless signal which is probably poached on their unsecured network making it impossible to work by computer except to write a novel. Their first suggestion?...bring my work down to the lobby where "the signal is guaranteed to be strong"; yes, I dragged it down there and indeed, it did find and connect to their network but signal strength was spotty and irregular.so it was frustratingly slow at best. Finally, there was no end solution after a call from the technical department, so I did the next best thing by giving up and going elsewhere.

reviews.author: Liliane Lockman
reviews.content: The reception desk staff offered great tips on nearby restaurants and were very courteous. The lobby was clean and comfortable as was our room. The bed was very comfortable and I appreciated the fan and the ability to control the room temperature easily. The breakfast at the restaurant adjacent to the lobby was healthy and delicious.

reviews.author: Dr. Fabian Hyatt
reviews.content: I am in in the "customer service" industry, myself and am very respectful of the people who carry out the jobs of delivering EXCELLENT customer service in whatever job it is that they do. When I travel I am very low profile. I make my own bed. I re-use the towels! The FRONT DESK staff were exceptional. They loaned me their stapler without the least hesitation! ( that can be a VERY big deal!) . They came up with a very suitable vase for my parrot tulips I picked up from a street vendor. The ice bucket was not doing them justice. I think "catering" was involved too. Thanks. I experienced a taxi driver dropping off a "found article" left in his cab the day before by an unknown lady who he had dropped off at the hotel. The front desk knew all about the incident and thanked the driver on the lady's behalf. Very gracious. Concierge Service. The room was large and pleasant. Great bed. Everything was just fine. All the TV channels! VANCOUVER is a great city. No matter which way you walk you'll find water. Turn "right" for FALSE CREEK or turn "left" and keep walking until you get to Burrard Inslet. Great location. Honest. It's a great little hotel.

reviews.author: Aryanna Turcotte
reviews.content: My wife and I stayed for 3 nights and found this hotel to be fairly priced for Vancouver (expensive city). Comfortable, good breakfast and very helpful staff. Would definitely stay again.

reviews.author: Angelina Beier
reviews.content: Hotel is in great location, just across the water from Granville Island. There's also a 7/11 and a little grocery store only one block from the hotel. The rooms were very nice for the price. I paid a little over $300 for a double for 4 nights.

title: Swansea

description: Located next to the Jersey Marine Tower which is the tall octagonal tower visible from the Fabian Way.  The tower itself is the hotel's premier suite and the top floor bedroom offers views of Swansea Bay.
name: The Towers Hotel and Spa

reviews.author: Monserrat Johns
reviews.content: I never stayed at the Hotel Riverview but live in the neighborhood. Believe all the negative reviews. This place is downright scary. There are drug addicts and transgender prostitutes that frequent here. I always feel sorry for the unknowing tourists I see arriving outside this hotel. STAY AWAY!

reviews.author: Alison Gutmann
reviews.content: Stayed at the Gild Hall last month and I was pleasantly surprised. I just moved from living in New York for 7 years so I am well aware that the financial district shuts down on the weekend but as a former New Yorker enjoyed the quiet streets and neat little finds for pubs and places to dine. It is also walking distance to Tribeca where you can find a little more night life. As for sleeping it was quiet and enjoyable. The staff was overly helpful in recommending places close by and gave us a room upgrade upon checking in (even having booked at a very discounted rate). If you are looking for the bright lights and touristy NYC don't stay here but if you want to enjoy a bit of New York off the beaten path then I highly recommend the Gild. Not to mention when the Monday rolled around the hotel was a buzz and you can't beat happy hour on Stone Street.

reviews.author: Ms. Dejuan Kautzer
reviews.content: My boyfriend and I both live in NYC and wanted to do a little "staycation" in the city. We found this hotel on a whim and booked it. We were SO pleasantly surprised. Leather tufted chairs, well-styled bookshelves, and beautiful objets adorned the very handsome lobby. A parquet staircase led to a gorgeous bar with a great ambiance. The room was immaculate and new - very comfortable bed and huge shower complete with Bigelow toiletries. We slept in, checked out an hour late and were not charged extra, the staff was super accommodating and friendly. All in all, a great value (probably the best value in NYC) for a stylish and modern hotel with great customer service.

reviews.author: Candido Ernser
reviews.content: Great Location walking distance to South Street Seaaport and the Seastreak Ferry to Atlantic Highlands NJ. Great rooms, clean,comfortable and great service and attention to detail.

title: Swansea Bay

description: Hotel just outside Swindon with fully equipped gym and 23 metre indoor swimming pool, as well as health and beauty spa. Special Spa Break from £75.00 per person for one night including three course dinner, full English breakfast and choice of beauty treatment.
directions: from Exit M4 (J15) and follow A419 to Cirencester, straight over roundabout, then take exit on left signposted Oxford (A420), turn right at next two roundabouts, stay on A420, cross the roundabout, pass the police station on left, pass the Esso garage on left, hotel is next turning on left, signposted to South Marston
name: Mercure South Marston Hotel

reviews.author: Lexus Jakubowski
