reviews.content: The hotel was well situated in the financial district. Staff was incredibly friendly and even the cleaning staff would greet you. The lobby was small but well appointed. Rooms were good although the glass door on the bathroom did not lend for privacy on a family trip. Hotel has 3 small cardio areas and a good reading room that serves as a bar on weekends. Rates appear to be steep but you can find good weekend rates. Close to South Street Seaport and other financial district tourist attractions, as well as Chinatown.

reviews.author: Nelle Hammes
reviews.content: The Gild Hall is really nice. Luxurious, comfortable, quiet, and close to the public transportation. The employees are very friendly and do their best to accommodate you in anyway possible. My room looked really nice, its had very interesting decor, check out the website to see what I am talking about. Its like a modern retro kind of feel, I can't explain it, but I loved it. My room had an iPod dock, bath robes, and all the fancy stuff hotels provide. The only issue I had was my room phone didn't work so I had to use my cell phone to make calls. Other than that my room was spectacular. My stay over all could've been better. I went to the Libertine Restaurant which is a part of Gild Hall and I wish I didn't. I called them every 10 minutes for about an hour before I planned on arriving and no one ever picked up the phone. When I finally went down I was told there was a 25min wait. Which I could've avoided if they picked up the phone. So after the 25min wait turned into 40min, I was upset and went for a walk. walking past the restaurant window I noticed there were three open tables. At this point I wanted to leave but my fiance insisted we stay; so we stayed. The manager seemed nice, but the waitress made us feel like she had better things to do with her time. The food was great though. I'm a sucker for good food, so I kinda forgot about the horrible service when I started eating. So to sum it up: Gild Hall is great stay, but beware of the Libertine.

reviews.author: Hermann Adams
reviews.content: Gild Hall really impressed when my girlfriend and I stayed there last month. The service was great, room was spacious and bed was super comfortable. This hotel is located in the heart of the financial district, but succeeded in making us feel like we were at home. It was convenient for all of the trains b/c they all basically converge on Wall St and Fulton St. Far and above better than a standard chain like the Hilton or Hyatt and a great deal, too. Highly recommended - we'll be staying there next time we're in NYC.

title: Swindon

description: Comfortable hotel just outside Tamworth town centre with Reuben's Restaurant & Bar.  Ideal for business guests with free wifi and easy access to motorway network.  Very family friendly with excellent value packages including entry to Drayton Manor & Thomas Land, Conkers, Twycross Zoo and National Space Centre.
name: Ramada Tamworth

reviews.author: Lera Stoltenberg I
reviews.content: I want to commend Hotel Le Marais on their hospitality, competence, reliability, efficiency and attentiveness regarding our hotel stay. From the beginning of our booking process earlier this year to the final checkout I have been very pleased with all stages and personnel. Shawn was excellent booking my room and giving me the room I requested. He was always cheerful and anxious to help The next day after we checked in, we overslept for breakfast and we came down to the front desk and explained that we have missed breakfast this morning and asked to the young lady who was working if we could get some fruit and yogurt. As fast as she could she ran to the kitchen and brought us oranges, apples, yogurt and amazingly she also included muffins, sausage patties with English muffins, milk and orange juice. Seriouslyâ€¦this is SERVICE!!! The type of service you donâ€™t find everywhere. She went above and beyond our expectations and if I remembered correctly her name was Daphneey. The room was clean and nice, with everything you could possibly need. The bar was awesome with candles lighting up in every table. Shawn and Alex at the bar were amazing. The heated outdoor pool was relaxing. My wife and I were really impressed with the overall appearance of the hotel, the staff and especially the comfort of the beds. Thank you Hotel Le Marais, your immediate staff, the front desk staff, to the housekeeping departmentâ€”each person made my wife and I feel welcomed, cared about and treated like a friend. We will definitely comeback again and again!!!!!

reviews.author: Isai Johns
reviews.content: This hotel is newly renovated. It looks great today. They cut corners in renovation, for example, they didn't replace the elevator which is painfully slow. They used cheap doors and you can hear right through them. While waiting for an elevator we could clearly hear a shower in one room and a whoopie session in another. The complimentary breakfast is lame. A few boxes of cereal and bagels laid out in the bar, not a service person to be seen. That said, the bed was great, free wifi is appreciated,location is great and quiet. The rooms are pretty, small but nice.

reviews.author: Athena Feil
reviews.content: I recently had the pleasure of staying at the newest French Quarter property, Hotel Le Marais. While still undergoing the final touches of a massive renovation, this is a beautiful little gem right off of Bourbon Street. Upon arriving, parking can be a little tricky, as with all of the boutique hotels in the quarter. But valet was great. Lobby was small but very efficient, with the hotel lounge overlooking a stunningly beautiful courtyard, complete with a small pool. The rooms were very nice and stylish,. The beds were incredibly comfortable. LOVED the step in shower. Although no tub, the shower was great! And, even though you are less than a block off of Bourbon street, I couldn't hear any of the noise. This property is a real asset to the French Quarter and I would highly recommend it whether your going to the city for business or pleasure. Can't wait to stay again!!

reviews.author: Georgianna Nitzsche
reviews.content: I would highly recommend this hotel. The room was great, very modern, comfortable bed, and very nice and clean room and bathroom. The restaurant and bar are amazing. They have a few tables with beer taps at the table very cool. The bar is very modern and well stocked, if Abby is your bartender then your in for a treat, she is the best. Great staff and service. I stayed with my uncle and his friend booked the room and he did not know I was coming so when we asked for a room with two beds they had nothing available so they took some $$ of our bill and gave us two money vouchers towards the bar or restaurant. Great location a few blocks from bourbon street so you don't get all the noisy rift raft at night, and walking distance to Jackson square and the Frenchman. If Acme has a line 30 deep which it usually does go across the street to Felix's its better and is where the locals go, huge fresh oysters the best I have ever had. Enjoy the devils play ground I did.

reviews.author: Doyle Trantow
reviews.content: Recently stayed there for a night. It was my first trip to New Orleans, and the staff (especially Helbert) had great recommendations for food and entertainment. They were incredibly nice. Parking was cheapish and on-site, so I just drove right up to the hotel and valet-parked. The room was what you'd expect from a W: stylish, comfortable bed, nice bathroom. There is some construction going on at the hotel, which is sort of annoying, but it was not a problem on my floor. There's a great pool as well.

reviews.author: Princess Reichert
reviews.content: I had a pretty nice stay for three nights at the W under renovation in the French Quarter. Great location, nice staff, service variable, but OK, and I am fussy. Was in a new room. The good news is that unlike most W's there was enough light for my aging eyes. The bad, the new decor is really terrible. Why didnt they keep it simple instead of painting the walls orange with an eyesore of a design as the focal point of the room and the ugliest carpet I have ever seen. Could have been amazing, now certainly comfortable, and the good part is you close your eyes at night and dont have to look up at the scary design above you. I'd stay again, but sorry for the poor designer.

reviews.author: Maia Wehner
reviews.content: Love this place. The construction is a pain, but should be wrapped by summer. The staff was so over the top nice and helpful it made up for any jack hammers. Especially ask for Halbert and Daniel. The two guys were super cool and couldn't be more helpful. Southern hospitality at its finest. Ya'll.

reviews.author: Joannie Effertz MD
reviews.content: The staff at this hotel was the friendliest and most helpful of any hotel we've ever stayed in. Since there is currently construction going on at this W, it is difficult to give a fair rating. As SPG members we expected a better room. The only available room was small and there wasn't even a comfortable chair in it. But at least it was at the rear of the total away from the construction noise and jackhammers. A stay at this W will probably be better after the construction is completed and, hopefully, the rooms are upgraded a bit. The extremely friendly and accommodating staff and great location in the French Quarter are reason enough for us to return to the W on our next visit (after renovations are completed).

reviews.author: Arlie Leannon
reviews.content: We just stayed at the W New Orleans French Quarter. We had a very unfortunate experience with our room being located close to construction taking place in the hotel. The staff at the hotel was extremely attentive and did their very best to make things right for us. I can't say enough about the concierge Halbert. Truly a stand-out in service. Recommend verifying up front if construction is still taking place and if so doing what you can to ensure you are not going to be affected by it. Don't expect a fancy W - this hotel is older and going through remodel - but do expect excellent service. Some of the nicest people we met in NOLA - a place where everyone is friendly and nice.

title: Tamworth (England)

description: A hostel run by the Gatliff Hebridean Hostels Trust in the remote village of Rhenigidale, which is 6 miles from Tarbert on foot, or 13 miles by road. The road has only been there since 1990 and the only way in used to be on foot or by boat. The hostel does not take bookings, and has no phone.
name: Rhenigidale Youth Hostel

reviews.author: Garett Balistreri
reviews.content: We stayed at the Hard Rock Hotel for two nights in February. The hotel was great. The rooms were nicely decorated and the beds were quite comfortable. There was a stocked refrigerator in the room. However, the prices of everything was outrageous. Needless to say, we didn't touch anything in the refrigerator. A bottle of water was $7.00 plus a 20% surcharge and 6.5% tax. The pool was beautiful, it had a nice waterslide. The water wasn't very deep. The deepest part of the pool was 4ft 6in. We stayed at the hotel for the fass passes and early access to Harry Potter. It was definitely worth it. Harry Potter reached maximum capacity by noon and with the fast passes we never had to wait to get on the rides. The location can't be beat if your going to the parks.

reviews.author: Ebony Balistreri
reviews.content: Before booking our trip to Universal Orlando, I read a lot of reviews on TripAdvisor - thanks to those who take the time to post. Some were favorable, others not. With two teenage boys in tow, we opted for the Hard Rock Hotel. Our room was ready when we checked in (around 2pm) - clean and all in order. No problems with housekeeping during our stay. No problems with noise (we had a "garden view" room not facing the pool). Ate at The Kitchen for breakfast each day. A bit pricey but typical for resort restaurants. Food and service were good. Very easy walk to Citywalk and the two parks. Using your room key as Express Pass is the BEST benefit. We did not do the early AM entry to Harry Potter. Too many people do that so the lines wind up being long. During the regular hours we never waiting more than 30 mins. Priority seating at restaurants never was useful. Being able to charge to your room key is handy - especially when teens are on their own and need to purchase food. But watch out for limits as your cards get cut off if you exceed them. You need to work out limits with the front desk. Many restaurants in Citywalk give AAA discount so always ask. We used the Mears Shuttle from the airport. For a family I would not recommend it. Mears puts too many people in a van and makes too many stops. For a few bucks more, opt for the taxi.

reviews.author: Mr. Taurean Schneider
reviews.content: Traveled here Jan 14th for 3 nights. Doubt we will make It to three. So expensive - worse customer service ever. Jonathan at the front desk was helpful, Paul with room service and a handful of others. This has been a nightmare. Room by elevators - listened to dinging of elevator all night. New room reeked of smoke and febreez in the smoke free hotel , not so good for a child with allergies. Jonathan was as genorous as he could be. After getting room service- it took 4 people over thirty minutes to get us a wine tool for the $70 bottle we had ordered. The food was freezing cold once it did arrive. When we called "star service", they repeatedly answered and hung up - or sent it to voicemail. Save your money. I wish I had. I have had better customer service at a gas station. Perhaps hiring the cute young girls is backfiring........

reviews.author: Delbert Conroy
reviews.content: Just got back from a wonderful birthday weekend at the Hard Rock! We had a basic room but were upgraded to one(b-day amenity??) with a great view of the pool , lush landscaping , and the twinkling lights of the Universal rides in the distance. Everyone on staff had a smile and a helpful attitude! We enjoyed food and drinks at the Velvet Bar,breakfast at The Kitchen, and drinks at the pool. The location was perfect to get to the Universal parks and it was a short drive from the airport. I think that families and romantic couples or just a bunch of friends would all have a wonderful stay in this hotel!! I highly recommend it!

reviews.author: Patience Mohr
reviews.content: average hotel don't phone home on the hotel phone. we paid $408 for 6 short phone calls to the uk.

reviews.author: Mr. Ulises Ankunding
reviews.content: We stayed in a Kids Suite at the Hard Rock Hotel for a week this summer, and we loved everything about our stay. The room was perfect for our family of 4. Our girls loved not only having their own room, but not having to share a bed with each other (they each had a twin bed). They also loved the pool slide. While others have complained about noise, we didn't notice any noise. The location cannot be beat - a short 5 minute walk to Universal Studios and CityWalk. And having front of the line passes for Universal was awesome. We can't wait to return!

reviews.author: Emelia Monahan
reviews.content: This was our second trip to the Hard Rock Orlando & if possible it was even better than the first. The hotel itself is stunning, immaculate & contains something for everyone - young & old, the music piping throughout all common areas adds a modern yet unintrusive touch. The staff could not have been more accomadating & friendly, from the bar staff to the cleaners passing in the corridors at all times of the day. Checking in & out was particularly straight forward, as was getting taxis from the front of the hotel. The rooms were cleans, spacious & comfortable. The location in relation to the parks & City Walk along with the free express passes are undoubtable perks to staying here & add to the already incredible holiday experience.

title: Tarbert (Harris)

description: Based on the Esplanade overlooking South Beach. A few minutes walk from the walled town of Tenby. 60 rooms (Standard, Premier and Deluxe). Restaurant and 'The Cwtch' Bar. Small car park at rear of the hotel.
name: Giltar Hotel
title: Tenby

description: This place offers well-equipped rooms, many with lovely views over the old fishing harbour and across Carmarthen Bay. It's part of a Listed Georgian terrace, built over 175 years ago as individual summer houses. A lift runs from the first half landing and there are footpaths directly to the beach.
name: Fourcroft Hotel

reviews.author: Mrs. Noemy Cummerata
reviews.content: just got back from Pier House. Stayed in Lanai room...the beds were heaven. Loved the beach area, pool was too warm during the day but great at night and open 24H. Location was great walked everywhere. Took the new CityView Trolley and Fury for catamaran ride. Loved walking the boardwalk along the ocean. Great stay at the Peir House and would stay there always the beach was such a plus ! Went to South Beach to watch the great 4th of July Fireworks too

reviews.author: Mathilde Marks
reviews.content: My boyfriend and I stayed here for 3 nights, which was way too short. The hotel was perfect! extremely clean and well maintained, great food, a beautiful beach (which was a pleasant surprise being i was prepared for the "lack of great beaches on key west" as I was told) but it gave me my "fix" when i wanted to lay out. Ironically we found we only layed on our beach for 2 hours during the entire 3 days as we explored all the streets of key west. there's so much to see and so much to do. I owe a great thanks to all the wonderful people on tripadvisor, as the suggestions on things to do and see was spot on. We loved our bartender Brian who sadly is moving back home. he helped us a lot. I highly recommend renting the bicycles...it's a good way to explore the town and burn off the calories from the wine the night before! few key points: great small clean beach and clean beautiful water hotel provides computer to check-in online and print boarding pass service was EXTREMELY nice always greeting you hotel was VERY clean... location is PERFECT..steps from mallory square/sunset festival/ (Roof top cafe is great to eat at) VERY QUIET despite being on top of Duval street. I AM A LIGHT SLEEPER and I swear they must have installed sound proof glass! Enjoy all key west has to offer .....I underestimated how much fun it would be

reviews.author: Dr. Titus Boehm
reviews.content: I would not recommend the room with the spiral staircase to the bedroom upstairs. The staff were friendly. The food was good. I would reccommend eating at Blue Heaven and having the Lobster Benedict. It was nice to look at all the boats going by. The location is where its at! Walk to everything! The cost of this hotel should be in question though. The pool is cold, and there isn't a beach. The deck is small. Safe and nice all in all.

title: Tenby

description: Celtic Haven is a family-run holiday cottage resort on the picturesque Pembrokeshire cliff tops near Tenby. Many of the pretty whitewashed cottages date right back to the 12th Century and on-site facilities include an Elemis spa, Waves cliff-top restaurant, a headland golf course and leisure club with an indoor pool. The Pembrokeshire Coast Path is a short stroll away and many of the cottages are pet friendly.
directions: Located on the A4139 between Tenby and Manorbier
name: Celtic Haven Resort & Spa

reviews.author: Shakira Welch
reviews.content: If you are going to stay at the Pier House you must stay in one of their spa rooms. They are in a seperate building where the spa is on the first floor. All of these rooms have recently been redone. They are large and spacious, they have wood floors which I love and they have huge luxurious bathrooms. We love the veranda/balcony - sitting out there and drinking coffee and just relaxing is the best. The Pier House is centrally located - walking distance to everything. The staff is always very friendly and helpful.

reviews.author: Blake Okuneva
reviews.content: Excellent hotel. Would definitely stay here again. As far as beaches go in the Keys, theirs was excellent. Great location right on the water and on Duval Street. I would highly recommend this hotel.

reviews.author: Jodie Hudson
reviews.content: Can you get any closer to Mallory Square? Can you get any closer to the beach? No... Pier House has great location for sure. The staff was super friendly and helpful. Our room was decorated in the region's style. Fun street signs marked the pathways between the different buildings and destinations. The drinks were a little expensive, but it's a resort and expected. Hard floors were perfect for getting sand in the room and lush plants were perfect in creating the island feel. Definitely a safe place to stay, too.

reviews.author: Ms. Brandyn Berge
reviews.content: We stayed in a harbor-view room with sailboats outside the patio. It was kind of other-worldly when I was awakened in the middle of the night by a dog on one sailboat barking at a cat on another sailboat. I've told that story quite a few times since. We also thought it was interesting that so many of the descendants of Hemingway's six-toed cats can be found around the property as we strolled around it. The location was also close to Mallory Square and much of the nightlife.

reviews.author: Hank Streich
reviews.content: We stayed here with 3 other couples for three nights, our first time in Key West. The hotel was beautifully decorated, & great bathrooms. A nice, small beach & pool, & an outstanding location. Right off Mallory Square, & most of the popular bars & restaurants. We all agreed we'd stay here again if we ever return to Key West.

reviews.author: Myles Lind
reviews.content: After a long beautiful drive from Miami, what a great place to settle down for a week...We loved our choice. The Pier House is in a perfect location. Once we got checked into our room, the only bad thing I can say is we didn't get a king bed like we requested. The front desk tried to accomodate us but we were fine with our 2 double beds. We were just happy to be away and in the sun and feel the Key West vibe. The rooms were clean and very comfortable. The private beach is fabulous, nice sand and a great place to hang out and relax. The pool is clean and open 24 hours. Make sure to take a mid night swim! We loved to finish off our nights at the hotels little bar "The Chart Room" we met great people. Make sure to meet Captain Dan. He took great care of us all week. Made fresh popcorn and made excellent drinks. We learned alot about the locals at this little bar....This vacation was filled with great memories and this hotel is where we would definately come back and stay. You cant get a better location. We didn't have a car the whole week and we didn't need one. Get ready to walk, or rent a bike which is a great experience. Loved It!!!!

reviews.author: Pansy Bahringer
reviews.content: Fantastic accommodation, clean & well appointed rooms. Centrally located with lovely pool & beach. Would return in a heartbeat. . . enjoy if you go!

reviews.author: Leatha Howe
reviews.content: Stay at the Hyatt next door...cleaner, bigger rooms, ELEVATOR and great staff! It's worth an extra $$ a night. Main building has two floors. If you are on the second floor and you anticipate use of a cooler, stroller, etc. during your stay good luck! We found out the hard way - lugging a stroller up and down stairs for 3 days. First mistake was not to use the bellman, not knowing an elevator did not exist we figured it should be easy enough to get our belongings to our room. Apparently that was a snub to the bellman as he was very rude to us the remainder of our stay. More than once we nearly took a spill down the stairs. However, the night crew seemed to outshine the day crew as the night crew was very nice and hospitable. Room was VERY small and had, what appeared to be ants. They had made an effort to update, but only went part way so their efforts seemed more like a poor attempt to cover up obvious deficiencies in the building rather than upgrading to "Resort-Like" atmosphere (new baseboards were already falling off the walls). I wont even get into the 2 dead roaches which were in the downstairs hallway for the last two days of our stay. Overall - Great beach (when construction is not going on), Rude Day Staff, Insects, Small Rooms, No Elevator and a poor attempt at upgrading

title: Tenby

description: Guest rooms and suites with complimentary hot breakfast, WiFi, and parking. Pool and fitness center are also provided.
name: Hampton Inn & Suites Thousand Oaks, CA

reviews.author: Maurine Rau
reviews.content: nice hotel, helpful staff, good price. I have stayed here several times and have always enjoyed the staff and hotel room. I will say the price usually determines where I will stay in New York because I visit about every other month, for a short stay.

reviews.author: Lilian Heathcote
reviews.content: My girlfriend and I just spent 3 nights at 4 days in New York City. The location of this hotel was more than we could have asked for. We ate at many excellent restaurants in the area, including the crooked knife across the street. The desk let us check in many hours early and leave our bags for many hours after checkout. Our room was on the 12th (top) floor and had a great view of the Empire State Building and midtown. Unlike previous reviewers, we had no indication of any smoke near our room. My girl said that on her trip to the lone, overworked ice machine on the 10th floor, she encountered a thick cigarette smoke smell, however. Unfortunately for us, the lobby was still under renovation. It is sure to be impressive when it is done. We will return to Hotel 3030 and certainly recommend it.

title: Thousand Oaks

description: 5 rooms and one 3-bedroom, 3-bath home.
name: Sequoia River Dance Bed & Breakfast

reviews.author: Cletus Huel
reviews.content: We stayed at Hotel Thirty Thirty for three nights in august 2010 and we enjoyed it a lot. The room was tiny but enough for us. The staff was really friendly and the concierge gave us very good help with tickets and tips. The location is great, close to Empire State Building. Only negative thing is that I sent an e-mail to the hotel in advance, and I had to send another three emails to get them to answer. From my first mail to their answer it took about 2 months.

reviews.author: Lucious Purdy
reviews.content: Fantastic Location and room was very comfortable. I arrived late at night and was greeted warmly. The room I had was very spacious and modern and the bed very very comfortable. The hotel is situated close to buses and underground, could not have asked for a better spot . Proved to be excellent value for money. When I return to NY I will return here. Something to improve: provide free internet. It was a hefty 13.95 for 24hours....Starbucks down the road is free if you buy a coffee.!

reviews.author: Helen Ryan
reviews.content: Service sucked. Our room did not get cleaned. When we called down for fresh towels we never got them. We were promised a queen size bed and they gave us a full size bed. We were also disappointed that the room lacked basic things such as a cup to drink water out of. Location was good but other than that it was not worth the price.

reviews.author: Ebony Reichert
reviews.content: This was my first stay at Hotel Thirty Thirty. I had a wonderful experience. Incredible staff, great room, perfect location, and a great price. I will stay here again and will recommend the hotel to friends and coworkers. Thank you!

reviews.author: Marguerite Altenwerth
reviews.content: As I was travelling with my 75year old mother we had booked a twin room, when we arrived we were 'upgraded' to a 1 bedroom & living area with a couch, I was told sleep on couch or a roller bed could be brought in! Corridor carpets were covered in plastic which made a noise when walked on, builders were in rooms with doors open sawing, drilling & creating dust that got everywhere. I spoke to another guest who was being moved to another hotel & was told by woman receptionist that I had spoilt that guests experience of the hotel. I asked to speak to the manager at this point & was told that she was the manager. We decided to find another hotel that was not a building site, could accomodate our needs & allow us to speak to other guests! The two reception staff we spoke to were unhelpful, churlish & belligerent not the customer service we were told to expect in New York. The bell boy was the most helpful pleasant person we could find at this hotel & we wish him luck.

title: Three Rivers

description: Tents, caravans and campervans welcome. Facilities include toilets, showers, indoor kitchen and dining area, and wifi.
name: Balinoe Campsite

reviews.author: Dejon Johnson
reviews.content: Location and views are very good, staff very helpful. However, a total lack of response to a personal request let's the place down, disappointing.

reviews.author: Sydney Kohler
reviews.content: I've never asked to change rooms before but did so when shown our first room. It had an fireplace that was poorly ventilated. I knew the smell would probably keep me up all night, so I asked for a different room; had same issue. Finally settled for a room w/out fireplace which was ok. However room still outdated. Lastly it was difficult to locate key ice machine. Overall it was difficult to navigate the resort.

reviews.author: Christa Hoppe
reviews.content: Everything at the resort was first class. Close to many wineries. A beautiful property with a great setting. Didn't play golf. The course has a great reputation. Enjoy a trip there.

reviews.author: Jaunita Krajcik
reviews.content: Excellent customer / guest service. Arrived for a four day stay for a conference looking forward to swimming every day in what had been described as an excellent 25 meter outdoor lap pool only to learn that there would be an extra daily fee to use that pool, per person, on top of the resort fee. I was unhappy about that and let the front desk know of my disappointment. Liz Accardo, the Front Desk Manager offered to waive that fee for us for the duration of the stay: no fuss or argument. Ms. Accordo made our stay! Besides that the one bedroom suite with kitchen, wood burning fireplace, was excellent (if a bit outdated), and clean. Housekeeping was great. We had a great stay. Went wine tasting at the many local winerys. I recommend this Resort and would stay again.

reviews.author: Miss Joshuah Bogisich
reviews.content: We spent our anniversary on this excellent property. Our suite was beautiful with an awesome view of the golf course. The staff was very friendly and the management gave us a bottle of champagne for our anniversary. What a wonderful surprise...

reviews.author: Tatyana Jacobi
reviews.content: Most important, I HIGHLY recommend getting a preferred room. I did and I still thought the walk to the bus stop and the main building was too long. I usually stay at one of the Deluxe hotels but this time I tried to save some money. Was it as nice as the Beach Club or grand floridian NO WAY! Was it 2 to 3 times cheap, YES! The room was clean but a little worn, it could use some updating. The food at the restaurant was pretty good but the food court was awful aside from the ice cream. Overall not great, not overly "magical", but reasonably priced for the location.

reviews.author: Mrs. Mack Braun
reviews.content: Maybe we are spoiled - maybe we are jaded, but after staying at a variety of Disney on-site properties we have to declare this one to be the least interesting. It is a bit of a flop on a variety of levels. First, they appear to install their "trainees" at the front desk - at least this was our experience. Then the place was under construction. Then the room was a long distance away. The room was clean and functional - but nothing more than one would find at a budget motel. A Hampton Inn, typically charging $150 a night in most cities beats this hands down. So we checked in at midnight and thankfully our main reservation was at the Beach Club...so we checked out at 8 AM. We couldn't get out fast enough. The one saving grace - the doorman was a terrific character in a lovely outfit. Go over there and get a picture taken with him - but don't stay there!

title: Tiree

description: Main St, Tobermory, Isle of Mull. Hotel on the seafront, near the pier. B&B from £30. Bar is popular with locals and visiting yachtsmen.
name: The Mishnish Hotel
title: Tobermory (Scotland)

description: Comfortable family run hotel with spectacular views and superb food produced from best local produce.
directions: On the waterfront near the distillery
name: The Tobermory Hotel

reviews.author: Trisha Roberts DDS
reviews.content: I've read other reviews where people seem unhappy with this resort. I found it perfect. I called 10 days before my arrival and got the exact room I'd hoped to get. I was upstairs on the corner. I had two windows, one faced the pool the other faced the river. I was in Oak Manor near the bridge that is closest to the main facility. One night on the way back from Magic Kingdom we had just missed the bus to the Riverside resort, so we decided to take the bus to French Quarter and walk the path over. We weren't halfway there when a security guy picked us up in his golf cart and dropped us at the bridge that goes straight to our building. This trip was during the holiday season and the resort was decorated beautifully. I would definitely stay at this resort again. I highly recommend it to families. The food court was great. The prices were high, but you expect that at Disney. Although we did order a pizza at the food court to take back to the room and it only cost about 15.00. And that fed us all. We flew so we were sort of at the mercy of Disney prices as we didn't have a car to go off property. I would definitely recommend having a car if at all possible. We had a fridge in the room so if I'd had a car I could have gone to Walmart for lunch meat. But whatever, it was fun. The hotel was great. Again, I would recommend this resort.

reviews.author: Mary Conroy
reviews.content: There are two types of themed residential areas in this resort. The â€œAlligator bayou.â€� area has smaller accommodation blocks and an informal feel and atmosphere. The other region (called Magnolia Bend) is an impressive and formal deep south, old grand mansion, look and feel area. There is a (0.9 mile) walkway / cycle path which forms a loop around and across the Sassagoula river which runs through the center of the resort. The pathway has a link to through to the French Quarter resort. The path affords great views of the resort as you wander, jog or cycle around it. Depending on which accommodation you get you may get very familiar with the walkway as you trail back and forward to the food court. Aside from the theming the rooms are identical. The Alligator bayou rooms have (fake) log bed frames which are really easy to stub your toes on. (yep I speak from experience there.) The rooms are slightly bigger than an All Star Resort room and have a refrigerator and coffee making facilities. Other than that they are the same basic layout with the door at the front and the bathroom (with no window) at the rear. The room can be a little dark if the lights are switched off. (Why would you be in the room during the day anyway?) The air conditioning is a through the wall unit rather than a central type and it can be a bit noisy if you leave it on. (Itâ€™s Florida, you will probably leave it on.) There are some good swimming pools with the relaxed â€œOlâ€™ Man Islandâ€� pool having a water slide. All Pools at Disney are heated so you can swim all year round. Food court. The resorts reception, bars shop and restaurants are located in the â€œSassagoula Steamboat Companyâ€� building. There is service restaurant (Boatwrightâ€™s) and a general dining area (Riverside Mill) with a reasonable choice of food. Both are nicely themed. There is also a bar which serves snack food in the main building and a bar poolside on Olâ€™ Man Island. The shop has a limited choice of essential items and the usual large choice of Disney items. This is a nice calm and relaxed resort. It is a more grown up resort than All Star for not excessively more money. The grounds and general ambiance is superb and this makes the resort feel like it is a higher standard than the moderate grade it is afforded. I would not recommend this as a first choice for families with young children as it isnâ€™t quite as â€œDisneyfiedâ€� as other resorts. If you want a similar standard that is a little more kid entertaining go next door to French Quarter.

reviews.author: Lenny Mills
reviews.content: This is the second time that we have stayed at Riverside and were not disappointed. This time we stayed in the Alligator Bayou rooms-which are exellant, and have a rustic feel; I liked these better than the Mansion rooms. The beds were very comfortable. The food court has many choices, one of my favorite is the Mickey waffle with strawberries. The gift shop is also great! One feature that keeps us coming to Port Orleans is their boat service to Downtown Disney. This is such a relaxing ride, and much better than taking the bus. It is also a short walk over to French Quarter. On evening we walked over to French Quarter and had a drink at their lounge (highly recommended is the Tropical Ginger Lemonade [I think that is the name]) and relaxed while looking at the Christmas decorations. The only bad part about the building our room was in is that there was no elevator in that building (some buildings have them and some don't). Overall I was very happy with our stay and highly recommend both Riverside and French Quarter.

title: Tobermory (Scotland)

description: Classic highland hotel (built in 1883) on the hill above Tobermory. Rooms from £49 to £169.
name: Western Isles Hotel
title: Tobermory (Scotland)

description: Ukiah California Hotel, Discovery Inn offering comfortable and affordable accommodations located in the heart of Mendocino Wine Country.
name: Discovery Inn Ukiah

reviews.author: Deion Boehm Sr.
reviews.content: It is one of my favourite hotel. Staff are very friendly and helpful. I have stayed there for 2 times. Although it is not located in city centre, shuttle bus is available to Shatin Town Centre and Tsim Sha Tsui. I also highly recommend Sha Tin 18. After you try the suckling Peking Duck, it just melts in your mouth.

reviews.author: Lue Wuckert
reviews.content: We brought our son to HK to celebrate his 4 yr old b'day. We chose to stay at Hyatt, Shatin mainly because of its Kids Club. Booked for 3 consecutive nights (Hyatt's website) and we were given an upgrade to a 1 bdrm executive deluxe. We loved the bedroom so much that we didn't want to go anywhere else. It's large and has the view of the mountains, waterfall and the constant MTR plying in front of us (minus the noise). We only left the hotel twice for an early lunch and some shopping at Shatin shopping center (2 MTR stops away). The rest of the time we spent in the room watching free in-house movies. Our stay was made extra special when my son was given a complimentary birthday cake (large chunks of fruits) which was so yummy!

reviews.author: Emmett Bode
reviews.content: The Hyatt Regency Sha Tin is located outside the city, its at least 20 mins away from Hong Kong. But at the same time it is very accessible as it is right next to the metro & bus station. You can take a bus, or a cab, or take the more convenient metro to the city. There is even a free shuttle to the other Hyatt located in the shopping district of Tsim Sha Tsui in downtown Hong Kong. The hotel itself is well built, modern & sophisticated. It seemed almost new when I stayed there so I dont know how old it is, but everything was very modern, well kept & clean. The rooms are large, very well made & up to the Hyatt standards. The food is good as well, & I dont know if it seemed reasonably priced to me because of the value of the Hong Kong Dollar or because it was actually cheap compared to other hotels? You be the judge & try it out yourself. Great hotel, great stay, but...is it worth staying so far away from the city? Is it worth spending up to 30 mins on the metro to reach any of the sights & attractions? I guess it depends on how much money you are willing to spend on a hotel. The hotels in the city are not cheap, & compared to the Hyatt Sha Tin are a lot more expensive even if its a three or four star hotel. So it pretty much depends on how you want to spend your money I guess. Spend less on a hotel & more time commuting to & from the city sights & attractions, or spend more on a hotel & no time commuting by staying in the city. There is a Hyatt right in the city centre, a lot more expensive though. You decide.

reviews.author: Mr. Sadie Donnelly
reviews.content: I'm a business traveler and I spend a considerable amount of time in hotels across the world. I am come to truly value the distinct experience I feel when I stay at Hyatt hotels. Everything you would expect from a Hyatt - you won't be disappointed! I was impressed with the hotel and especially the staff. They were all very friendly and professional.

reviews.author: Vallie Friesen
reviews.content: We stayed here for a business conference, it was amazing... Had the water front view... Room #1129...amazing... A bit far away from central & tst... But is definitely the best hotel in shatin

reviews.author: Aditya Hessel V
reviews.content: I have stayed at this hotel last year. It has not changed. What ever your needs, they seem to excell. The staff is trained and professional. Young proffessional staff is including the door men to the lady who puts your nightly treat in your room! I recommend this Hotel highly. Close to University MTZ, just acouple stops from Sha Tin shopping. Nice pool with a great excerise room. Oh, don't forget the breakfast buffet. Close to the Sha Tin Racecourse.

reviews.author: Sandrine Feest
reviews.content: Very nice hotel, great rooms and facilities. It has a great gym and swimming pool. However they seem to try and charge you for absolutely everything. You would think that a chain as large as hyatt, with it's room rates, would include free or very cheap wifi but it is extortionate. And the business centre charges quite a bit to use the printer and for paper.

reviews.author: Lonzo Conroy
reviews.content: I spent three nights at the Hyatt Regency Hong Kong Sha Tin hotel during a recent business trip. The hotel is very nice, with large, well designed rooms and comfortable beds. My room had a great view over the river. The bathroom had a walk-in shower and a separate bath. The breakfast buffet had a large variety of food, and the quality was excellent. Unfortunately, dinner off the menu in the Cafe was not so great. The dinner buffet may have been better. The rooms have both wired and wireless internet access, which worked well, but was an extra charge. I don't like this policy, but it is common in mid to high end hotels. (Lower cost hotels do not see the need to charge extra for Internet access, so this charge is more of an opportunity for the hotel than a necessity.) I was there only for business, so I cannot comment on how far the hotel may be from downtown Hong Kong.

reviews.author: Florencio Corwin
reviews.content: Very low end version of the Hyatt properties. Its ok for the price but rooms are small and its far away from the city. Staff was not willing to upgrade despite being a Hyatt Platinum member (whats irking is that he didnt even check availability until I insisted). Water views are ok, but that depends on how well you haggle for the room with view. Don't expect alot...

title: Ukiah

description: The only hotel in Venice Beach located on the boardwalk on Ocean Front Walk and offering views of the Santa Monica Bay. All rooms have been recently renovated.
directions: on Ocean Front Walk btwn Speedway Ave.
name: The Cadillac Hotel

reviews.author: Selmer Ryan
reviews.content: We were driving through the area and thought that Calistoga would be a nice place to stop for one night. The Roman Spa is a decent place to stay but is not a resort by any stretch of the imagination. It's an old establishment and shows it, but generally is comfortable. The rooms are updated, but the air conditioning unit is dismal. It was impossible to find a good setting during the night, it was either too cold, but when you turned it up a bit, you woke up sweating. Lots of older couples there which I thought was endearing. The baths are quite old and the tiles are fading badly, but that didn't seem to bother anyone. The reception and service seems to be an afterthought for those who work there. With the exception of a nice young lady, they would just let you stand at the counter indefinitely as they walked back and forth doing "their work". It's okay for one night, but I didn't feel it lived up to it's description on the website.

title: Venice (California)

description: Newly launched full service boutique hotel about 200 feet from the ocean in the heart of Venice Beach. Rooftop lounge called High with incredible panoramic views of the ocean and City of LA. Hotel has spacious rooms and 2 room suites, ideal for families. Many rooms have beautiful ocean views. Hotel has gated indoor parking.
name: Hotel Erwin

reviews.author: Destiny Nicolas
reviews.content: April 11, 2008 Sue Duvall Rossi We should be in Kauai right now. Yes, we are part of history, Airline history. April 7th to 14th in a free condo and ATA Airlines went under. So, we thought of Calistoga and the Roman Spa. The Roman Spa is the only place we ever stay, coming almost every year when we can. We love the proximity to Main St. and all the restuarants and shopping. We absoutly love the lush and beautiful gardens the pools and piece and Quite. Highly Suggest you come and Enjoy, Sue Duvall Rossi

title: Venice (California)

description: Located one block from the Venice Beach Boardwalk, adjacent to the world's largest man-made yacht marina. Has direct online reservations and special packages.
name: The Inn at Venice Beach

reviews.author: Delphine Batz
reviews.content: Roman Spa is funky and comfortable; the spa and pool are warm and inviting. Love the fact that the Oasis is right across the parking lot. A great place to veg with your girlfriends!!!

reviews.author: Ms. Katherine Nader
reviews.content: The Roman spa in Calistoga, is a paradise of flowers, humming birds, fountains, and mineral pools. We return here year after year anticipating the relaxed and rejuvinated sensations that overcome us during our visits. The pools have varing degrees of temperatures, you can find your bliss in anyone or all of them. The service is superb, with easy acess to extra towels, and friendly desk service. The location is perfect, just steps away from main street, and its great eateries. The tranquil atmospher is really pleasing with the beatiful grounds, flowers, fountains, and Palm trees, I think the hummingbirds are slow to migrate because they refuse to leave this oasis. We love the Roman Spa and plan our return when ever we can.

reviews.author: Deonte Cole
reviews.content: Paid 300.00 a night for a tired "family suite", only to find it was a one bedroom room with a wallbed in the main living room. Kitchen is small, and the room is older in look and furnishings. Pool and spas are stained but ok, but get this - we took our two year old into the pool area only to be reprimanded and told that it was a "law" that we couldn't have him in the pool. Funny - we've stayed in other hotels in Calistoga and NEVER had that problem. I believe it was most likely an insurance issue. Stay away...We enjoy our stays in another very nice Calistoga property as we go up there frequently, and the only reason we took a chance on this place was that it was booked. In the future, we'll make sure it's available..!!! (If I could give ZERO stars as a review, I would)

reviews.author: Selina Wilkinson
reviews.content: My huband and I just recently returned from a peaceful and relaxing extended weekend at the Roman Spa Hot Springs in Calistoga. We return to this heavenly resort every year in February or March to have a weekend to rest and enjoy the beautiful surrounding of the Roman Spa. Not only is the heated pool and indoor Jacuzzi used, but the peaceful and beautiful grounds at the Roman Spa are something we look forward to visiting. The flowers are beautiful. We have some friends who join us on this wonderful weekend and on the grounds they have available picnic tables, along with BBQ's to use. This year they have added a gas BBQ and it was great! We met our friends, who were also staying at the Roman Spa, for dinner out at the picnic tables and really enjoyed ourselves. We also love the friendly visitors and staff at the Roman Spa and we have made this a tradition for years to come.

reviews.author: Misael Miller
reviews.content: Do you remember the "Calgon, take me away," commercials? This is like - Roman Spa take me away! So nice to dip into the hot mineral pool and let go of the cares of this world. Relaxing atmosphere, always friendly and helpful staff. This was our 5th time here in the last 13 years and we will be back sooner than later. Walking distance to excellent food. The rooms are basic, but clean, the grounds are well kept. Enjoyed a massage at the Oasis as well. Good times!

reviews.author: Icie Willms
reviews.content: Roman Spa is tucked away one from down town Calistoga. Quietly located across from a historical building, it is conveniently located to shops, restaurants, a market, art galleries, and book stores. At night it is quiet. The gardens at the Spa are beautifully tended. Many waterfalls or fountains created a peaceful and serene atmosphere. The soaking and swimming pools are small but I never felt crowded. Three pools offer temperatures from warm to hot with the jacuzzi being the hottest of the three. It is wonderful to sit outside in the sun. Deck chairs and recliners are located throughout the Spa grounds for relaxing. A picnic and Bar-B-Que area is equipped with Weber stoves and the items necessary to have a fun outdoor dinner. At night the pools are softly lit and the night sky, midnight blue when we visited, is filled with stars. Coffee is organic Thanksgiving coffee sustainably grown. Instead of those tedius little pots in each room, you can walk to the office and enjoy as much coffee as you like. Our room did not have a kitchenette but did have a refrigerator. We enjoyed lunch and breakfast (fruits and salads) during the day time at the Spa but ate dinner in town. The staff is friendly and our maid spoke both English and Spanish. She was very helpful when we asked her to make up a couch into a day bed. We love the Roman Spa. This is our 15th year of visiting the Spa. I would recommend the Roman Spa to my friends.

reviews.author: Allie Leuschke
reviews.content: We were greeted warmly and had an early check in. The rooms are super clean and comfortable. The pool is small but nicely landscaped to feel like an "oasis". The water temperture was perfect. The best feature is how close the hotel is to the center of town- just a few steps away to our favorite restaurant, Wappo Grill, and the wonderful coffee shop, museum and park. Makes it a super pleasant and easy get-away for a night in Calistoga.

title: Venice (California)

description: Private and shared rooms, housekeeping apartments, all with free internet.
name: Venice Beach Hotel & Hostel

reviews.author: Domenick Bayer
reviews.content: First, I'd like to advise readers that the words "spa" and "resort" are freely bandied around in relation to the motels in Calistoga, and somehow I missed that when researching the Roman Spa Hot Springs Resort. (The word "motel" is on their sign, seen if you go directly to their site online.) This is an important distinction that I overlooked - a Motel as opposed to a Hotel - and this evidences itself in terms of austerity in accomodations. All the glowing reviews on this site caused me to abandon a more comprehensive research, so I'd like to give a very thorough review so people can make up their minds with a variety of info. I was hoping for a hot springs soak, and a rejuvenating stay at this "resort". I left feeling very tired and discouraged. The pros are that indeed, the staff is friendly, the grounds and rooms are clean, and the springs are used to full advantage, whether you rent a private whirlpool room as I did, or wish to avail yourself to the pool or hot tub outside. The cons of the place? I was a bit unhappy to detect the scent of chlorine in the outside pool, thinking I would be getting the same unadulterated hot spring soak as I could get in my room. It would have been easier to revel in a body of water that is "pure" hot springs water, rather than swimming in something with chemicals in it. But the water was nice, the moon was full, and I continued to try to get into the spirit of my retreat. Back in my room, my partner and I excitedly tried to use our new laptop for the first time...he had bid on an auction item online that was due to close. (I admit that not asking the Roman Spa Motel whether or not they had wireless internet service is my own fault, but since I've seen the rankest little motels advertising it, I erroneously assumed they would have it.) We went to the office to see if there was a complimentary PC for guests, but this was not the case either. I was also able to let this detail go, and my partner and I slipped into the whirlpool in our room. This was a nice feature, hot, pure sulpher-smelling water filled the nicely clean tub...but I was disappointed that the tub wasn't just a bit deeper. My partner and I are small people, so if you're a big guy, be advised that in a sitting position, your shoulders will be way above the water line. Scooching down into the tub, we found it difficult to find a comfortable position and hung the back of our necks on the squared edge of the tub. Romance was not to be....We retired to a hard mattress, and closed the curtains that didn't block out the light from outside to our satisfaction. During the night, we finally surrendered and shut off the window-heater-conditioner unit that vibrated and clanked every time it came on...so I woke up cold the next morning. Huddling under the blankets to attempt the last couple hours of precious rest, I was disturbed by the sounds of maids using the laundry next to my room, and the distinct sounds of another guest in an adjoining room, stirring something in a cup and speaking. I was amazed that the walls were so thin! Getting up with sore hips from the hard mattress, I searched the room in vain for a coffee maker...another amenity I guess I've been taking for granted. I guess in short, even if my destination has some charm and the draw of natural features, if I can't get a good night's rest, I won't be inclined to return. Hope this review helps someone's decision-making.

reviews.author: Ms. Kathlyn Rau
reviews.content: Calistoga Nov. 8 & 9th, 2006 This was our second visit, having stayed only one night last year. Very relaxing experience. Enjoyed all of the pools and the other guests. Grounds were very clean. The room was very clean, but the bed was not comfortable and the pillows were too hard. This will not deter us from coming back. Staff was very friendly. Looking forward to our third visit.

title: Venice (California)

description: An affordable hostel with a central location
directions: located on Windward btwn Pacific Avenue and Speedway
name: Venice Beach Cotel
title: Venice (California)

description: Venice Beach Suites & Hotel offers fully furnished vacation/corporate suites in the heart of Venice Beach.
name: Venice Beach Suites and Hotel

reviews.author: Avery Mills
reviews.content: We had a great experience at Roman Spa Hot Springs. Convenient location, comfortable room, and "warm hot springs spa". Took advantage of the Oasis Spa "mud bath" and loved it.

reviews.author: Joannie Ebert
reviews.content: The Roman Spa is a favorite. I have gone to the Roman Spa several times for a romantic weekend. The lush foliage gives the Roman Spa a tropical peaceful ambiance. It is especially beautiful during the holidays. I have also visited the Roman Spa Mother's Day weekend with my mother and sister. The staff was so accomodating. My sister had broken her leg a couple of weeks earlier and the weekend proved to be a bit much for her. The Roman Spa provided a wheel chair, not only for getting around the resort, but for getting to dinner and around town as well. I've even taken my young niece and nephew, who are preteens, to the Roman Spa for an unforgettable weekend. They loved the warm pools. Great restaurants and shopping are all close by. Calistoga is a fun little getaway and the Roman Spa is a special place to enjoy it.

reviews.author: Rachel Carter
reviews.content: I read the (mostly negative) reviews before I stayed at this hotel, and decided to try it anyway to save some money. I was just in town one night to see a band and I was by myself. Hotel was recently updated and is in decent shape. Hotel staff was friendly. Room was small, but bathroom was decent size. The beds aren't as bad as some people have stated but are by no means great. The main problem with this hotel is that the trains constantly run and it's LOUD. I was awoken repeatedly - it sounds and feels like an earthquake. I am normally not someone who gets up at every little sound. I'm guess I would stay here again for one night if I was on a budget, but if you are trying to have a relaxing time, consider whether you can afford a few extra bucks to stay somewhere without the train commotion.

reviews.author: Idell Osinski
reviews.content: I'll tell you what..Nice location.close to La Zona Rosa(relatively speaking) and a great value..Staff was courtious friendly and spoke English well...Will go back this year hopefully!

reviews.author: Ricky Bashirian
reviews.content: Great find the staff were very helpful and gave us very good recommendations where to eat and I must we were'nt disappointed. The room was well appointed and the bed was very comfy. I must say the general manager was great and very professional. Would deffo be back.

reviews.author: Melany Murazik
reviews.content: Hotel is great, staff is friendly and helpful. You certainly get your value for money, whether you book online or directly with the hotel. Rooms are very cosy (see photos), new furniture and most importantly, hotel is very, very clean. All the staff is very friendly and at your disposal, from waiters, reception staff to manager Serpil. After our four days stay, we have decided this is going to be "our Istanbul hotel" that we will be coming back to whenever there. Location is perfect, just off the main street which makes it less noisy and enables you to sleep, yet just few steps away from the main happening. Breakfast is nice, buffet type and you can additionally order anything you want. The option of pick up at the airport if you are staying more than 3 nights is very nice and it was comforting to see the sign with your name at a busy airport in Istanbul. Hotel is very near Taksim square (5min walk) where you can get the metro, bus, taxi to go to other parts of the city. Really enjoyed this stay and will hopefully be going there soon again.

title: Venice (California)

description: Ocean front fully furnished vacation suites on Venice Boardwalk. Beautiful brick building has been recently remodeled retaining classic Venice Beach charm but with chic design and a variety of amenities. Full kitchens, bathrooms with rain showers, walnut floors, free WiFi, cable TV, parking and spectacular roof deck with BBQ and panoramic views across Los Angeles. Nightly, weekly, monthly rates available.
directions: Located on the boardwalk, facing the beach
name: Venice Breeze Suites
title: Venice (California)

description: Four rooms, each with its own decor, are available.  No pets and children are not recommended.
name: Volcano Union Inn

reviews.author: Jed McDermott
reviews.content: Loved it and everything about it! Am planning to return soon! Amazing service, lush rooms with views to die for! Beautiful poor area and great bar staff.

reviews.author: Dianna Pfannerstill
reviews.content: Part of a Southwest Airlines four day package. Chose the Vdara because it was new, totally non-smoking, no casino and in the middle of everything. Got a free upgrade to a Panorama Room - windows on three sides. Only negative - it was on the fifth floor. Room was great - large kitchen, living room and bedroom. Electric curtains and electric room blackout shades on all windows. Very quite and housekeeping was excellent. Had a small cafeteria style restaurant in the lobby. I picked up breakfast each morning and we ate in our room. Short walk to the Bellagio on a private walkway from our lobby. Also same access to the overhead tram that stops in the Aria, City Center and Monte Carlo. Two trams running - wait always less than six minutes.

reviews.author: Miss Taylor Gutmann
reviews.content: I love going to Vegas, but hate the constant smell of smoke at night so this was a perfect fit for us. The room was upgraded for free to the belagio fountains view. the beds, shower, and set up was just amazing. They do not have a place to eat late at night though so prepare for that. Also its not actually on the strip you walk through the belagio to get to the strip which was fine for us

reviews.author: Anthony Harris
reviews.content: I have been to Las Vegas twenty-three times on business. This is my favorite hotel and I'll tell you why - no casino and no smoking! You walk in the front door, pass the beautiful reception desk in the lobby and head right to the elevator. No walking a mile through a smoky casino to get to the elevator to your room. This hotel, originally planned as luxury condos, I believe, is beautifully appointed with comfortable modern furnishings. The unit was extremely clean, the bed was wonderfully comfortable, and the bathroom was luxurious with a large glass shower and separate tub. Each suite has a small kitchen. If you ask at check-in, you may get a room with a view of the Bellagio fountain! We did! Even though Vdara is not directly on the strip, it's a short walk to the Bellagio. Not an inconvenience at all. I will definitely stay here next time!

reviews.author: Corbin Crist
reviews.content: First of all, being charged a $20 "resort fee" is a rip-off serious enough for me to take away one star. They jack up the daily room rate by this fee supposedly for internet access, local & toll-free phone calls, access to the Fitness Center, a daily newspaper, two bottles of water, and turndown service on request. A decent hotel would include internet access and turndown service on request in the regular room rate - which is not low; with cellphones, who needs free calls; the newspaper is at the front desk, not delivered to the door, and can be grabbed by anybody coming off the street. If a guest wishes to use the Fitness Center, he/she should be able to opt to pay or not. On general principles, I refuse to return to any hotel which engages in this abhorent rip-off. If more travelers would stop patronizing these places, maybe the hotels would stop doing it. However, if you don't mind being ripped off $20 per day, here are the pros and cons: Pros: Being in a completely non-smoking hotel is wonderful. Also, I liked being able to go to our room without going through a casino. The location is good; easy access to Bellagio and from there to the Strip. We had a 50th-floor room with a fantastic view. The room is divided into bed and living area. It's spacious, and the bathroom wonderful, with a huge tub and lots of space. The hotel is very clean, and the hotel staff were all helpful, friendly and courteous. Big kudos to them; they are the best feature of this hotel! Cons: There's a kitchen, but you have to beg for plates, cutlery and pots & pans because nothing is in the cupboards (which is annoying). Worse, they don't have a coffee maker -- they wouldn't even bring one up for me. No coffee maker??? Even a Holiday Inn will have a coffee maker in the room! Supposedly the pricier rooms have coffee makers, but this lack almost convinced me give the place two stars instead of three (the staff kept that third star). They'll bring you a robe, but don't bother; we saw people wearing them to/from the pool. The robes are flimsy and cheap and you'll look like an inmate in a psychiatric hospital.

title: Volcano (California)

description: Located in Uptown Whittier.
name: Radisson Hotel - Whittier

reviews.author: Marques Kuvalis
reviews.content: We just returned from 4 days at the resort and feel like we have been gone for 10. The hotel was packed when we were there, however it is so spread out that we never felt the crowds. What I love about this place is the variety of things to do. Each day was different. The kids loved the water park. I loved taking the ferry to the beach. During the day there is plenty to do for everyone. We stayed at the marina this time and our room was spacious and had the same decor as the last stay. Great sleep. Loved the addition of free wifi. It worked great. The magic show was really great and the kids loved the games set up for vacation week. The teen lounge was fun for them. I thought that I would mind taking the Funicular everywhere, however it did not bother me at all. We had three great dinners at the hotel. The Strip house has the best salad, Blossoms was a great family style chinese/sushi meal. The italian restaurant food was fabulous ( service was a little slow). Our most favorite place to eat was the pizza/salad spot just off the lobby overlooking the pool. The setting of the hotel is spectacular. It reminded us of Hawaii. The hotel is older so don't expect it to be "perfect". I'll take that "aged, casual feel" anytime, versus a new hotel in a setting that is less spectacular. We are already trying to figure out when we can go back. Kudos to the entire team at the hotel for making the stay so enjoyable. We made great family memories. We had 3 other families at the hotel due to our "talking up" the resort. They all loved it too.

reviews.author: Dr. Khalil Oberbrunner
reviews.content: The two of us spent 3 days followon to Caribbean cruise at El Conquistador, where we planned to experience Puerto Rico's rain forest and bioluminescent bay. After debarking from the ship, we taxied to the airport for rental car, and headed east for some fun in the sun. The trip to Fajardo was effortless, and when we arrived at the hotel (earlier than checkin time) the valet told us the wait to check in might take awhile, because of the line of people checking out. We thought "no problem, we'll just hang out and explore the grounds until the line subsides". We did stop at the lobby anyway, and saw that there was no line at the HHonors check in counter, so we stopped and asked if we could check in early. The staff were very helpful and courteous, even though the line of people waiting to check out extended way past the lobby. I hadn't been in contact with the news services for several days, so I didn't realize what was happening. Hurricane Earl was imminently approaching the island, and this hotel at the eastern tip of Puerto Rico was directly in the predicted path. To make a long story short, the three days my wife and I spent celebrating our 41st anniversary were both scary and wonderful at the same time. The hotel staff did a great job keeping us comfortable through some of the worst weather we have ever experienced. Needless to say, all services and visitor facilities on the Island were shut down for most of that time, power outages were frequent, and our plans were totally ruined. We stuck it out though, and my wife and I got to spend some quality time together doing abolutely nothing but watching the weather. We couldn't be happier with the facilities at the hotel that kept at least minimal guest services running, Who could imagine that this would turn out to be such a memorable event doing absolutely nothing? We hope to return to the island and to this resort again in the near future to visit all the things we missed out on. But we have no regrets for the time we spent there in this beautiful, wild and wet paradise.

reviews.author: Danyka Raynor
reviews.content: We spent a couple of days at this beautiful resort. The Resort Manager was extremely helpful in order for us to book the right room-rate-location, thank you so much! The facilities are very well maintained, the room was very clean and perfectly located next to "Coqui waterpark". Food at Stingrays, Iguanas and Room Service was very good too. The short boat trip to Palomino Island went a very long way - Palomino is just beautiful and peaceful, yet very interesting for our 7 yrs. old, he really had a blast and we are so glad that we came to El Conquistador since this short time was meant to spend some family quality time - mission accomplished - Thank you Conqui!

reviews.author: Queenie Miller
reviews.content: Just got back from 4 days at El Conquistador. It was an interesting experience in comfortable mediocrity. Everything was fine. Rooms were nice, People were friendly enough. Food was decent. Nothing was notable though. Renting a car was really the key to enjoying the place in my opinion. You don't have to ever leave the hotel compound. We rented the car after arriving to visit the nearby rain forest and just being able to see a little more of real life around the area felt like being released from house arrest. Old San Juan was pretty long drive but it was well worth it.

reviews.author: Kian Wunsch
reviews.content: After months of online research, I finalized our vacation plans choosing Hilton's El Conquistador in Fajardo, Peurto Rico. It was gorgeous! The staff was the friendliness and most helpful we have ever encountered! We spent six beautiful days there and can't wait to return. The pools, golf course, and restaurants were of the highest quality. The views are spectacular and our teenage boys never complained about being bored! I thank all of you who waited on us, talked with us, and gave us the dream vaction of a lifetime (I wish I remembered all your names). I am so grateful to Asst. Hotel Manager, Mr. Manny Melendez, for answering all of my questions and being so patient with me when booking the trip. It was amazing!

reviews.author: Earnestine Balistreri III
reviews.content: We traveled last Christmas with a large extended family - ages 5 to 69. This was a perfect destination. The hotel has a separate island which is reachable by a short ride on the hotel ferry. At the Palamino Island site there is plenty of shade, a beachside restaurant, volleyball, and water toys for rent. The beach is wide and not crowded. The whole family went for the day and was sorry when it was time to take the ferry back to the hotel. There is also an entire water park with various slides and a lazy river feature. This provided another whole day of fun for the entire family. There is a charge for entrance to this water park, but it was a nice way to vary the days. If you do not want to pay extra for the water park, there are plenty of beautiful swimming pools available. We also used the tennis facility and loved it. Our rooms were very clean and comfortable. We went on 2 "outings" while there. The first was the rain forest for hiking. The second was a night-time canoe trip to the luminescent pool. Both were relatively close by and a nice family outing. The night-time canoe triip might be too late for the very young. The food choices/restaurants offered great variety. We expeciallhy enjoyed the teppan-style dining where the chef entertained us all with his knife skills! I would definitely recommend this hotel for a family destination!

reviews.author: Ezekiel Kertzmann
reviews.content: Beautiful view, we got out upgrades. Breakfast is excellent, a lot of fruits.. Staffs are very polite and friendly.. Great trip!

title: Whittier

description: Offering an AAA 2-Diamond garden hotel in the heart of Whittier.There are jacuzzi suites and free Wi-Fi.
name: Lambert Inn - Whittier

reviews.author: Kylie Beatty
reviews.content: The views surrounding this resort are simply amazing. I've never seen more beautiful surrounding in my life and I've traveled a lot. And if this is all you care about, then go for it. However, restaurants (and everything else) in this resort is redicuolosly overpriced. The small bottle of water goes for $3.50, two eggs breakfast costs $17 and small glass of orange juice is another $3.50. Me and my 10years old easily spent $500 on food in 5 days and we normally would share appetizer and one main dish and never order any drinks besides juice or water. They charge $20 per person for their own water park that consists of three water slides and lazy river. This is per day, not per stay. Service is very poor. The first thing you hear from a waiter is a reminder that tip is %15 and not included. Waterpark closes at 6pm, however at 5:30 I was told that they just put a bunch of chemicals in the pool and they don't want any people to be in it. The rooms are big, but run down. Dirty carpet, stains on the bed sheets. The pool towels needed to be replaced years ago. My daughter refused to use them at all. Beach at the private island is nice, however boats go there only once in a hour, so you have to wait in long line sometimes under the hot PR sun. Internet also costs money and the same about parking.

reviews.author: Elsa Reinger
reviews.content: When you associate a hotel with the Waldorf Astoria Collection you think of luxury and upscale - dismissed that Idea from your head if you are staying at this hotel. I also do not understand why the hotel is rated so high. It is overpriced in every aspect. I just returned from a 4 night stay and this is the first time I have traveled to this location in PR. 1. The room we stayed in was in bad need of renovation. Mold on the ceiling in the bathroom closet which actually was leaking on to our clothes. Mold in tub/shower area and the countertop needed to be replaced. Walls needed to be painted and floor needed to be grouted and cleaed. The radio clock did not work - no way to tell what time it was, or to have some background music. 2. Slowest service I have ever witnessed, and I have traveled throughout the Carribean. Food and drinks highly priced plus they were always running out of products. 3. Our outside patio never had to be cleaned, around patio in grass glass and debris. 4. Casino closed at midnite, and the so-called nightclub had a sign stating either 18 or 21 or older to enter, collar shirts. Well, there was a baby in a stroller and lots of kids dancing on the dance floor. Hotel personnel walked in there and never said a word. 5. Went to the private island, took the tram down to the boat shuttle which only came every hour and was packed. The second day we went to the island "no towels" and no staff member seemed to know why, when or where to towels would arrive. 6. No adult section, the pool that had the swim up bar (usually for adults) filled with children - (jumping into the pool and screaming). The positive things about the hotel was the morning breakfast buffet was very nice and had a nice selection of food. You could rent a car from enterprises right at the resort. Arriving at the airport it was easy to find the shuttle to the hotel which they provided you with water, soda, and rum.

reviews.author: Ludwig McClure
reviews.content: My husband had a conference at this hotel, and families were invited to join for the weekend (Thursday-Sunday). My son (19 months) and I joined my husband on Thursday. On Friday afternoon we found out that the main pool area would be closed all day saturday and part of Sunday. If we had known that ahead of time, I don't think we would have stayed the weekend as outside of not being able to use the pools, we also had to deal with really loud music, spilt beer, and people walking everywhere in their swim wear acting like they were at spring break. (while also navigating hoards of people) But, assumably most people reading this hopefully wouldn't be dealing with such a circus so I'll share the relevant parts of my experience. Check-in.- My husband mentioned it took more than 45 minutes after arriving in line at 3:30 pm. with only a couple people in front of him to get through check in and too his room. I asked him "why' and he said it seemed like they were trying to find rooms for everyone. El Conquistador handled the transfer from San Juan-surely they could have in the 1.5 hours it took to get to the resort work on finding rooms to expedite this process? Room- We were fortunate and unfortunate to be in the Marina area in a corner room overlooking coqui water park. On the plus side, this was a pretty quiet area of the park-particularly a corner unit. This was especially helpful for the chaos of the spring break Heineken party on the upper part of the resort. It was also close to the boat to Palomino island which was good for us. Finally, the room had been recently renovated so that was nice. Bathroom was huge, deck was huge, and room was a decent size. View was also nice. The negatives: Lighting was pretty bad at night. It only had 3 lights. This was okay for us as we put our son to sleep and hung out in the bathroom but would be irritating otherwise. Also, the location was far from most restaurants and basically the whole resort. It was kind of a pain to have to trek in for breakfast. In retrospect, I wish I just ordered room service on the days we were heading to the beach. Beach- This is a huge drawback and is actually why i had booked another hotel (caribe hilton) for our last night in Puerto Rico. In order to go to the beach, you need to take a ferry. I was told it was an 8 minute ferry leaving every 1/2 hour. The reality? A 20 minute ferry leaving whenever. The day we went to the beach, we treked up the funicular for breakfast then made it down for the 9:30 am ferry (arriving at 9:25 am) That ferry left at 10:15 am. Try waiting in line with a toddler for 45 minutes in the hot sun. fun. Ferries also have limited times- you can only go over to Palomino island between 9 and 3. Not very convenient to coordinate around naps. Once we got to the beach, it was nice, with many shallow areas for young kids. But, no showers that I could find. We had to rinse the sand off in our hotel room. Very odd. How can a beach not have any showere nearby? Pools- Well, they were closed for much of our stay. In 500 acres though, there didn't appear to be a toddler pool. I asked the bellman and he didn't know of one. He said my son could play on steps. Coqui water park (additional charge) had an area that was like a beach (with a low gradual increase in depth) We received complimentary passes with our group. If I were a regular guest, I'd be irritated that I had to pay separately for my toddler to go in a pool. (oh no fee for under 3, but I'd have to pay). Food- I actually was pleasantly surprised to have some affordable food options (ie. breakfast for $10/entree) No kids menu though. Most of our meals were included with the conference so I basically only went to breakfast. Thought the lunch on palmomino was good. Spa: A real trek t get here from the Marina. I did this the festival day and it was a bit of a headache. I did the caribbean escape session. I thought the spa was poorly marketed.
