description: A small country guest house providing bed and breakfast with stunning views across the countryside to the sea and Caldey Island. Close to the [[Pembrokeshire Coast National Park]] and a good base for walking, sightseeing and cycling and for those brave enough to tackle [http://eu.ironman.com/triathlon/events/emea/ironman/wales.aspx#axzz2qprvonAU ''Ironman Wales'']  Gumfreston is just 10 minutes from the starting line.
name: St Lawrence Country Guest House

reviews.author: Hortense Stehr
reviews.content: We went there to celebrate my husbands 50th birthday day and couldn't have picked a better resort. Read alot of reviews on this hotel and we did not have any complaints. Beach, food, service and room were all wonderful. I can't see how anyone can complain about this resort. This was one of our best vacations. Thanks to Sue and Steve for going with us.

reviews.author: Aletha Pfannerstill
reviews.content: I never usually write reviews, but I felt compelled, as we relied on so many before we booked. We had the absolute best time at Secrets Maroma! To give you some background on where our point of view comes from, my husband and I are in our mid-30's, and we were there celebrating our 11 year anniversary. We are pretty well-traveled when it comes to the Caribbean. This was my fourth trip to Mexico, and my husband’s first trip to the Mayan Riviera. We stayed from 10/1-4. As for all-inclusives we have stayed at 3 different Sandals resorts, and have had really negative experiences at 2 of the 3. However, we cannot travel as much as we'd like to, so all-inclusives are an easy way to alleviate the extra planning as far as dining and activities are concerned. This time, we decided on Mexico, and booked Secrets due to the positive reviews. We are so glad we did. And I will never give Sandals another single cent of my money now that I see how much more superior Secrets is. They ought to be ashamed of themselves, charging 2-3 times as much for such substandard accommodations and below-par service….yet, I digress. I won't break down every aspect of the resort, as this has been done. However, I would like to address some of the negative comments. First, this resort is designed in a specific Mexican style. As such it has interesting fountains and waterways, and a very clean design aesthetic. Everything has been laid out to promote the feeling of tranquility and a spa-like atmosphere. We loved this about Secrets. We aren't the type to live in the pool, as the reason we go to a beach resort is to enjoy the beach, but we were happy with the set-up of the pool areas. As for the complaints about lack of lush vegetation, again-I feel that the people complaining just don't understand the design. There was absolutely nothing brown while we were there. Quite the contrary, everything was very green and there were flowers everywhere. Short of staying in a tropical rainforest, I am not sure what these people are looking for as far as landscaping is concerned. We have been to beaches in 10-plus different Caribbean islands and I will say that this is one of the most beautiful beaches we have ever seen. The water is very clear and you can see your feet on the bottom. I suppose it gets cloudy from time to time--when a WAVE crashes the beautiful, soft SAND onto the shoreline. If that's a problem, then I am afraid there may be no pleasing you. The seaweed is minimal (and is raked away), there are pretty angel fish everywhere, and it is simply gorgeous. It was hard to stay out of the ocean. We always got a palapa in a spot we liked, the service on the beach (and everywhere else) was amazing, and we could not have been happier. There was never a crowded feel. The ashtrays are there to keep smokers from putting their butts out on the beach. As a non-smoker, I appreciated this tremendously. Basically, I know that not everyone can be pleased all of the time. There were a couple of areas that we felt could have been a little better (food variety at dinner, mainly), but I cannot say we were ever complaining. The good exponentially outweighed the less than good, and you can be sure you will have a wonderful time at this resort. Look at it this way, if the main complaints are mosquitoes (which is out of anyone's control--try Jamaica or St. Lucia if you think Mexico is bad), not enough trees, and beach ashtrays, then you really don’t have problems. Book with confidence and enjoy.

reviews.author: Candice Koelpin
reviews.content: This resort is Wonderful. I'm still unclear why one would complain about the grounds not being tropical enough or the food being below average. We ate far better than we expected, and the place is beautifuI. I mean, come on, this place was incrediable! I won't even try to describe the breathtaking ocean view because you just can not unerstand it until you've seen for yourself. The colors of the water and sky look more like a painting. I didn't think anything could really be That Picture Perfect. My husband, better known around the pool's swim-up bar as "Tuscaloosa" (Johnny) and our buddies Kandy and her husband "Alabama" (Richard) were pampered and spoiled from the time we were picked up from the airport until we were,sadly enough, delivered back there almost a week later. We had swim-out rooms that were fantastic! Really, I would have protested had they tried to upgrade us to anything else. Yes, the A/C are below par. We spent Very Little time in our room and we're always greated with little suprises when we returned...Roses, drawn bubble baths, turn down services. (and we were not even honeymooners or anything) Please, don't be one of those Non Tippers! REALLY, These people work way too hard for you to use the excuse that it's not required. Besides, You'll be surprised at the extra attention to detail you receive when you repect the people who are working so hard to please you. The spa is a must. My husband went kicking and screaming but now is checking for local spas around our home town so we can enjoy little weenend "pick me ups" Ha! The swim-up bar was a blast. The event staff was great at getting a willing, and usually tipsy gang to join in on the activities. I can't say enough about the pool volleyball. Although my back picked the worst weenend EVER to go out, I laughed more in two days just watching and listening to all the funny "smack" talk from the guest AND event staff. If you see Fernando at pool bar, ask him to introduce you to Don Julio. We give them (Don and Fernando) honerable mentions every time we talk of our vacation !!! Please remember to take a bottle of fresh water and a little extra bite of meat and share with the stray dog at the beach. She sometimes plays in the ocean after she's been fed. Look for the man on horseback a bit south down the beach. For tips, He does a few tricks on horseback and will let you take pictures of them or he will take pixs of you on the horse..Pretty cool for photo opp. Please tell Fernando that Diane and Tuscalosoa said hello. And relax, you're gonna love it here!

title: Gumfreston

description: Aberdovey Hillside Village offers award winning self-catering holiday accommodation. "The Village" is a cluster of specially designed houses and apartments which blend naturally into a south-facing hillside taking full advantage of magnificent views. We are also pet friendly, with your dogs able to enjoy long walks on sandy beaches and magnificent countryside.  The village is remarkably quiet and peaceful, set in spacious landscaped grounds which lead into the open countryside, yet it is just above the heart of picturesque Aberdovey. The shops and beaches are within 300 metres
directions: Turn right in square, past front of chapel and continue straight up Church St for approximately 200 metres, ignoring left dog-leg and continue to metal gates.
name: Aberdovey Hillside Village

reviews.author: Mr. Al Simonis
reviews.content: My girlfriend and I decided to surprise our 11-year-old daughter with a trip to Seattle for her birthday this last weekend. She had never been and we knew she would love it. I actually went on a hotel discount site and was given this hotel. I had been in the Portland location once and remember it being beautiful and have stayed at other Kimpton hotels and had great experiences. After receiving notice of our reservation I emailed their staff and informed them this trip was for a birthday and requested a room with 2 beds, hopefully towards the top. The assistant manager promptly replied and said that he could accommodate that request but the 2-bed options were lower and didn't have the best views. He then offered to upgrade us for $40 to one of the suites on the top floor. Given that we got such a good deal on the hotel price it was a no-brainer. The suite was excellent with a king bed in the bedroom and a pullout queen sleeper sofa in the living area. Both rooms had their own TV's and there was a curtain that could be drawn to separate the two areas. The room was very clean and well appointed. The bathroom was nice but wasn't as lavish as some other 4-star hotels we've been to. All of the soaps and shampoos though were high-end and there was nothing lacking. That night the hotel staff also left a note in our room with a birthday card for our daughter which included a free in-room movie rental as well as an invitation to call down for a complimentary birthday cake. We called down and they brought up a delicious personal-sized chocolate cake with ice cream and a candle in it. She was very excited! Throughout our 2-night stay the staff continued to be amazing. We spent a lot of our time checking out Seattle attractions but each time we came back we were greeted warmly. There was a wine tasting each night in the lobby and the staff always offered to get my daughter a soft drink from the restaurant. There were bowls of chocolates around that we all enjoyed as well. If I had anything to add to the "con" side it would be that the views from this hotel aren't as attractive as some others I've stayed at in Seattle. It's only an 11-story building and there are taller buildings surrounding it. If you're expecting a full city view or one of the water you may be disappointed. We also thought the cost of valet parking was a little much, coming to nearly $40 per night with taxes. I am sure this is on-par with other 4-star hotels but is pretty hard to justify. We opted to valet on Friday night but found street parking on Saturday night since parking is free on Sundays. Overall though, it was a great experience and I would highly recommend staying there. Even with getting our reservation through a third party site we were never treated differently and that says a lot about a place.

reviews.author: Rossie McGlynn
reviews.content: My wife and I decided to visit Seattle for a quick weekend trip to get away for our 20th anniversary. We always love staying at Kimpton hotels and have stayed at the Alexis Hotel and Hotel Vintage Park in Seattle, so this time we decide to try the Hotel Monaco. As expected, our stay was wonderful. When we arrived we were met by the bellman how helped with our luggage. This was helpful since we had brought our two Shih Thus with us. Check in was quick and in less than 5 minutes, the valet had our car and we were checked in and heading to our room. The room was very nice with a small living room that made it a little more than â€œjust a roomâ€�. We had room service the first night and the food was great and was delivered in less than 20 minutes. Evening turndown service got our room ready for the night including chocolates on the pillow. The hotel is in the perfect spot in Seattle because you can walk to Pikeâ€™s Market, the movies, the shopping center and even the tram to get you around town. The hotelâ€™s wine reception was great and we found others had brought their pets with them. Kimptonâ€™s â€œpet friendlyâ€� program is wonderful. We came back from running around one night and found a bottle of champagne to help us celebrate our anniversary. Our three days went by much too fast and we really did not want to leave, but all good things must come to an end. The good news is we can always go back and know we will get great service.

reviews.author: Ibrahim Cassin
reviews.content: First impressions: The bellman and the front desk people both immediately demonstrated they were well trained and paying attention to their guests. The front desk lady provided great information (at a pace that was energetic but not rushed), helpful leading questions about the area, and major positive energy without bubbling or being insincere. The bellman was busy with another car when we arrived, but noticed the car in front right away and within a very short period met up with me at the reception desk to get the key from me. We stayed in one of the Monte Carlo suites -- great energizing decor. Comfortable living room area, seperated from bedroom by large drapes, which was great for reading the morning papers or sipping the wine from the lobby before heading out to dinner. The bath had plenty of counter space for both of us (though one sink). The bed was comfortable with a range of pillows, as well as seating arrangements including a nice, comfortable chair and a small, two person bench seat for shoes, dressing, etc. Our maid service did a great job with meticulous neatening up. We also had dinner one night in Sazarac, a New Orleans style restaurant where we encountered more of the same: normal people, working hard, to provide thoughtful, positive service. This included our host, who conscientiously got us a table and our waitress who was busy, friendly, informative and attentive. Monaco is a tremendous location: next door to Starbucks (though there is free coffee in the lobby in the mornings); a block from the Capitol Grill; and easy walking to the retail core. The room was very reasonably priced and we like service, but service at a bargain is even better!

reviews.author: Melyssa Veum
reviews.content: I have stayed at Hotel Monaco at least five or six visits over the past month. The staff is consistently friendly and efficient. I believe they care about their guests and will do what it takes to make your stay as comfortable as possible. This extends from the front desk to the bell men and housecleaning. The staff in Sazerac restaurant is also fantastic.

reviews.author: Cristobal Schimmel
reviews.content: Just returned from 3 night stay over the Labor Day weekend at the Hotel Monaco Seattle. We met some friends of ours, who also stayed there in a separate room. The location was good for us and anyone who doesn't have issues with moderate walking -- it was a multi-block walk to Pikes Market, the waterfront, etc. -- you do have up hill walking when you return to the hotel from Pikes Market or the waterfront, though we found some streets to be less steep than others (Union Street, for instance). From the moment we arrived at the hotel we found the staff to be friendly, professional and helpful, and this continued throughout our stay -- the valet, doorman, front desk reps, concierge, housekeeping, etc. Each time we were leaving the hotel, the front desk people would acknowledge us with pleasantries such as "have a nice day"; upon our return they would again acknowledge us with "welcome back", or something similar. The evening wine event in the lobby was a very nice touch. The overall feel of the hotel was that it was nicely decorated and clean and felt welcoming. The room was also nicely decorated and clean and larger than the average hotel room. There was ample comfortable seating, i.e. two upholstered chairs and a very comfortable desk chair at the large desk. Also, the room had multiple sources of bright lighting -- best lighting of any hotel we've stayed in. There was a nice size flat screen TV, stocked mini-fridge (items for purchase), stocked snack tray (also for purchase), and a room safe as well. Though coffee service is provided in the lobby each morning, there is no coffee service in the room, however, you can request a set-up for your room, if desired. The beds were extremely comfortable, i.e. the mattress, linens, comforter, and pillows. The air conditioner worked great and you are able to control the temp. to your liking from the in-room thermostat. The bathroom, too, was larger than usual. The shower head was to die for and with great water pressure, so you didn't have to spend a longer-than-usual amount of time in the shower trying to shower with a trickle of water, as is the case in many hotels (especially important to those of us with longer, thicker hair). They also had a wall-mounted rack containing full-size pump bottles of shampoo, cream rinse, and liquid bath soap. A hair dryer was also provided. You should know ahead of time, as we did, that many of the rooms face directly towards another high rise, in close proximity, especially if you want a room with two beds versus a king; we were told that there are no two bed rooms not facing the building; besides not having a view or much natural light, this necessitates keeping your curtains closed for privacy -- but, again, at least there's great lighting provided in the room. There are only two things I would add to my wish list for the hotel -- one is to have at least some two-bed rooms that don't face a building and the second is to provide larger than the standard size bath towels. All in all, this was a terrific hotel experience and we will definitely return there on future trips. This was our first stay at a Kimpton Hotel but, based on this experience, it won't be our last!

reviews.author: Kaela Shanahan
reviews.content: My son and I just stayed a week at the Hotel Monaco in Seattle. The location was great; we were able to walk to WNBA, MLS, and MLB games. There were a couple issues with the service. We are members of the InTouch club and are supposed to get newspapers delivered to the room each day. We only got papers two of the five days. I asked the front desk after the fourth day, and they said "well, there are other guests, and sometimes we run out, but there's a whole bunch of papers over there against the wall". Then, I didn't get the paper the next day either. My young son was supposed to get a welcome gift as part of the InTouch club, but he received nothing. I asked about this the next morning, and they said there's a box where kids can go chose something (we got a deck of cards). Also, for the morning tea/coffee service in the lobby, the black tea ran out very early each day as did the lemonade/tea in the afternoon. It seems there's just a half hearted effort for these "perks". They should either support the service or not. Other than these things, the hotel was fine. The room was nice; the food in the restaurant was great. We loved our pet fish (Fred).

title: Aberdyfi

description: 29 rooms
name: Tre-Ysgawen Hall, Country House Hotel and Spa

reviews.author: Mr. Kurtis Lang
reviews.content: The rooms were very beautiful and very clean. The bed was so comfortable, i slept amazing! The breakfast up on the gorgeous roof was a great way to start the day. The staff was so friendly, polite, and helpful. I have never recieved that great of service at a hotel. Staff helped me with anything from directions to handing me an umbrrella when it was raining. It was a great place to stay! :)

reviews.author: Jazlyn Berge Sr.
reviews.content: Stayed for a long weekend with my 2 sons we found the room very clean ,tidy and very quiet but is some way from the train stations and the west end ,there is a bus service 113 from the hotel into the west end 'The hotel is on a very busy highway,as is not near any shops or pubs ,so if you like a drink you will have a good walk,but for the price you pay its good value.

reviews.author: Raphael Cormier
reviews.content: They are putting money into this hotel. The rooms were 89Â£ (pounds). They had redone the lobby, they were doing the brick driveway, and the room I stayed in 217 looked brand new. The breakfast was included and was standard english breakfast. It was quiet. Parking is a bit tight, but at no additional charge. It is outside the city, but half the city cost or less. I would recommend it.

reviews.author: Jimmie Thiel
reviews.content: The extremely loud music from a celebration carried on till 3.30am. We were informed by other very bleary-eyed breakfast guests that they had also suffered the noise the previous night! Complaining at Reception we were informed music should have stopped at Midnight. Reading previous reviews on this Hotel it is obvious they do not read thier customers reviews and they do not care. No wonder they want the fees paid in advance...

reviews.author: Mae Rosenbaum
reviews.content: Couldn't have asked for better service. We didn't have a car and were offered free shuttle to any restaurant we chose!! Delightful, clean nice outdoor pool! Like!!!!

reviews.author: Ms. Isadore Fritsch
reviews.content: Have stayed at this hotel five times and it has been a pleasure every time. Decent breakfast and they have a free dinner Mon-Thurs (menu posted in the frig). Rooms are large and have the full kitchen setup. If you have to make a left turn when leaving the hotel (NW 74th to NW 36th st) I suggest taking the street behind the hotel (Herman St also know as NW 25th Terrace) to Milam Dairy Rd then left to NW 36th St. This will save you time during peak traffic hrs. Intenet was free for me but was bogged down by heavy usage.

title: Llangefni

description: Fortress style built in 1862, now a hotel
name: Great Orme Lighthouse

reviews.author: Vaughn Miller
reviews.content: Our stay at the I Hotel was brief but wonderful. The rooms are quiet, the beds are very comfortable, and the decor is modern and elegant. There is much beautiful woodwork throughout. The staff members went out of their way to be helpful and informative. The landscaping is lovely. They provide a free shuttle service to anywhere on the University of Illinois campus and a room rate discount for those of us on a college visit. I highly recommend this hotel and we certainly plan to stay there again on future visits to the area.

reviews.author: Mable Mertz
reviews.content: My son and I spent two nights at the I Hotel and Conference Center which is located adjacent to the University of Illinois in Champaign. We found the staff to be friendly and very helpful yet unobtrusive, the hotel and rooms spotless and comfortable, and the location next to the university very convenient. Wireless internet was free, and when I asked to use a printer to I was given access to a computer in a peaceful and secure room. I would definitely stay there again.

reviews.author: Mya Feeney
reviews.content: It is really the best stay with value for money I ever stayed in Dubai. If you want economic stay with 5 star hotel, this is the one. For bed room including kitchen, 2 bathrooms and living room with 2 LCD tv, you pay ONLY less than $120 per night. So what do you think? It is really lovely hotel. The breakfast is delicious. The location near Dubai Mall and the Metro station on Zayed Road. It is your best shot if you are coming with your family and small kids.

reviews.author: Donna Schultz
reviews.content: Hotel quality is very terrible. Last year turkish great hotel chain company "dedeman" release this hotel to the best western. Before releasing hotel had acceptable management even, over the expectations. After best western took control of management hotel staff did not change but their mentality changed. They are look like a summer intern and do not care about anything. Staff's skill terrible and they are rude. Tea and coffee smells chlorine from the water. I asked them to control their waters and tea smells chlorine. One staff answered me i dont know because i did not do tea. Also extra bed is about the 150 cm. Its like a comedy and the bed sizes looks like children's bed but its NOT !!! :O Never go there !!

reviews.author: Demarcus Bartell
reviews.content: With a wealth of hotels to choose from in the Chi area, I have sampled from the best. Many of them have been quite good, but for the past couple of years, I've opted for the Dana. Location-wise, it's just off the Magnificent Mile in the midst of everything that particular stretch has to offer. Room-wise, it's got everything I need -- they're relatively spacious, have floor to ceiling windows/Juliet balconies that afford you a great view or if it's a balcony, just some fresh air (a great alternative to air conditioning), to-die-for bathrooms situated in the middle of the room (with glass-enclosed showers that let you see out while you shower if you desire, or shades if it's privacy you want), wonderful bath amenities, and -- something I've never had at any other hotel -- hand-made chocolates/candies in their honor bar in lieu of the usual M&Ms etc. Plush bathrobes and slippers too. Room service is good (in terms of offerings and timeliness) and the food is fine. The gym is just OK, unfortunately. Rather small & cramped, there is only 1 workout bench and only a couple of machines. Earlier this week I was there with 4 other (unrelated) guests and we were falling over each other and jealously watching as soon as someone finished his/her reps or workout so we could grab the equipment before anyone else. Dana management -- this is an easy fix -- please expand. The restaurant (Aja, pronounced like the continent) is pretty good too. I've only eaten there once (there are so many choices in this neck of the woods), but when I did, the menu was varied and unusual, and the service good -- even a bit over the top (I lost count of the number of people who checked in with us to make sure everything was OK); I almost expected the chef to be next! Unless my company changes its travel policy, I expect to continue to stay here, esp if they expand the gym.

reviews.author: Tierra Schultz
reviews.content: This is a very trendy, fun place to stay. My girlfriend loved it and anytime someone is coming into town we recommend it. The food is excellent, although the only complaint was that the nueskis bacon wasn't the black pepper crusted type, which is the best bacon on the planet. Other than the small disappointment here we were both thrilled with the room, service, and food. slightly pricey, but you get a lot more than the average hotel. def a step up from the more popular W downtown. And close to a lot of great downtown and river-north spots.

title: Wales Coast Path

description: Built in 1821, now a hotel.
name: West Usk Lighthouse

reviews.author: Laron Braun DDS
reviews.content: Recently stayed at the Hotel Dana and had a excellent experience. Location is great and every staff member we dealt with was professional, courteous and very helpful. The rooms are very comfortable(stayed a Serene Rain King or something along those lines-it was the one around 335 SqF) and it had all the amenities I needed and the perfect amount of space. I have stayed in many of the boutique and regular hotels in the Magnificent Mile area and I would rank this among the best in terms of hospitality and quality. When I was looking at this hotel a few mentioned that they could hear neighboring rooms and the walls were thin. I never had this issue nor did it seem that way at all. I would not hesitate to stay here again. The hotel also has a nice bar on the first floor and a great rooftop lounge (both indoor and out and open year round) that during the week is not too busy and a nice stop for a drink.

reviews.author: Dr. Derek Roob
reviews.content: This hotel has a very modern, young vibe. Our room was large with a living room, bedroom and bathroom with a walk-in shower. The bathroom was all tile, 2 shower heads and 2 benches. We had 2 balconies with a great view of the city. The night-club upstairs was hip and seemed to be the in-place to be. Everything was within walking distance for us (we love to walk). Michigan Ave 3 blocks away. Lots of shopping, restaurants, all within a few minutes.

reviews.author: Roxane Heathcote
reviews.content: A last-minute booking in downtown Chicago on Halloween weekend... Never having before been to Chicago, and not knowing my State St. from my LaSalle Ave... Without a clue as to the relative distances between things in the downtown area... This tale isn't starting out so good, is it? So I took a gamble on a highly-rated, glowingly-reviewed, but perfectly-priced downtown Chicago almost-boutique property, the Dana (pronounced "day-nah"), and let the Fates have their way with me. This time they were most kind. Too kind, in fact. In a word? The Dana is CRUSHING!!! That's what the experience was like. Everything began from the moment I arrived... Seeing as I'd booked so late after my local contact dropped the ball on my hotel reservations, the order hadn't even cleared Expedia.ca's queue (I ordered off the Canadian site, seeing as I'm based in Toronto) when Frederick came through in the clutch -- one call to Admin, he had me sorted out lickety-split. And I thought I'd be waiting for at least 20 mins. No vacancies given the Halloween weekend? Nope...rather than shunt me off to some out-of-the-way silly room facing a brick wall or nestled in a noisy alleyway (read my review of my last hotel stay in Cascais, Portugal)...I was treated like arriving royalty. I was given a top-floor room with a majestic Chicago-style skyscraper view facing north in a sumptuously-appointed suite with all the fixings, the majority of which I regrettably didn't use, but were available to me if needed. All manner of drinks and snacks were *already* available for the taking as I stepped in (no phone call to room service), so for those of you who don't like venturing out into the urban wilderness to fetch victuals or groceries...it's a snap. Only thing I feel terrible about is the fact that I came alone, and had business to attend to in town. Definitely the next time I have occasion to be in Chicago, I'll be bringing company and enjoying all of the Dana's cute little charms. Seeing as it was a birthday trip, Romeo on concierge duty was uber-helpful in suggesting jazz venues for my birthday evening jaunt -- even offering me a drink on-the-house -- and his cab directions were spot-on. Romeo has a knack for remembering everyone's name and as you pass through the lobby, the Dana Front Office guys and gals are always quick to share a laugh or a kind word with you as they address you by name, which makes all the difference when staying at some of the medium-priced hotels. You don't want to ever be treated like a number and that was never the case during my stay. Bonus! Checking out? Breeze! I had an insanely early checkout time (five-ish in the a.m.), and Lindsay realized that I was in a rush to get to O'Hare/ORD for my morning cross-border flight back north. He noticed that I was getting a bit jittery and antsy, seeing as he was serving an arriving guest just as I was about to dance on out of Dodge, within two keystrokes he had my invoice printed and my cash deposit back to me. #FTW!!! Bottom line: while I didn't get a chance to use all the facilities to their maximum -- pity, I know, given the high quality of this place and the fact that the Dana seems like a place tailor-made for fun -- it's an all-star hotel. I even made a short video of the bathroom area to show my friends that such a thing actually exists, and that I wasn't making it all up. Added feature: there's even a nightclub on the top floor -- with some pretty stylish attractive guests (yes!) who were streaming through the patron-only exclusive elevator that spirits them skyward -- though I didn't have time to party there but makes me want to get back to Chicago ASAP just to sample it. That shower is heavenly -- I won't describe it and ruin your surprise (nor will I forget it), but it's worth every dollar you'll spend and newlyweds, couples, or businessmen enjoying a little extra-curricular fun away from home will appreciate the look, and, er...feel of it. And that king-sized bed? I didn't even realize what hit me as I woke up most mornings, and those were the nights I wasn't enjoying a few beers! Unless you've got family in Chicago and they'd be insulted that you're not staying with them during your visit, stay at the Dana and be happy. Very happy. I was and plan to be again...

title: Wales Coast Path

description: Hotel and restaurant
name: George Borrow Hotel

reviews.author: Delia Kuhlman
reviews.content: We stayed here for 1 night before catching the eurostar. I usually go for travelodge when I want good clean comfortable accommodation that is cheap. The hotel only managed to fulfill one of my criteria, it was cheap enough, but that was were the usual comparisons ended. It was not a clean hotel nor was our room comfortable, the bed linen was grubby, when I sat on the bed my bum was nearly touching the floor it sagged so much! The cleanliness of the bathroom left much to be desired and the staff were rude when I asked for an extra pillow, saying they didnt have any! I requested a quiet room as we had an early start, granted it is difficult in London to give you a quiet room but our room was on the first floor, opposite the bus and train station, and the door to the lift so quiet it definately was not. I would think twice before staying here again

reviews.author: Mckenna Schultz DVM
reviews.content: We stayed at this hotel New Years Eve, the staff were very friendly on our arrival we were checked in easily no problems. We had a double room which was the typical Travelodge room basic no frills, once again just a pet hate of mine a double room has 2 people so why is there only 3 pillows I always have to ask for another one. Excellent location for all the train stations just over road from Euston and about 5 minutes to Kings Cross/ St Pancras. Breakfast was terrible though, eggs smelt of kippers, orange juice was just water with a bit of orange in it, We couldnt drink it. Bed was too soft and very lumpy Otherwise this is a reasonable hotel if you just want a base to sightsee its a perfect location for underground. If you would like to contact me please feel free plus please click the helpfull button if you thought this review has helped you.

reviews.author: Arno Heathcote
reviews.content: If you want luxury at budget prices forget. This is a budget hotel located across the road from Euston station. We were efficiently booked in by courteous staff. The room was basic but clean. Bed ok I have slept in a lot worse in more expensive hotels. TV in room and coffee tea making facilities. Bathroom clean and adequate for our needs. Had breakfast which was probably one of the best value breakfast I have had in a hotel, hot, tasty and plenty of it .Good location for transport to get around London. For the price I would certainly recommend this.

reviews.author: Marilie McLaughlin
reviews.content: Stayed at this hotel for 2 nights in April 2011 while attending a gig. Found the double room to be quite small, especially when compared with similar rooms offered by Premier Inn. The air conditioning did not seem to work and the cushions were poor. First morning's sleep was disturbed by a policeman shouting in at some guests 3 or 4 doors down. Looked like some form of negotiation was going on? On the good side it is conveniently located across the road from Euston tube and was easy to find.

reviews.author: Kali Kling
reviews.content: Plus points - Ok rooms, basic mine but clean enough - Eating facilities and a bar - TV in room - Great location for Euston - Reasonable price Could be better - No hairdryer - No toiletries - Didnt like being in basment - Noisey with church bells ringing!

reviews.author: Marilie Smith
reviews.content: Stayed here for two nights in September 2011. The main draw was the location - my train got in late and I didn't want to be traipsing across the city - it is right next to Euston and about a 5 minute walk from Kings Cross. Euston is well equipped with shops, including an M&S food store so you can grab breakfast there! There is an automatic check in machine which was simple to operate. My double room was on the third floor and on the side street - there was some noise at night but not too much. The rollerblind shut out any light. The room was clean although a few of the fixtures, especially in the bathroom needed fixed or upgraded - eg the bathroom bin had a metal spike sticking out , one of the buttons on the shower was broken and a bedside lamp needed fixed. The bed was reasonably comfortable, and the room was equipped with a kettle and a flatscreen tv on the wall - it was next to the bed so you had to lie across it to see properly. All in all, its fine for a place to lay your head and the location is very convenient.

title: Ponterwyd

description: 8 berth, 3 bedroom caravan sited in its own grounds situated in the garden of a farm.
name: Llanbedrgoch Holiday Caravan

reviews.author: Tommie Steuber
reviews.content: Stayed for one night as catching the eurostar early the next day and was great for this purpose. 10 min walk to st pancreas... Check in was fine. although I had asked for a quiet room and been allocated one on the main road and with young children I wasnt happy with this but reception were very friendly and happy to change us to the basement. (although this meant we ended up having to collapse and take the travel cot to our new room) but this was a small price in my eyes to get a lovely quiet room. Room modern, clean and new tv. Paid Â£29 so great value for money and a bargain for central london.

reviews.author: Grayce Crooks
reviews.content: This was only Â£85 for one night for a family room including breakfast, cheap for London.However be aware that there is a reason for this. The hotel is clean as you would expect and the room had air conditioning which was a god send with 31degree temperatures BUT you would think that the windows were wide open with the noise from outside. Not just the station noise but bus noise and people coming home from pubs. Stayed in another travelodge in the City on previous nights with no noise but no A/C. I guess you cant have it all!!!

reviews.author: Nikolas Beer
reviews.content: I stayed in this hotel for 1 night before travelling on the Eurostar to Paris. I choose it because its only a 5 minute walk from St Pancreas station and right beside Euston Station. However I did not sleep a wink because of the terrible traffic which goes on all night long. The hotel itself was ok for a Travelodge as it was clean an quite comfortable. We did have breakfast included, which was a bonus, but the choice was very limited. All in all very handy location but don't stay here if you are a light sleeper

reviews.author: Abner Wolff
reviews.content: Me, my partner and our 6 year old son stayed in London Euston Travelodge for 3 nights from Friday to Monday. Room was clean and spacious for the price we paid (Â£95+Â£19+Â£19= Â£133 - for all 3 nights) on the third floor facing back of the house. Room was medium size with king-size bed and sofa bed. Sofa bed actually had a pull out, so if needed 4 people could sleep easy in one room, they say 2 adults and 2 kids, but sofa cold accommodate adults as well if needed. The hotel is situated right next to the Euston station, easy access to trains, tube and buses and it is easy walk to Kings Cross and if you don't mind 10-15 walk you could walk to soho or Oxford street. Bed was comfortable. Only thing I would mark down is that only continental breakfast was available, but there are plenty options in near station. Staff was very friendly toward us and between them pleasure to deal with them, I would employ them myself. They gave us a room on the back of the house after we asked politely for a quite room.

reviews.author: Amara Hilll
reviews.content: Travelodge is a basic hotel chain. It delivers what it says it will, at a great low price. I stayed in the London Euston travelodge for two nights. The reception was busy when I arrived. I knew that check-in was after 3:00 and I planned my arrival accordingly. I like that check out is up to 12:00, an earlier time can be troublesome. There were two receptionists on duty and the queue cleared quickly. The Euston Travelodge only offers continental breakfast. Watch out for the times as it is quite late on weekends, 8:00. I arrived early, then again dead on time and the door was locked. When I was there only a few people were eating so the self service was fast and convenient. It was probably healthy for me too. The room was basic, which was what was expected. There was a double bed and somewhere to hang clothes, hospitality tray for tea and coffee, tv and desk. All adequate, clean and comfortable. The bedside lights were mobile and gave enough light. There was a good blind on the window, which faced onto other buildings not the busy streets. Euston station is 2-3 minutes away, less if the crossing lights are with you. The British Library is very close as are the Eurostar terminal at St Pancras and Kings Cross. Both Euston and Euston Square underground stations are close. There is a catholic church down the road. There is no restaurant but the area has several to pick from. This is a bed and breakfast hotel in an excellent location with no frills. I liked best the lack of fuss and the efficient nature of the service provided. Least good were the breakfast times, at weekends, and the number of pillows, but you can always ask for another pillow. This hotel is five stars because you get exactly what was advertised.

title: Benllech

description: family run caravan park
name: Ty Newydd Leisure Park

reviews.author: Gladyce Larkin
reviews.content: Stayed at the Travelodge Euston for 3 nights on a London break with wife and teenage daughter. There has been loads of reports on here about check in staff being dis-interested but the girl who checked us in was very polite & helpful. We had a room on the lower ground floor (basement basically) which had advantages and dis-advantages. The advantage was there was no traffic noise at all which many reiewers on T.A. complained of. The disadvantage was the window was sealed so therefore it became very stuffy, there was aircon which obviously wasn't working properly. The hotel location was great. Literally across the road from Euston Station which is only 4 stops from Leicester Square on the tube. Also, outside the station there are various eateries / coffee shops etc and a tip for the blokes - the Doric Arch pub in the station shows the Ashes on large LCD tellies which is where I sloped off to when the women were getting ready for the evening! There is a bar in the hotel which opened til around 11pm which was quite convenient. If anyone needs any info, please feel free to ask & I will glady answer as best I can.

reviews.author: Lessie Collier
reviews.content: Was part of a group of friends who were travelling on via Eurostar the next morning. We booked 3 family rooms, which could have slept 3 people easily for an average of Â£40 per room. For such a central location this represents great value. The hotel is fairly new so still is clean and fresh, something that Travelodges sometimes fail on. It is situated right next to Euston station so is very handy. The area remains fairly noisy all night with plenty of street noise so this can lead to a broken nights sleep. If you are looking for budget accomodation in Central London then this is a really good bet.

reviews.author: Jaunita Veum
reviews.content: Stayed here for a couple of nights and had to change room 4 times before finding a room with working heating!! the rooms were like fridges and some were very noisy due to the 24hr bus route outside which shakes your room. Rooms were quite small but ok. bathroom had a nice shower but annoying curtain which was useless and resulted in the batroom floor being flooded each time. Breakfast was ok and staff were very nice, location in terms of seeing london is great and only 5 mins walk from Eurostar terminal

reviews.author: Kaia Gulgowski DDS
reviews.content: The hotel was clean and new and not too far for us to walk to from Kings Cross. Got the room for Â£49 on a super saver deal luckily. We also found it annoying that they have nowhere to hold luggage and charged us Â£10 to check in early to room that was ready anyway! We had a quiet room although the windown did not open and has a horrible frosted screen over it to stop you being able to see out of it! I wouldn't want to pay full price for a room there but for Â£45 it was bearable Why do travelodges always have those nasty thin pillows though!!!

reviews.author: Mckenzie Nicolas
reviews.content: My husband and I stayed here for one night as a stop-over through Miami. We got a great price on the room through the hotel's website. The hotel has plenty of free parking, a friendly, competent staff, the room was immaculate and nicely decorated, comfortable bed, on-site breakfast buffet (we were able to get a reduced price by asking when we checked in), free wireless internet. We definitely would recommend this hotel. As for "be aware" items - it is located very close to the airport, so we did occasionally hear a plane, but not to the point of it being a disturbance. Also the bathroom has a walk-in shower (no tub), which was fine for us. My over-6-ft-tall husband appreciated that the showerhead was mounted high up on the wall, so the water didn't hit him mid-chest (you tall people will know what I'm talking about!!). We would definitely stay here again if we needed a room in Miami.

reviews.author: Marquis Hansen
reviews.content: This hotel was clean, the service was great; however, the bed was terrible. It was like sleeping on concrete, my boy friend I checked out two days earlier and checked into a different hotel

reviews.author: Ernesto Erdman
reviews.content: Although we stayed for only 1 night, we enjoyed our stay and would stay again. Hotel was clean and rooms were quite large. Staff was helpful. Breakfast was not included.

title: Benllech

address: Talwrn, nr Benllech, Isle Of Anglesey
description: Detached barn conversion
name: Swallow Cottage Benllech

reviews.author: Damaris Hettinger
reviews.content: The Hilton Garden Inn is a rare find when trying to stay near Miami Srings to visit my sister. The Hotel is conveniet, close to airport, food, & shopping. The moment you arrive the property is clean, well lighted, and very clean. The front desk staff greets you & it is obvious that they have reviewed their guest reservations before I checked in. "Colleen" is just fantastic at the front. She knew all the info, explained every detail & was Nice. The room, hallways, gym & pool were spotless & made us feel secure from the germ world . The main focal point of this hotel is the lobby, bar, & restaurant area that is a central happy hour meeting place as well as the breakfast venue in the morning. The clientele are mostly business travelers & airline personnel. Given that information the regard from all the staff is that they are greeting you as a professional. Great Coffee, Great Evolution Bed and Plush clean smelling towels. It is really nice to get out of the pool or hot tub & have blue striped towels waiting for you. The bathroom products are Neutrogena & were very well stocked. The fitness room has a clean bathroom & Blue Crystal Water cold water dispenser with cups. The breakfast is run by the real kitchen with a real cook & wait staff. The beginning buffet is simply self serve with real fruit, juice, & the usual breakfast fare. We were impressed with the staff & the nighttime security in the parking lot. For convenience you park right up on the building and all is real close. It helps that the Hilton Homewood suites sister property is adjoining on the west side. We felt safe and relaxed usiung the pool area at night. we will definitely stay here again. Colleen & Brian make this place a service oriented great place to stay. thankyou & enjoy

reviews.author: Dr. Rolando Feeney
reviews.content: I didn't expect big city hotel staff to be this friendly. Almost all employees smiled and greeted my family. Especially, one employee named Pam went beyond to make us feel welcome and comfortable by talking with us and even offered complimentary amenity. She made real positive impression of the hotel and the Miami. Room was spacious and the whole property was clean and fresh. It is right next to another Hilton brand hotel Homewood Suites and whole property is semi gated and has plenty of free parking. Price of hotel breakfast is about twelve dollars but is well worth it. My children enjoyed heated, clean, spacious swimming pool. Location is what you might expect from a near airport hotel and the area reflects that. Which means nowhere scenic or serene. My family really had a good stay.

reviews.author: Yvonne Collins
reviews.content: We just returned from a week's stay at the Wyndham on W. 24th while getting our daughter setup at Parson's. The staff there was incredibly helpful and friendly (especially Aaron and Winnie). It is located between 5th and 6th Avenue and is incredibly convenient to a variety of great shops, stores and restaurants, including a Michelin one-starred place right next door. 24th is not a major cross street but we never had to wait more than 3 minutes for a cab plus you could walk to either 5th or 6th, in about 2 minutes time, if you wanted to catch a bus. We stayed on the 11th floor and did not hear any street noise - other guests, staying on lower floors, said the street noise was annoying - see if you can book a room higher up. Also, check with the front desk folks about getting vouchers for breakfast - the restaurant is a separate thing but they do a good job on omlettes and have a good variety of breakfast choices. We'll stay there again, gladly, when visiting Manhattan.

reviews.author: Juana Grant
reviews.content: The Wyndham is a very nice hotel with a very good sized shower and bathroom and the room was large by cpmparison to every hotel we have stayed in during prior trips to Chelsea where our son lives. Friendly staff, internet included and very nice location. We've decided this is our favorite and will e the place we will come back to many times. The price is very good as well for the square footage. There is a nice but tight fitness room with two tread mills and an eliptical in between that is open with your key card 24 hours a day. Dean from Myrtle Beach

reviews.author: Billy Haley
reviews.content: Nice hotel, great location and staff.... but - the room was tiny, cheap towels in the bathroom, noisy HVAC unit in the room kept us up all night. I know rooms in NYC are expensive, but for $400 a night was expecting something a lot better.

reviews.author: Richmond Yost
reviews.content: The Wyndham Hotel was amazing! A few friends and I made a trip to New York recently and stayed at this place for 3 nights. The service was spectacular. The front desk offered helpful advice on places to go and things to eat. The location was also very convenient because everything was within walking distance. Whenever you're in New York, definitely make it a point to stay here!

reviews.author: Cloyd Gusikowski
reviews.content: Perfect location and wonderful staff all wrapped up in great price

reviews.author: Sylvan Kub
reviews.content: This was my second stay here and it was just as good as the first. Easy to book, easy to check out. SUPER friendly front desk staff, especially Winnie. Rooms are clean and set up nicely. I love the quiet location and the cozy lobby. As long as the price continues to work with my budget, I'll be back!

title: Benllech

description: Panoramic views over the Menai Straits, Château Rhianfa is set in a Grade II listed Victorian villa.
name: Chateau Rhianfa

reviews.author: Deshaun Jast
reviews.content: Stayed at the Wyndham for a one night business trip. The staff was very friendly and helpful upon check-in. The rooms are very small (typical for NYC) but they make excellent use of space and it was very comfortable for the business traveler. Neat and clean with nice toiletries in the bathroom, a coffee maker and hotel safe. The breakfast in the associated restaurant next door was very nice and the location was convenient to the subway.

reviews.author: Jairo Bartoletti
reviews.content: I stayed here due to the price and walking distance to my meeting. Typical NYC Tiny Rooms. My room had a view of the ally, so it was quiet. For an overnight or even a couple of nights it would be ok. The restaurant next to the lobby had good appetizers

reviews.author: Dion Koch
reviews.content: We stayed here for 4 nights & were very happy. The rooms were spotless (& NO sign of bedbugs!) & the area convenient for exploring the city. The staff were without exception smiling, polite & helpful; we would single out for special mention Angie the concierge who was always happy to answer questions & do all she could for us, including checking in online for our journey home. A great place to stay in NYC.

title: Menai Bridge

description: Breathtaking views over Menai Strait. Strictly non smoking site. No pets.
name: Coed y Berclas Holiday Cottage & Luxury Apartment

reviews.author: Xander Schimmel
reviews.content: Stayed at the Wyndham Garden Hotel in Chelsea/Flatiron District for the fifth or sixth time in the past two years. Had three rooms books for four nights each. All three rooms were very clean. Located us all on the same floor with an early check-in. Had two separate occassions to call the front desk on different nights to ask for help quieting some neighbors on the floor....seemed liked high school field trip participants who were exhuberant to be in NYC and away from their parents for the first time. Problems were resolved within five minutes each time. Tried San Rocco (restaurant adjacent to hotel) for drinks/snacks. Nice and reasonably priced for the city. Aside from a great location and rate, the staff at Wyndham Chelsea are always very professional, polite, and friendly.

title: Menai Bridge

description: Winner, Best Place to Stay (Self Catering) Wales National Tourism Awards 2013. Five beautifully restored cottages set in secluded Hidden Gardens. Walled Garden; woodlands; waterfalls. Self catering cottages with luxury accommodation. Choice of cottages from cosy Brewhouse sleeping 2 to grand Coach House (sleeps 12/13) with semi professional kitchen.
name: Plas Cadnant Hidden Gardens and Cottages

reviews.author: Isobel Kemmer
reviews.content: We stayed at this hotel for 2 nights. Prior to arriving I had sent an email to the Assistant Gen. Manager, who had responded to some other posts on this site. I told him that the trip was for my wifes birthday and asked if the hotel offered anything that I could purchase to make the stay more special. He was out of the office for the week so my email was forwarded to the Gen. Manager who upgraded our room to a suite with a balcony. While the room was a little small it was no smaller than any other rooms that we have stayed at in New York City. Upon check in the desk clerk mentioned my wifes birthday and provided us with vouchers for breakfast in the morning. We then went to a great local restaurant that was recommended to us by the Gen. Mgr. and when we returned to the room there was a nice desert with a birthday card from the staff and a balloon in the room. Very nice touch. Another post on this site mentioned noise being a problem but we didn't find that to be the case at all, we had a great nights sleep on both nights. We did stop in the restaurant that is attached to the hotel (Rocco's) for desert on the other night. I'm not sure if this is part of the hotel itself or just shares the same space but we weren't impressed with the restaurant. We were seated at the table for at least a 1/2 hour before our order was taken. We would absolutely stay at this hotel again and have already recommended it to friends. It was a short walk to Chelsea Market, and we also walked to Times Square which was a little far but definitely doable.

reviews.author: Tristian Kautzer
reviews.content: Stayed at Wyndham Garden Inn Chelsea seven nights, from December 23 to December 30, 2009. Most all hotels in Manhattan considered the last few nights of our stay as part of the high priced New Years Eve week. We were getting decent rates for the first 3 or 4 nights, but the last few nights tripled! We ended up calling hotels directly to ask for a lower price for those nights since we would be staying so long. Wyndham Garden Inn Chelsea was the only hotel that would adjust their prices. So we paid $149 for the first six nights and $229 for the last night, before taxes of about $20 a night. We paid about $40 for a taxi from LGA. The hotel is on 24th Street halfway between 5th and 6th Streets (a little closer to 6th), just one block over from the major cross-street in Chelsea, 23rd Street. There are subway stations all along 23rd street. The closest to the hotel is the FV station at 6th Avenue, but the 1, RW, 6 and CE stations arenâ€™t far within Â¼ mile. The location of the hotel is its best feature. There is quick access to all parts of the city. But Chelsea/Flat Iron is full of interesting shops and incredible restaurants. We walked to all of these restaurantsâ€¦ we had breakfast at Murrayâ€™s Bagel (on 8th Avenue south of 23rd Street), had the best BBQ brisket ever at RUB (on 23rd Street between 7th and 8th Avenue), had an excellent European brunch at Markt, enjoyed incredible soup at Pipaâ€™s inside the ABC Carpet Shop on Broadway, indulged in old fashioned diner-style meals at the Lyric Diner on 3rd Avenue, and even sipped shakes at Burger Shack in the Madison Square Park. The area has really fun for people watching. The hotel is obviously newly re-constructed. All the materials and fixtures are new. There is essentially no lobby. The doors open right at the front desk. There is a sofa and a couple ottomans but itâ€™s not a spot you would spend time. A ticket desk/concierge is squeezed into a corner. The restaurant is supposed to be a part of the hotel, but it didnâ€™t really seem that way. We never ate there. Room 903 is steps from the elevator and faces the front of the building. The small room was adequate for two people who travel well together but donâ€™t think of sharing a room with someone who getâ€™s on your nerves. It has a desk and chair, big flat screen TV on the wall, arm chair, two nightstands, a luggage rack and a closet equipped with an iron/board. There is no dresser. The king sized bed has a good quality mattress topped with a comfy feather bed. The sheets are good quality (probably 350-threadcount). The duvet and comforter are nice and cozy. The pillows are decent foam. The heating system was a little quirky; it made a lot of noise whenever it kicked on. But we got used to it and slept through the repeated ruckus. The bathroom is well equipped with a good-sized shower, decent towels, enough counter space and True Blue Spa soap, shampoo, conditioner and lotion. The water pressure and temperature were good. Except one morning there was no hot water. By the time we went down to the lobby, the repair truck was already parked in front of the hotel and they were repairing the frozen boiler. We had plenty of hot water when we returned that afternoon. Our room was cleaned completely and promptly when weâ€™d leave in the morning. Although no one knocked when we had the do not disturb sign on the door, the cleaning crew was very noisy. Two of them even got into a screaming match about who wasnâ€™t working fast enough! But everyone on the staff was very friendly to the guests. The hotel worked for us because we donâ€™t need a fancy lobby, an onsite restaurant or other services. It was a good value for the price compared to other hotels in Manhattan. It is in an area that we like and has good access to public transportation. If you travel like we do, youâ€™ll like this hotel.

reviews.author: Magali Bruen
reviews.content: I would highly recommend this Hotel is you are interested in Location and Good Value for your Money. The Location for this Hotel is Great -Very close to Union Square, the Flatiron Building, Empire State Building, Penn Station, Madison Square Garden, Chelsea and other landmarks. All within easy walking distance. It is also very convenient to many subway lines. The building is brand new and it is on a quiet street just one block beyond 23rd St. The building was nice, the room was good - not huge but it met our needs for a few days stay. We Got a Great Room Rate which was good for a Stay in New York. Most New York Hotels are too expensive and not worth the price, but this one was Great. For the same price, I would happily stay at this hotel again. The location, cleanliness, and price cant be beat. I am very glad that we stayed here as opposed to somewhere else. It met our Needs Very Well. The Staff was very friendly and helpful. We arrived later than usual and they checked us in quickly and had our room ready. They even offered us a discount rate for an extra nite or two for the room because we may have had to stay longer due to a heavy snowstorm that was about to hit the New York Metro area that day but we were able to leave before it arrived. That was really nice to offer that to us. Quality: I was impressed when we first entered the room. The hallway was warm, but the room was perfectly heated and comfortable as it was brutally cold outside. The room was very clean and cozy. Granted, it was a small but you have to expect that in Manhattan. We had no problems with it. I would highly recommend this hotel for location, value and its cool boutique style. Well worth it. Enjoy.

reviews.author: Sidney Schaefer
reviews.content: We stayed at the Wyndham Garden Chelsea for 5 days in May and thought the location was great. Very close to the subway line, Flatiron building and Madison Square Park. The room we stayed in was small but we only used it to sleep! So much to do in NY! A few comments for management would be: The bathroom could have been a bit cleaner, not sure the floor was cleaned before we checked in. When we asked the front desk about help with getting tickets to a Broadway show we were just told to "check the internet" A little more help, tips or ideas would have been nice. Lastly, a street/subway map of Manhattan would have been great. Most hotels give these out but the front desk only seemed to have a map of the Flatiron district. Over all a great stay here and would definitely recommend it to others as well as stay here again ourselves.

title: Menai Bridge

address: 2 Plas Hafod Lon, Lon Ganol, Llandegfan, Ynys Mon, LL595UD
description: Self-contained first-floor two bedroom apartment with its own private entrance. The apartment is situated in the village of Llandegfan between the town of Menai Bridge (1.5 miles) and the seaside town of Beaumaris (2 miles). The apartment occupies the top floor of a large private manor house, overlooking the Menai Strait towards the university town of Bangor and the Snowdonia Mountains beyond. The property is located in a private spot down a private lane and has of parking space if you need somewhere secure to park your trailer, boat, canoes, etc.
name: Hafod Lon Holiday Apartment

reviews.author: Miss Nathanael Morissette
reviews.content: i stayed in the hotel from Friday to monday. we arrive very late friday night to find the hotel in an area surrounded by outdoor clubs, fast food outlets and young drunk kids, mostly of the Punk variety. we did not feel safe on the train platform or walking the 200 meters to the hotel. once at the hotel it was beauitful, you cannot hear the techno music from the clubs or the sounds from the roads outside. the room was a good size, the staff were excelent, the breakfast will keep you full well into the day. during the day the surrounding area looked fine. mainly young students living and working in the area. there was some broken glass on the gound from the nights before. i would not recomend this hotel if you have young children as the drinking culture in this area is a big turnoff good hotel if your looking for cheap, comfortable hotel close to the train lines.

reviews.author: Kadin Willms
reviews.content: Travelled in a group of 7, and stayed 4 days in Miami prior to our cruise. At first impression, I am not sure if they are going for the nostalgic dark decor, but the hotel had a sort of antique features and dark wood, with low lighting. We had to find someone to take our bags to our room as there was no doorman when we arrived and only one conceirge with the trolley full of luggages, so we had to go up the elevator to the main lobby and wait for the concierges there. From previous tips from this website I requested a high level bay view which the three of us received. We were very happy and amazed from the views. The rooms were of substantial size and had all the amenities except for a minibar, although there is a ice and drinks vending machine a few doors away. However, my Uncle was unfortunate to get locked in the bathroom and had his wife call maintenance to unscrew the door to let him out. They fortunately were able to change rooms later that day. The rest of the group had no problems with the room. We had dinner on our first night and was throughly entertained by our Egyptian waitor (cannot remember his name) but we really enjoyed the evening. Breakfast was ok, however the variety was limited but I did expect it after reading the previous reviews, so I was not surprised. As a vegetarian, I did fill up on fruits and bread, however the savoury foods only limited me to scrambled eggs and oatmeal. Would have liked beans or hash browns instead of pancakce rolled up with creamy cheese! The staff were helpful and the internet service was good as it was free if you are a guest. The gift shop was also good as well as the bar in the main lobby, however it did take long to get our order as there was only 1 bar man serving...he gave us complimentary drinks for waiting so long. The surroundings were ok, no problems there as we mostly took taxi around town, we did try the mono rail which was exciting but a bit scary at the freedom tower stop, a guy was screaming which led me to believe he was mentally insane, there are no barriers from the platform so be careful as it does get windy up there. We went on the city tour and the Orlando day tour as recommended by Danilo the concierge. We enjoyed the boat city tour, however I would not recommend the Orlando trip as it was a nightmare. The main journey took 3 hours (expected) however if you are going to the magic kingdom, you have to transfer to a mini van, which the driver then took us into the car park of a supermarket area as he had to wait for a guy who was buying the entrance tickets, we had to wait in the car park for 10 minutes, at this time after travellig 3+ hours we were furious as we were told we would get at the park around 10am instead we arrived at 11am, thus cutting short our enjoyment at the park. We vented our frustration but the driver said to complain to the company and muttered in Spanish. We tried to enjoy the rest of the day. The tickets should've been purchased prior to the day. The following days were uneventful and we went on our cruise. Lambert the doorman was thoroughly considerate.

reviews.author: Moriah Rippin
reviews.content: I stayed here for one night due some mix-up with accommodations in Ft. Lauderdale but that was fine as my cruise was departing from the Port of Miami anyway. Location-- very close to the free people mover and major bus connector to get all over Miami or South Beach. A Burger King was directly across the street for a quick coffee or salad but that was it for restaurants. Room-- I did like the floor to ceiling windows and it was clean but, in all honesty the room was no more different than any hotel that I stayed in with a lower star rating. The bathroom light is on a timer so that was good for energy conservation. Bed was comfortable and TV worked fine. Walls looked a bit old though so I am thinking that perhaps this hotel could be showing its age somewhat. Staff-- were nice, friendly and always had a smile. Negative-- the wireless internet. I decided to purchase it and it was horrible. Kept crashing and when it did open it was slower than dial-up I had years ago. Was good for one night but I would not do longer.

reviews.author: Bette Bernier
reviews.content: First time staying at the Miami Hilton Downtown. I was in town for a short business trip and the location was perfect, so decided to give it a try. It's very much a Hilton, with all the standard amenities and qualities one expects to find at a Hilton hotel. That also means you know you're in a hotel and not at home :-) The room is nicely furnished and clean, and surprisingly quiet in spite of being located right next door to the ice and vending machine. TV selection was pretty basic, but I'm not here to watch the tube so no biggie. Lots of elevators, so I didn't ever have to wait long. Bed was comfy, though the pillows were a bit thin for my liking. It would be nice if the hotel offered a selection of pillows, as some other chains do. Bath was clean and everything worked flawlessly. The drain in the shower was a bit slow (probably clogged with hair) but a quick call to maintenance fixed that. I did eat in the hotel restaurant one night and it was good. Had the mahi-mahi, with rice. Location is good, with the Sea Isle marina a short walk across the street. I took a walk one night after dinner and enjoyed the view. I'd stay here again.

reviews.author: Stone Cummerata
reviews.content: We stayed here for 2 nights in Nov. 2011 for a romantic getaway. Our view from the room was not that great but the view from the terrace was. The staff was very friendly and I tipped generously. The room itself was massive and clean. This is 1 of the best 3 hotel rooms I have ver stayed in and I've been to a lot. The staff was also very courteous and evyeryone was willing to go the extra mile. I was not used to not having free wifi, since its availabele for gold hilton honours members, which we werent at the time. However the odd thing is the wifi fee the charge you is per device not for the room. This means if your not a Gold HIlton Honors member, and have 3 devices you want to connect to wifi in your room, Hilton expects you to pay 3 times. This seems odd consdering that number of devices that have a mobile hotspot feature. Another way around this is just use a device or phone that has a mobile hotspot and connect all your devices thru that. Nedless to say we found out the hard way and were charged twice but the front desk attendant made it right by covering one of our charges. Our only regret was that we wish woul dcould stay longer. We will be staying here next time we visit to see the Heat play.

reviews.author: Myrl Stehr
reviews.content: Stayed here when we missed out flight to San Juan. Arrived late, tired and hungry. Avi, manager of the restaurant took great care of us, helping get us fed after the kitchen was about to close. Went out of his way to help. Nice front desk personnel as well. So far a great experience.

reviews.author: Herman Bins IV
reviews.content: We stayed at the Hilton for 2 nights after getting of a cruise. The hotel itself was pretty good. The staff were friendly and helpful, and the lobby and bars downstairs were very relaxing and we did spend alot of time there. The room was spacious, but the walls very thin. We were near the lifts and they were noisy all night. The airconditioning in the room was rather loud as well. But the room was clean and bright. Except for the location, we would stay there again. When we travel, we like to walk around the area/city and enjoy the sights. DO NOT walk too far from this Hotel. We should have stayed at South Beach area instead. Downtown did not feel safe at all, and there were alot of unsavoury looks as we did walk 4 blocks from the Hotel. We soon turned around, went back and called a taxi to take us where we wanted to go. The Hotel is good - the location is not.

reviews.author: Margret White Sr.
reviews.content: We spent one night prior to cruising and were not disappointed. Our room on the 14th floor had a great view of downtown, the port, and the waterfront. The room was clean, spacious, and well appointed. The front desk staff was courteous and efficient during our check-in. The location is very convenient, only a short 1 1/2 miles from the cruise terminal. It also is only a block away from the Omni station, which provides access to the free Metro Mover, as well as numerous buslines (including multiple lines serving South Beach / Miami Beach for $2 per ride). We ate a late dinner at the hotel bar and were pleasantly surprised at the food selection, quality, and moderate prices. However, service was a bit slow, even though it wasn't very busy. The bar, as well as other public areas were nicely decorated and clean.

title: Menai Bridge

description: Fantastic little B&B with 3 rooms, all en-suite. Very comfortable beds, friendly hosts, delicious breakfasts. Ideally placed for waterfalls and mountains, Walkers and cyclists welcome.
directions: From Penderyn, follow Cwm Cadlan road from Lamb Hotel for 1.5 miles, you'll see sign and yellow grit bin at the gate on your left.
name: Beili Helyg Guest House

reviews.author: Oda Gerlach
reviews.content: Staying at any Ritz is always a nice experience and the facilities at the Ritz Carlton Kapalua were beautiful. The pool was beautiful and our view from the balcony was great. We actually sat on our balcony one afternoon and watched whales for hours. How many places can you do that? However, when we arrived after about 12 hours in the air and another hour or so in pouring rain driving from the airport, we were informed that our "Club Level" lounge had just closed. Even though we paid full price for the Club Level that night, they did not even give us a free drink. A little disappointed there, but everything else was pretty nice.

title: Brecon Beacons National Park

description: Hiking trails, hot springs, firewood, toilets. No potable water available.
name: Buckeye Campground

reviews.author: Elyssa Gutkowski
reviews.content: We stayed at the Whaler for the 2nd half of our honeymoon from December 16-22nd. We were in Tower 2, and booked through AAA/Pleasant Holidays. The first room they had us in was fairly outdated so we simply asked if they had any more updated rooms and they showed us a room on the 8th floor. It was a studio, completely re-done with a King-size Murphy bed in the wall, sofa, chair, and all the comforts of home. We had plenty of space for the 2 of us, they did offer us an upgrade to a 1 bed/bath for an extra 100/day, but seeing that is more of a hike than their original ticket price, we decided the studio was the perfect fit. We overlooked Whaler's village, but also had a view of the ocean and mountains and the perfect sunsets (the same view all units have). We stopped at k-mart by the airport and got breakfast and lunch food and went out for dinner each night. The beach area right out in front of the Whaler was great as well, it never seemed as crowded as the areas in front of the large resorts. It was a honeymoon to remember and we would definitely stay at the Whaler again.

reviews.author: Mr. Lauriane Parker
reviews.content: The Westin Resort and Spa at Lahaina is a beautiful property. While it could use a little updating in places, it was in very good shape overall. The landscaping is excellent, and the exterior design is very nice. Our main concern was the sheer number of people who were using the property -- beach chairs sold out very quickly, and conveniently-located chairs on the pool deck could be hard to find. The resort restaurants serve very good food, and the staff is courteous and diligent.

reviews.author: Ara Hermann
reviews.content: We just got back from getting married at the westin maui, sarah snider was a huge help in making this happen. they gave us a nice room for the wedding night and when we showed up there was rose pedals all over the room and a bottle of wine for us to enjoy. Everyone at the front desk was helpful and nice to deal with. The grounds for this resort were so nice we enjoyed every minute. You can see whales off in the distance right from the beach, the restaurants were amazing, i had one of the best steaks in my life at tropica. Having whalers village right next door for shpping and cheaper food was great as well. my only complaint was having to leave!!! cant wait to come back to maui it was truly paradise on earth.

reviews.author: Lolita Kshlerin
reviews.content: The down side was that we only booked for one week. We rented a car, but didn't use it very much so there is so much within walking distance. Anyway, a wonderful resort with a wonderful staff. I don't understand the people on here that complain about the cost of things. You're in a waterfront resort in Maui. If you want to spend less, move inland or stay home. We're booking for two weeks next year. We won't bother with a rental car for the first week, we will make use of the car in week two. By the way, we highly recommend the Blue Hawaiian Helicopter tours, it is worth every penny. Anyway, enjoy. We certainly did, and will again. :-)

reviews.author: Mia Cremin
reviews.content: What an amazing place to stay right on the ocean with beautiful amenities and plenty of opportunity to explore this beautiful get away. The lodging itself was gorgeous enough not to speak of the setting. Very comfortable room that had a jacuzzi in the bath that could open up to the room to sit and look out the window to the ocean. Very nice lanai to sit and soak in the atmosphere as well. We only ate at one spot and spent most of our time exploring Lahaina for eating establishments. The resort is close enough to take day trips away and see the sites of Maui. We enjoyed both the beach and the pool. The staff there was very accomodating. We were celebrating a birthday and I wanted to have fresh flowers in the room and they arranged that very nicely for me and included an "unasked" for small birthday cake for my traveling companion. They went all out to make it a wonderful stay, my only regret is that we only spent 3 days there and then were off to Oahu. In retrospect I wish our week would have been on Maui. It is a much more of a relaxing and less hurried atmosphere than we found on Oahu. It depends on what you are looking for. As for the Westin, do stay!

reviews.author: Hazle Miller II
reviews.content: We booked our trip 11 months in advance and traveled with family with a total of 9 people total, 3 of them kids. I sent the guest manager, Sean an email a month prior to our trip to let him know this was our first trip with a Starwood Property and that we were very excited to celebrate my birthday and our anniversary during this trip. Upon arrival, we were greeted by several valet attendants who all welcomed us with huge smiles and helped us with the kids and our bags. At check in, I was excited to learn we had been upgraded to an Ocean View room by Sean. Will brought our bags up to our room and gave us a quick yet detailed run down of the property and what to do and how to get there. Our room was fantastic! Great view of the ocean, the pools and the whales every morning! We went out for dinner shortly after for less than two hours and returned to find a delicious cake and a bottle of champagne waiting for us!!! Thanks Westin! That was the best birthday I had ever had, HANDS DOWN! And that was just the first night. We enjoyed some relaxation time in the pools with the kids the first night after a long day of flying.
